rows.spanish_base_english: So on the next day, Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the audience hall with the military tribunes and the prominent men of the city, and at Festus's command Paul was brought in.

rows.spanish: Y Festo dijo: «Rey Agripa y todos los hombres presentes con nosotros: ustedes ven a este hombre, acerca de quien todo el cuerpo de los judíos me presentó una petición, tanto en Jerusalén como aquí, gritando que ya no debía vivir».
rows.current_english_pob: And Festus says, “King Agrippa, and all the men present with us, you see this man, about whom the whole body of the Jews petitioned me, both in Jerusalem and here, shouting that he ought no longer to live.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Festus says, “King Agrippa, and all the men present with us, you see this man, about whom the whole multitude of the Jews appealed to me, both in Jerusalem and here, crying out that he ought no longer to live.”

rows.spanish: Pues bien, todos los judíos conocen mi modo de vida desde mi juventud, que desde el principio he pasado entre mi propio pueblo y en Jerusalén,
rows.current_english_pob: So then, all the Jews know my manner of life from my youth, which from the beginning took place among my own nation and also in Jerusalem,
rows.spanish_base_english: So then, all the Jews know my manner of life from my youth, which from the beginning was spent among my own nation and in Jerusalem,

rows.spanish: ¿Por qué se considera increíble entre ustedes si Dios resucita a los muertos?
rows.current_english_pob: Why is it judged unbelievable by you if God raises the dead?
rows.spanish_base_english: Why is it judged unbelievable among you if God raises the dead?

rows.spanish: Rey Agripa, ¿les crees a los profetas? Sé que sí les crees.
rows.current_english_pob: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you do believe.
rows.spanish_base_english: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.

rows.spanish: Cuando se decidió que navegáramos hacia Italia, entregaron a Pablo y a algunos otros prisioneros a un centurión llamado Julio, de la cohorte augusta.
rows.current_english_pob: When it was decided that we should sail for Italy, they handed over both Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan Cohort.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when it was decided that we should sail for Italy, they handed over both Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan Cohort.

rows.spanish: Así que nos embarcamos en un barco de Adramitio, que estaba por navegar hacia los lugares de la costa de Asia, y zarpamos, estando con nosotros Aristarco, macedonio de Tesalónica.
rows.current_english_pob: So we boarded an Adramyttian ship that was about to sail to the places along Asia, and put out to sea, with Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, being with us.
rows.spanish_base_english: So we boarded an Adramyttian ship that was about to sail to the places along the coast of Asia, and put out to sea, with Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, being with us.

rows.spanish: Pero el centurión prestaba más atención al piloto y al propietario del barco que a lo que Pablo decía.
rows.current_english_pob: But the centurion paid more attention to the pilot and the shipowner than to what was being said by Paul.
rows.spanish_base_english: But the centurion was persuaded more by the pilot and the shipowner than by what was said by Paul.

rows.spanish: Después de haber pasado mucho tiempo sin comer, Pablo se puso en pie en medio de ellos y dijo: «Hombres, debieron haberme escuchado y no zarpar de Creta, y así habrían evitado este daño y esta pérdida».
rows.current_english_pob: Since they had gone a long time without food, then Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have listened to me and not set sail from Crete, and so have avoided this damage and loss.”
rows.spanish_base_english: After they had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have listened to me and not set sail from Crete, and so have avoided this damage and loss.”

rows.spanish: diciendo: «No temas, Pablo. Es necesario que comparezcas ante César, y he aquí que Dios te ha concedido a todos los que navegan contigo.»
rows.current_english_pob: saying, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar, and look, God has granted to you all those sailing with you.’
rows.spanish_base_english: saying, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar, and behold, God has granted to you all those sailing with you.’

rows.spanish: Hasta que iba a amanecer, Pablo seguía instando a todos a tomar alimento, diciendo: «Hoy es el día catorce que han continuado esperando sin comer, sin haber tomado nada».
rows.current_english_pob: Until the day was about to dawn, Paul kept urging them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you have continued in suspense without eating, having taken nothing.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Until the day was about to dawn, Paul kept urging them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you have continued waiting without food, having taken nothing.”

rows.spanish: Y había en total 276 personas en la nave.
rows.current_english_pob: There were 276 persons in the ship in all.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now there were 276 persons in the ship in all.

rows.spanish: Cuando amaneció, no reconocieron la tierra, pero notaron una cierta bahía con una playa, en la cual planeaban, si podían, varar el barco.
rows.current_english_pob: When day came, they did not recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, into which they planned, if they could, to run the ship ashore.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when day came, they did not recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, into which they planned, if they could, to run the ship ashore.

rows.spanish: El plan de los soldados era matar a los prisioneros para que ninguno escapara nadando.
rows.current_english_pob: The soldiers’ plan was to kill the prisoners, so that no one might swim away and escape.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the soldiers’ plan was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim away and escape.

rows.spanish: Y en los alrededores de aquel lugar había propiedades del hombre principal de la isla, llamado Publio, quien nos recibió y nos hospedó cortesmente durante tres días.
rows.current_english_pob: In the area around that place there were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who welcomed us and hosted us courteously for three days.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now in the area around that place there were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who welcomed us and hosted us courteously for three days.

rows.spanish: Entonces sucedió que el padre de Publio estaba enfermo en cama, con fiebres y disentería. Pablo entró a verlo, y después de orar y poner las manos sobre él, lo sanó.
rows.current_english_pob: It happened that the father of Publius was lying sick with fevers and dysentery. Paul went in to him, and after praying and laying his hands on him, healed him.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now it happened that the father of Publius was lying sick with fevers and dysentery. Paul went in to him, and after praying and laying his hands on him, healed him.

rows.spanish: Allí encontramos hermanos y se nos invitó a quedarnos con ellos siete días. Y así llegamos a Roma.
rows.current_english_pob: There we found brothers, and we were invited to stay with them seven days. And so we came to Rome.
rows.spanish_base_english: There we found brothers and were invited to stay with them seven days. And so we came to Rome.

rows.spanish: Sucedió que, después de tres días, reunió a los principales de los judíos. Y cuando se reunieron, les dijo: «Yo, hermanos, aunque no había hecho nada contra el pueblo ni contra las costumbres de nuestros padres, fui entregado como prisionero de Jerusalén a manos de los Romanos».
rows.current_english_pob: It happened that after three days he called together the leading men of the Jews. And when they had come together, he said to them, “I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people or the customs of our fathers, was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Now it happened that after three days he called together the leading men of the Jews. And when they had come together, he said to them, “I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people or the customs of our fathers, was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.”

rows.spanish: Y como no estaban de acuerdo entre sí, se retiraban, después de que Pablo dijera una palabra final: «El Espíritu Santo habló acertadamente por medio del profeta Isaías a sus padres».
rows.current_english_pob: And since they were disagreeing with one another, they were leaving after Paul had said one final word: “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers
rows.spanish_base_english: And disagreeing among themselves, they were departing after Paul had spoken one final word: “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers

rows.spanish: Porque el corazón de este pueblo se ha vuelto insensible, y con los oídos apenas oyen, y han cerrado sus ojos; no sea que vean con los ojos, oigan con los oídos, entiendan con el corazón y se vuelvan, y yo los sanaría.
rows.current_english_pob: For the heart of this people has become dull, and with their ears they heard heavily, and they closed their eyes; otherwise they might see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn back, and I would heal them.
rows.spanish_base_english: For the heart of this people has become dull, and with their ears they scarcely hear, and they have closed their eyes; otherwise they might see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn back, and I would heal them.

rows.spanish: proclamando el reino de Dios y enseñando lo referente al Señor Jesús Mesías con toda valentía, sin estorbo.
rows.current_english_pob: proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus the Messiah with all boldness, unhindered.
rows.spanish_base_english: proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Messiah with all boldness, unhindered.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, estos son los nombres de los hijos de Israel que vinieron a Egipto con Jacob, cada uno con los de su casa.
rows.current_english_pob: These are the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob, each man with his household.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob, each man with his household.

rows.spanish: Dan, Neftalí, Gad y Aser.
rows.current_english_pob: Dan, and Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
rows.spanish_base_english: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

rows.spanish: Se levantó sobre Egipto un nuevo rey que no conocía a José.
rows.current_english_pob: A new king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now a new king arose over Egypt, who did not know Yosef.

rows.spanish: Así que pusieron capataces sobre ellos para afligirlos con sus cargas, y construyeron ciudades de depósito para Faraón: Pitom y Raméses.
rows.current_english_pob: So they set taskmasters over him to afflict him with their burdens, and he built storage cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Rameses.
rows.spanish_base_english: So they set taskmasters over them to afflict them with their burdens, and they built storage cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Rameses.

rows.spanish: Y les amargaron la vida con trabajo duro en mortero y ladrillos, y en toda clase de trabajo del campo: todo el trabajo que les impusieron con dureza.
rows.current_english_pob: And they made their lives bitter with hard labor in mortar and bricks and in every kind of field work—all their labor that they imposed on them with harshness.
rows.spanish_base_english: And they made their lives bitter with hard labor in mortar and brick and in every kind of field work—all their labor that they imposed on them with harshness.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, un hombre de la casa de Leví fue y tomó por esposa a una hija de Leví.
rows.current_english_pob: A man from the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi as his wife.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now a man from the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi as his wife.

rows.spanish: La abrió y lo vio, al niño, y he aquí, un niño estaba llorando. Tuvo compasión de él y dijo: «Este es uno de los hijos de los hebreos».
rows.current_english_pob: She opened it and saw him, the child, and behold, a boy was crying. She had compassion on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrews’ children.”
rows.spanish_base_english: She opened it and saw him, the child, and behold, a boy was crying. She had compassion on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrews’ children.”

rows.spanish: Aconteció en aquellos días, cuando Moisés ya había crecido, que salió a ver a sus hermanos y vio sus cargas. Y vio a un hombre egipcio que golpeaba a un hombre hebreo, uno de sus hermanos.
rows.current_english_pob: It happened in those days, when Moses had grown up, that he went out to his brothers and saw their burdens. And he saw an Egyptian man striking a Hebrew man, one of his brothers.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now it happened in those days, when Moses had grown up, that he went out to his brothers and saw their burdens. And he saw an Egyptian man striking a Hebrew man, one of his brothers.

rows.spanish: Salió al día siguiente, y he aquí, dos hombres hebreos estaban peleando. Entonces dijo al malvado: «¿Por qué golpeas a tu compañero?»
rows.current_english_pob: He went out the next day, and behold, two Hebrew men were fighting. And he said to the wicked one, “Why are you striking your companion?”
rows.spanish_base_english: He went out the next day, and behold, two Hebrew men were fighting. And he said to the wicked one, “Why are you striking your companion?”

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, el sacerdote de Madián tenía siete hijas, y ellas vinieron, sacaron agua y llenaron los abrevaderos para dar de beber al rebaño de su padre.
rows.current_english_pob: The priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came and drew water and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came and drew water and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.

rows.spanish: Y él dijo a sus hijas: «¿Dónde está él, pues? ¿Por qué dejaron al hombre? Llámenlo, para que coma pan».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said to his daughters, “Then where is he? Why is it that you left the man? Call him, so that he may eat bread.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said to his daughters, “Where is he then? Why is this, that you left the man? Call him, so that he may eat bread.”

rows.spanish: Y aconteció en aquellos muchos días que murió el rey de Egipto, y los hijos de Israel gimieron a causa del trabajo y clamaron, y su clamor subió a Dios a causa del trabajo.
rows.current_english_pob: It happened in those many days that the king of Egypt died, and the sons of Israel groaned because of the slavery and cried out, and their cry for help went up to God because of the slavery.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now it happened in those many days that the king of Egypt died, and the sons of Israel groaned because of the labor and cried out, and their cry for help went up to God because of the labor.

rows.spanish: Dios vio a los hijos de Israel, y Dios supo.
rows.current_english_pob: God saw the sons of Israel, and God knew.
rows.spanish_base_english: God saw the sons of Israel, and God took notice.

rows.spanish: Ahora Moisés estaba pastoreando el rebaño de Jetro, su suegro, sacerdote de Madián. Llevó el rebaño más allá del desierto y llegó al monte de Dios, Horeb.
rows.current_english_pob: Moses was shepherding the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian. He led the flock beyond the wilderness and came to the mountain of God, Horeb.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Moses was shepherding the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian. He led the flock beyond the wilderness and came to the mountain of God, Horeb.

rows.spanish: Entonces se le apareció el ángel de Yahvé en una llama de fuego, de en medio de la zarza. Miró, y he aquí que la zarza ardía con fuego, pero la zarza no era consumida.
rows.current_english_pob: Then the angel of Yahweh appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of the bush. He looked, and behold, the bush was burning with fire, but the bush was not consumed.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then the angel of Yahweh appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of the bush. He looked, and behold, the bush was burning with fire, but the bush was not consumed.

rows.spanish: Cuando Yahvé vio que se había apartado para mirar, Dios lo llamó de en medio de la zarza y dijo: «¡Moisés, Moisés!». Y él dijo: «Heme aquí».
rows.current_english_pob: When Yahweh saw that he had turned aside to look, God called to him from the midst of the bush and said, “Moses, Moses!” And he said, “Here I am.”
rows.spanish_base_english: When Yahweh saw that he had turned aside to look, God called to him from the midst of the bush and said, “Moses, Moses!” And he said, “Here I am.”

rows.spanish: Y ahora, he aquí, el clamor de los hijos de Israel ha llegado a mí, y también he visto la opresión con que los egipcios los oprimen.
rows.current_english_pob: And now, behold, the cry of the sons of Israel has come to me, and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them.
rows.spanish_base_english: And now, behold, the cry of the sons of Israel has come to me, and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them.

rows.spanish: Entonces Moisés dijo a Dios: «He aquí, cuando yo venga a los hijos de Israel y les diga: “El Dios de sus padres me ha enviado a ustedes”, y ellos me digan: “¿Qué nombre tiene?”, ¿qué les diré?»
rows.current_english_pob: Then Moses said to God, “Look, when I come to the sons of Israel and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you,’ and they say to me, ‘What is his name?’ what shall I say to them?”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Moses said to God, “Behold, when I come to the sons of Israel and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you,’ and they say to me, ‘What is his name?’ what shall I say to them?”

rows.spanish: Y Dios dijo a Moisés: «Yo Soy el que Soy». Y dijo: «Así dirás a los hijos de Israel: “Yo Soy me ha enviado a ustedes”».
rows.current_english_pob: And God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.” And he said, “Thus you shall say to the sons of Israel: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
rows.spanish_base_english: And God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.” And he said, “Thus you shall say to the sons of Israel: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”

rows.spanish: Entonces Moisés respondió: «Pero he aquí, no me creerán, ni escucharán mi voz, porque dirán: “Yahvé no se te ha aparecido”».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Moses answered and said, “But behold, they will not believe me, and they will not listen to my voice, for they will say, ‘Yahweh has not appeared to you.’”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Moses answered and said, “But behold, they will not believe me, and they will not listen to my voice, for they will say, ‘Yahweh has not appeared to you.’”

rows.spanish: Y Yahvé le dijo: «¿Qué es eso en tu mano?» Y él dijo: «Una vara».
rows.current_english_pob: And Yahweh said to him, “What is that in your hand?” And he said, “A staff.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Yahweh said to him, “What is that in your hand?” And he said, “A staff.”

rows.spanish: Entonces Yahvé le dijo de nuevo: «Por favor, mete tu mano en tu seno». Él metió su mano en su seno, y al sacarla, he aquí que su mano estaba leprosa, como la nieve.
rows.current_english_pob: Then Yahweh said to him again, “Please put your hand into your bosom.” So he put his hand into his bosom, and when he brought it out, behold, his hand was leprous, like snow.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Yahweh said to him again, “Please put your hand into your bosom.” So he put his hand into his bosom, and when he brought it out, behold, his hand was leprous, like snow.

rows.spanish: Y dijo: «Vuelve a meter tu mano en tu seno». Él volvió a meter su mano en su seno, y al sacarla de su seno, he aquí, había vuelto como su carne.
rows.current_english_pob: And he said, “Put your hand back into your bosom.” So he put his hand back into his bosom, and when he brought it out from his bosom, behold, it had returned like his flesh.
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said, “Put your hand back into your bosom.” So he put his hand back into his bosom, and when he brought it out from his bosom, behold, it had returned like his flesh.

rows.spanish: Y Yahvé le dijo: «¿Quién puso boca al hombre? ¿O quién hace a uno mudo, sordo, con vista o ciego? ¿No soy yo, Yahvé?».
rows.current_english_pob: And the LORD said to him, “Who has put a mouth on man? Or who makes one mute, or deaf, or sighted, or blind? Is it not I, the LORD?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Yahweh said to him, “Who has put a mouth on man? Or who makes one mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Is it not I, Yahweh?”

rows.spanish: Entonces se encendió el enojo de Yahvé contra Moisés, y dijo: «¿No está tu hermano Aarón, el levita? Yo sé que él sí sabe hablar. Y además, mira, él sale a recibirte; cuando te vea, se alegrará en su corazón».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Yahweh’s anger burned against Moses, and he said, “Is there not Aaron your brother, the Levite? I know that he can speak well. And also, look, he is coming out to meet you; when he sees you, he will rejoice in his heart.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Yahweh’s anger burned against Moses, and he said, “Is there not Aaron your brother, the Levite? I know that he can indeed speak. And also, behold, he is coming out to meet you; when he sees you, he will rejoice in his heart.”

rows.spanish: Y te dije: «Deja ir a mi hijo, para que me sirva», pero te rehusaste a dejarlo ir. Mira, yo estoy por matar a tu hijo, tu primogénito».
rows.current_english_pob: And I said to you, ‘Send out my son so that he may serve me,’ but you refused to send him out. Look, I am about to kill your son, your firstborn.
rows.spanish_base_english: And I said to you, ‘Let my son go, so that he may serve me,’ but you refused to let him go. Behold, I am about to kill your son, your firstborn.’

rows.spanish: Y dijeron: «El Dios de los hebreos ha salido a nuestro encuentro. Por favor, déjanos ir un viaje de tres días al desierto, y ofrezcamos sacrificios a Yahvé nuestro Dios, no sea que él caiga sobre nosotros con peste o con espada».
rows.current_english_pob: And they said, “The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go a journey of three days into the wilderness, so that we may sacrifice to Yahweh our God, lest he strike us with plague or with the sword.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And they said, “The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go a journey of three days into the wilderness, and let us sacrifice to Yahweh our God, lest he fall upon us with plague or with the sword.”

rows.spanish: Y los capataces israelitas, a quienes los supervisores del faraón habían puesto sobre ellos, fueron golpeados y les preguntaron: «¿Por qué no han terminado su cuota de ladrillos como antes, ni ayer ni hoy?».
rows.current_english_pob: And the Israelite foremen, whom Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, saying, “Why have you not finished your quota of brickmaking as before, both yesterday and today?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And the Israelite foremen, whom Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, saying, “Why have you not completed your prescribed amount of bricks as before, both yesterday and today?”

rows.spanish: No se da paja a tus siervos, y nos dicen: «¡Hagan ladrillos!». Y he aquí, tus siervos son golpeados, pero la culpa es de tu propio pueblo.
rows.current_english_pob: No straw is given to your servants, yet they say to us, ‘Make bricks!’ And behold, your servants are being beaten, but the fault is with your own people.
rows.spanish_base_english: No straw is given to your servants, yet they say to us, ‘Make bricks!’ And behold, your servants are being beaten, but the fault is with your own people.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, vayan, trabajen; pero no se les dará paja; sin embargo, ustedes deben entregar la cantidad exigida de ladrillos.
rows.current_english_pob: So now, go, work; but straw will not be given to you, yet you must deliver the required number of bricks.
rows.spanish_base_english: So now, go, work; but straw will not be given to you, yet you must deliver the required number of bricks.

rows.spanish: Entonces Moisés volvió a Yahvé y dijo: «Señor, ¿por qué has causado daño a este pueblo? ¿Por qué, entonces, me enviaste?».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Moses returned to Yahweh and said, “Lord, why have you brought harm on this people? Why then did you send me?”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Moses returned to Yahweh and said, “Lord, why have you done evil to this people? Why then did you send me?”

rows.spanish: También establecí mi pacto con ellos para darles la tierra de Canaán, la tierra donde vivieron como extranjeros.
rows.current_english_pob: I also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land where they lived as sojourners.
rows.spanish_base_english: I also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojourning, where they sojourned.

rows.spanish: Pero Moisés habló delante de Yahvé, diciendo: «He aquí, los hijos de Israel no me han escuchado; entonces, ¿cómo me escuchará Faraón, siendo yo incircunciso de labios?».
rows.current_english_pob: But Moses spoke before Yahweh, saying, “Behold, the sons of Israel have not listened to me; so how will Pharaoh listen to me, since I am uncircumcised in lips?”
rows.spanish_base_english: But Moses spoke before Yahweh, saying, “Behold, the sons of Israel have not listened to me; so how will Pharaoh listen to me, since I am uncircumcised in lips?”

rows.spanish: Estos son los nombres de los hijos de Leví según sus linajes: Gersón, Cohat y Merari. Los años de la vida de Leví fueron ciento treinta y siete años.
rows.current_english_pob: These are the names of Levi’s sons according to their generations: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. And the years of Levi’s life were one hundred thirty-seven years.
rows.spanish_base_english: These are the names of Levi’s sons according to their generations: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. And the years of Levi’s life were one hundred and thirty-seven years.

rows.spanish: Y sucedió el día que Yahvé habló a Moisés en la tierra de Egipto—
rows.current_english_pob: It happened on the day when Yahweh spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt—
rows.spanish_base_english: Now it happened on the day when Yahweh spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt—

rows.spanish: Pero Moisés dijo delante de Yahvé: «He aquí, yo soy incircunciso de labios; ¿y cómo me escuchará Faraón?»
rows.current_english_pob: But Moses said before the LORD, “Look, I am uncircumcised of lips; so how will Pharaoh listen to me?”
rows.spanish_base_english: But Moses said before Yahweh, “Behold, I am uncircumcised of lips; so how will Pharaoh listen to me?”

rows.spanish: Y Moisés tenía ochenta años, y Aarón tenía ochenta y tres años, cuando hablaron a Faraón.
rows.current_english_pob: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron was eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron was eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

rows.spanish: Entonces Yahvé dijo a Moisés y a Aarón, diciendo:
rows.current_english_pob: Then the LORD said to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Yahweh said to Moses and to Aaron,

rows.spanish: Y le dirás: «Yahvé, el Dios de los hebreos, me ha enviado a ti, diciendo: “Deja ir a mi pueblo, para que me sirvan en el desierto. Pero he aquí, hasta ahora no has escuchado”».
rows.current_english_pob: And you shall say to him, ‘Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying: Let my people go, so that they may serve me in the wilderness. But behold, until now you have not listened.’
rows.spanish_base_english: And you shall say to him, ‘Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying: Let my people go, so that they may serve me in the wilderness. But behold, until now you have not listened.’

rows.spanish: Así dice Yahvé: Con esto sabrás que yo soy Yahvé: he aquí, estoy golpeando con la vara que está en mi mano las aguas que están en el Nilo, y se convertirán en sangre.
rows.current_english_pob: Thus says Yahweh: By this you will know that I am Yahweh: behold, I am striking the water that is in the Nile with the staff that is in my hand, and it will be turned to blood.
rows.spanish_base_english: Thus says Yahweh: By this you will know that I am Yahweh: behold, I am striking the water that is in the Nile with the staff that is in my hand, and it will be turned to blood.

rows.spanish: Entonces Yahvé dijo a Moisés: «Di a Aarón: “Toma tu vara y extiende tu mano sobre las aguas de Egipto —sobre sus ríos, sobre sus canales, sobre sus estanques y sobre todo depósito de sus aguas— para que se conviertan en sangre. Y habrá sangre en toda la tierra de Egipto, incluso en vasos de madera y de piedra”».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt—over their rivers, over their Nile canals, over their ponds, and over every collection of their waters—that they may become blood. And there will be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, even in wooden and stone vessels.’”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt—over their rivers, over their canals, over their ponds, and over every pool of their waters—that they may become blood. And there will be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, even in wooden and stone vessels.’”

rows.spanish: Pero si te niegas a dejarlos ir, he aquí, yo golpearé todo tu territorio con ranas.
rows.current_english_pob: But if you refuse to let them go, behold, I will strike all your territory with frogs.
rows.spanish_base_english: But if you refuse to let them go, behold, I will strike all your territory with frogs.

rows.spanish: Él dijo: «Mañana». Y dijo: «Conforme a tu palabra, para que sepas que no hay nadie como Yahvé nuestro Dios».
rows.current_english_pob: He said, “Tomorrow.” And he said, “According to your word, so that you may know that there is no one like Yahweh our God.”
rows.spanish_base_english: He said, “Tomorrow.” And he said, “According to your word, so that you may know that there is no one like Yahweh our God.”

rows.spanish: Yahvé hizo conforme a la palabra de Moisés, y las ranas murieron en las casas, en los patios y en los campos.
rows.current_english_pob: And the LORD did according to the word of Moses, and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courtyards, and out of the fields.
rows.spanish_base_english: And Yahweh did according to the word of Moses, and the frogs died from the houses, from the courtyards, and from the fields.

rows.spanish: Entonces Yahvé dijo a Moisés: “Levántate muy temprano por la mañana y preséntate delante de Faraón. Mira, él sale al agua, y le dirás: ‘Así dice Yahvé: Deja ir a mi pueblo, para que me sirvan.’”
rows.current_english_pob: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning and station yourself before Pharaoh. Look, he is going out to the water, and you shall say to him, ‘Thus says the LORD: Let my people go, so that they may serve me.’”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning and station yourself before Pharaoh. Behold, he is going out to the water, and you shall say to him, ‘Thus says Yahweh: Let my people go, so that they may serve me.’”

rows.spanish: Porque si no dejas ir a mi pueblo, he aquí, yo envío sobre ti, sobre tus siervos, sobre tu pueblo y en tus casas el enjambre. Y las casas de Egipto se llenarán del enjambre, y también el suelo sobre el que están.
rows.current_english_pob: For if you do not let my people go, behold, I am sending the swarm upon you, upon your servants, upon your people, and into your houses. The houses of Egypt will be filled with the swarm, and also the ground on which they are.
rows.spanish_base_english: For if you do not let my people go, behold, I am sending the swarm upon you, upon your servants, upon your people, and into your houses. The houses of Egypt will be filled with the swarm, and also the ground on which they are.

rows.spanish: Y haré distinción entre mi pueblo y tu pueblo. Mañana será esta la señal.
rows.current_english_pob: And I will make a distinction between my people and your people. Tomorrow this sign will happen.
rows.spanish_base_english: And I will put a distinction between my people and your people. Tomorrow this sign will be.

rows.spanish: Entonces Yahvé dijo a Moisés: «Preséntate ante Faraón y háblale: “Así dice Yahvé, el Dios de los hebreos: Deja ir a mi pueblo, para que me sirvan”».
rows.current_english_pob: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh and say to him, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, so that they may serve me.'"
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Yahweh said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh and speak to him, 'Thus says Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, so that they may serve me.'"

rows.spanish: Porque si te niegas a dejarlos ir y todavía los retienes,
rows.current_english_pob: For if you refuse to let them go and still hold on to them,
rows.spanish_base_english: For if you refuse to let them go and still hold them back,

rows.spanish: Faraón envió, y he aquí que no había muerto ni uno del ganado de Israel. Pero el corazón de Faraón se puso pesado, y no dejó ir al pueblo.
rows.current_english_pob: Pharaoh sent, and behold, not even one of Israel’s livestock had died. But Pharaoh’s heart was heavy, and he did not let the people go.
rows.spanish_base_english: Pharaoh sent, and behold, not even one of Israel’s livestock had died. But Pharaoh’s heart was heavy, and he did not let the people go.

rows.spanish: Y se convertirá en polvo fino sobre toda la tierra de Egipto, y se convertirá en llagas que brotan con ampollas sobre el hombre y sobre la bestia por toda la tierra de Egipto.
rows.current_english_pob: And it will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and it will become boils breaking out with blisters on man and on beast throughout all the land of Egypt.
rows.spanish_base_english: And it will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and it will become festering boils on man and on beast throughout all the land of Egypt.

rows.spanish: He aquí, como a esta hora mañana haré llover granizo muy pesado, como nunca ha habido en Egipto desde el día en que fue fundado hasta ahora.
rows.current_english_pob: Behold, about this time tomorrow I will rain down very heavy hail, such as has never been in Egypt from the day it was founded until now.
rows.spanish_base_english: Behold, about this time tomorrow I will rain down very heavy hail, such as has never been in Egypt from the day it was founded until now.

rows.spanish: Así que ahora, manda a poner a resguardo tu ganado y todo lo que tienes en el campo. Toda persona y todo animal que se encuentre en el campo y no sea llevado a la casa—el granizo caerá sobre ellos, y morirán.
rows.current_english_pob: So now, send word and bring your livestock and everything you have in the field to safety. Every man and beast that is found in the field and is not gathered into the house—the hail will come down on them, and they will die.
rows.spanish_base_english: So now, send word, bring your livestock and everything you have in the field to safety. Every person and beast that is found in the field and is not brought into the house—the hail will come down on them, and they will die.

rows.spanish: Entonces Yahvé dijo a Moisés: «Extiende tu mano hacia el cielo, para que caiga granizo sobre toda la tierra de Egipto, sobre el hombre y sobre la bestia y sobre toda planta del campo en la tierra de Egipto».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky, so that hail may come over all the land of Egypt—on man and on beast and on every plant of the field in the land of Egypt.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky, so that hail may fall on all the land of Egypt—on man and on beast and on every plant of the field in the land of Egypt.”

rows.spanish: para que cuentes a oídos de tu hijo y de tu nieto cómo hice escarnio de los egipcios, y mis señales que puse entre ellos, para que sepan que yo soy Yahvé.
rows.current_english_pob: so that you may tell in the hearing of your son and of your grandson how I dealt harshly with Egypt, and my signs that I placed among them, and so that you may know that I am Yahweh.
rows.spanish_base_english: so that you may tell in the hearing of your son and of your grandson how I made a mockery of the Egyptians, and my signs that I placed among them, so that you may know that I am Yahweh.

rows.spanish: Porque si te niegas a dejar ir a mi pueblo, he aquí, mañana traeré langostas dentro de tu territorio.
rows.current_english_pob: For if you refuse to let my people go, behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your territory.
rows.spanish_base_english: For if you refuse to let my people go, behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your territory.

rows.spanish: Cubrirán la superficie de la tierra, de modo que no se podrá ver el suelo; comerán lo que queda de los sobrevivientes que les dejó el granizo, y comerán todo árbol que crece para ustedes en el campo.
rows.current_english_pob: And it will cover the surface of the land, so that one will not be able to see the land; and it will eat what remains of the survivors left to you from the hail, and it will eat every tree growing for you out of the field.
rows.spanish_base_english: And it will cover the surface of the land, so that one will not be able to see the land; and it will eat the rest of what has escaped, which remains to you from the hail, and it will eat every tree growing for you out of the field.

rows.spanish: Moisés dijo: «Iremos con nuestros jóvenes y nuestros mayores; iremos con nuestros hijos y nuestras hijas, con nuestros rebaños y nuestro ganado, pues debemos celebrar una fiesta para Yahvé».
rows.current_english_pob: Moses said, “We will go with our young and our old; we will go with our sons and our daughters, with our flocks and our herds, because we must hold a feast to the LORD.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Moses said, “We will go with our young and our old; we will go with our sons and our daughters, with our flocks and our herds, for we must hold a feast to Yahweh.”

rows.spanish: Así que Moisés extendió su vara sobre la tierra de Egipto, y Yahvé condujo un viento del oriente sobre la tierra todo aquel día y toda aquella noche. Cuando llegó la mañana, el viento del oriente trajo las langostas.
rows.current_english_pob: So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and Yahweh drove an east wind over the land all that day and all the night. When morning came, the east wind had brought the locusts.
rows.spanish_base_english: So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and Yahweh drove an east wind over the land all that day and all that night. When morning came, the east wind brought the locusts.

rows.spanish: Y las langostas subieron sobre toda la tierra de Egipto y se posaron por todo el territorio de Egipto, muy grave; nunca antes había habido langostas como ellas, ni después de ellas volverá a haber algo semejante.
rows.current_english_pob: And the locusts came up over all the land of Egypt and settled in every territory of Egypt—an extremely severe swarm. never before had there been locusts like it, nor will there be again after it.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the locusts came up over all the land of Egypt and settled within all the territory of Egypt, very severe; never before had there been locusts like it, nor will there be again after it.

rows.spanish: Y morirá todo primogénito en la tierra de Egipto: desde el primogénito de Faraón, que está sentado sobre su trono, hasta el primogénito de la esclava que está detrás de las muelas de molino, y todo primogénito del ganado.
rows.current_english_pob: And every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sits on his throne, to the firstborn of the servant woman who is behind the millstones, and every firstborn of the livestock.
rows.spanish_base_english: And every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sits on his throne, to the firstborn of the slave woman who is behind the millstones, and every firstborn of the livestock.

rows.spanish: Y habrá un gran clamor por toda la tierra de Egipto, cual no lo ha habido antes ni lo habrá de nuevo.
rows.current_english_pob: And there will be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as has never happened before, nor will ever happen again.
rows.spanish_base_english: And there will be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as has never been before, nor will ever be again.

rows.spanish: Yahvé dijo a Moisés y a Aarón en la tierra de Egipto, diciendo:
rows.current_english_pob: The LORD said to Moses and to Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
rows.spanish_base_english: And Yahweh said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,

rows.spanish: Y la sangre les servirá de señal sobre las casas donde estén ustedes. Cuando vea la sangre, pasaré sobre ustedes, y no habrá sobre ustedes plaga para destrucción cuando hiera la tierra de Egipto.
rows.current_english_pob: And the blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you are. When I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will be among you to destroy, when I strike the land of Egypt.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you are. When I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will be upon you for destruction when I strike the land of Egypt.

rows.spanish: Hornearon la masa que habían sacado de Egipto en tortas sin levadura, pues no había fermentado: habían sido expulsados de Egipto y no podían demorarse, y no habían preparado provisiones para sí mismos.
rows.current_english_pob: They baked the dough they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened cakes, since it had not become leavened: they had been driven out of Egypt and could not delay, and had not prepared provisions for themselves.
rows.spanish_base_english: And they baked the dough that they had brought out from Egypt into unleavened cakes, because it had not leavened; for they had been driven out from Egypt and could not delay, and they had not prepared provisions for themselves either.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, la residencia de los hijos de Israel, que habitaron en Egipto, fue de cuatrocientos treinta años.
rows.current_english_pob: The dwelling of the sons of Israel, who lived in Egypt, was four hundred thirty years.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the dwelling of the sons of Israel, who lived in Egypt, was four hundred thirty years.

rows.spanish: Pero todo esclavo de un hombre, comprado con dinero, cuando lo hayas circuncidado, podrá comer de ella.
rows.current_english_pob: But every man's servant, bought with silver—when you have circumcised him, then he may eat of it.
rows.spanish_base_english: But every man's slave, bought with silver—when you have circumcised him, then he may eat of it.

rows.spanish: Consagra para mí todo primogénito, el primero que abre todo vientre entre los hijos de Israel, tanto del hombre como de la bestia; mío es.
rows.current_english_pob: Consecrate to me every firstborn, the first to open every womb among the sons of Israel, among man and among beast; it is mine.
rows.spanish_base_english: Consecrate to me every firstborn, the first to open every womb among the sons of Israel, both of man and of beast; it is mine.

rows.spanish: Y cuando tu hijo te pregunte en el futuro: «¿Qué es esto?», le dirás: «Con mano poderosa Yahvé nos sacó de Egipto, de la casa de servidumbre».
rows.current_english_pob: And when your son asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What is this?’ then you shall say to him, ‘By a mighty hand the LORD brought us out from Egypt, from the house of servants.’
rows.spanish_base_english: And when your son asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What is this?’ then you shall say to him, ‘By strength of hand Yahweh brought us out from Egypt, from the house of slavery.’

rows.spanish: Cuando el faraón dejó salir al pueblo, Dios no los condujo por el camino de la tierra de los filisteos, aunque estaba cerca; porque Dios dijo: «No sea que el pueblo cambie de parecer cuando vean la guerra y vuelvan a Egipto»
rows.current_english_pob: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, though it was near; for God said, “Lest the people change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, though it was near; for God said, “Lest the people change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt.”

rows.spanish: Y endureceré el corazón de Faraón, y él los perseguirá; y me glorificaré en Faraón y en todo su ejército, y los egipcios sabrán que yo soy Yahvé». Y así lo hicieron.
rows.current_english_pob: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he will pursue them; and I will get glory over Pharaoh and over all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am Yahweh.” And they did so.
rows.spanish_base_english: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he will pursue them; and I will gain glory through Pharaoh and through all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am Yahweh.” And they did so.

rows.spanish: Cuando el faraón se acercó, los hijos de Israel levantaron sus ojos, y he aquí que los egipcios iban marchando detrás de ellos; y tuvieron mucho temor, y los hijos de Israel clamaron a Yahvé.
rows.current_english_pob: As Pharaoh drew near, the sons of Israel lifted up their eyes, and behold, the Egyptians were marching after them; and they were very afraid, and the sons of Israel cried out to Yahweh.
rows.spanish_base_english: As Pharaoh drew near, the sons of Israel lifted up their eyes, and behold, the Egyptians were marching after them; and they were very afraid, and the sons of Israel cried out to Yahweh.

rows.spanish: ¿No es esto lo que te dijimos en Egipto: «Déjanos para que sirvamos a los egipcios»? Habría sido mejor para nosotros servir a los egipcios que morir en el desierto.
rows.current_english_pob: Is this not the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Leave us alone so that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.
rows.spanish_base_english: Is this not the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Leave us alone, and let us serve the Egyptians’? For it is better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.

rows.spanish: Y Moisés dijo al pueblo: «No teman. Manténganse firmes y vean la salvación de Yahvé, que él realizará para ustedes hoy; porque los egipcios que hoy ven, no los volverán a ver».
rows.current_english_pob: And Moses said to the people, “Do not fear. Stand firm, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will accomplish for you today; for the Egyptians whom you see today, you will never see again forever.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Moses said to the people, “Do not fear. Stand firm, and see the salvation of Yahweh, which he will accomplish for you today; for the Egyptians whom you see today, you will never see again.”

rows.spanish: Y quitó las ruedas de sus carros, y los hizo avanzar con dificultad. Y Egipto dijo: «Huyamos de delante de Israel, porque Yahvé pelea por ellos contra Egipto».
rows.current_english_pob: And he removed the wheels from his chariots, and drove them with difficulty. And Egypt said, “Let me flee from before Israel, for the LORD is fighting for them against Egypt.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he removed the wheels from their chariots, and drove them with difficulty. And Egypt said, “Let us flee from before Israel, for Yahweh is fighting for them against Egypt.”

rows.spanish: ¿Quién como tú entre los dioses, oh Yahvé? ¿Quién como tú, majestuoso en santidad, imponente en alabanzas, hacedor de maravillas?
rows.current_english_pob: Who is like you among the gods, O LORD? Who is like you, majestic in holiness, feared in praises, doing wonders?
rows.spanish_base_english: Who is like you among the gods, O Yahweh? Who is like you, majestic in holiness, awesome in praises, doing wonders?

rows.spanish: Así que clamó a Yahvé, y Yahvé le mostró un trozo de madera. Él lo arrojó al agua, y el agua se volvió dulce. Allí estableció para ellos un estatuto y un juicio, y allí los probó.
rows.current_english_pob: So he cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a tree. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There he made for them a statute and a judgment, and there he tested them.
rows.spanish_base_english: So he cried out to Yahweh, and Yahweh showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There he made for them a statute and a judgment, and there he tested them.

rows.spanish: Mientras Aarón hablaba a toda la congregación de los hijos de Israel, ellos se volvieron hacia el desierto, y he aquí, la gloria de Yahvé apareció en la nube.
rows.current_english_pob: And it happened, as Aaron spoke to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, that they turned toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of Yahweh appeared in the cloud.
rows.spanish_base_english: And it happened, as Aaron spoke to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, that they turned toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of Yahweh appeared in the cloud.

rows.spanish: Cuando la capa de rocío se había levantado, he aquí que sobre la superficie del desierto había algo fino, como en hojuelas, fino como escarcha sobre el suelo.
rows.current_english_pob: When the layer of dew had gone up, behold, on the surface of the wilderness was a fine, flaky thing, fine as frost on the ground.
rows.spanish_base_english: When the layer of dew had gone up, behold, on the surface of the wilderness was a fine, flaky thing, fine as frost on the ground.

rows.spanish: Esto es lo que Yahvé ha mandado: “Recojan de eso, cada uno según lo que coma; un omer por cabeza, según el número de las personas que tengan. Cada uno tomará para los que están en su tienda.”
rows.current_english_pob: This is the word that Yahweh has commanded: ‘Gather from it, each man according to his eating; an omer per person, according to the number of your persons. Each man shall take for those who are in his tent.’
rows.spanish_base_english: This is the thing that Yahweh has commanded: ‘Gather from it, each one according to his eating; an omer per person, according to the number of your persons. Each one shall take for those who are in his tent.’

rows.spanish: Sucedió que el sexto día recogieron doble porción de pan, dos ómeres para cada uno, y vinieron todos los jefes de la congregación y se lo dijeron a Moisés.
rows.current_english_pob: And it happened on the sixth day that they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for each person, and all the leaders of the congregation came and told Moses.
rows.spanish_base_english: And it happened on the sixth day that they gathered double the bread, two omers for each one, and all the leaders of the congregation came and told Moses.

rows.spanish: Y Moisés dijo: «Cómanlo hoy, porque hoy es un sábado para Yahvé; hoy no lo encontrarán en el campo».
rows.current_english_pob: And Moses said, “Eat it today, because today is a Sabbath to the LORD; today you will not find it in the field.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Moses said, “Eat it today, for today is a Sabbath to Yahweh; today you will not find it in the field.”

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, un ómer es la décima parte de un éfah.
rows.current_english_pob: An omer is a tenth of an ephah.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now an omer is a tenth of an ephah.

rows.spanish: Así que el pueblo contendió con Moisés y dijo: «Dennos agua para que bebamos». Y Moisés les dijo: «¿Por qué contienden conmigo? ¿Por qué ponen a prueba a Yahvé?»
rows.current_english_pob: So the people quarreled with Moses and said, “Give us water so that we may drink.” And Moses said to them, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test Yahweh?”
rows.spanish_base_english: So the people quarreled with Moses and said, “Give us water so that we may drink.” And Moses said to them, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test Yahweh?”

rows.spanish: Y allí el pueblo tuvo sed de agua, y el pueblo murmuró contra Moisés y dijo: «¿Por qué nos sacaste de Egipto, para matarme a mí y a mis hijos y a mi ganado con sed?»
rows.current_english_pob: And there the people thirsted for water, and the people grumbled against Moses and said, “Why is this—that you brought us up from Egypt to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And there the people thirsted for water, and the people grumbled against Moses and said, “Why did you bring us up from Egypt, to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?”

rows.spanish: He aquí, yo estaré delante de ti allí, sobre la roca en Horeb; y golpearás la roca, y de ella saldrá agua, y el pueblo beberá. Y Moisés hizo así, en presencia de los ancianos de Israel.
rows.current_english_pob: Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock at Horeb, and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out from it, and the people will drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
rows.spanish_base_english: Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock at Horeb, and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out from it, and the people will drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.

rows.spanish: Y Josué venció a Amalec y a su pueblo con la espada.
rows.current_english_pob: And Joshua overcame Amalek and his people with the sword.
rows.spanish_base_english: And Joshua weakened Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.

rows.spanish: Entonces Jetró, sacerdote de Madián, suegro de Moisés, oyó todo lo que Dios había hecho por Moisés y por Israel, su pueblo; es decir, que Yahvé había sacado a Israel de Egipto.
rows.current_english_pob: Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel his people, that Yahweh had brought Israel out of Egypt.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel his people, that Yahweh had brought Israel out of Egypt.

rows.spanish: Que juzguen al pueblo en todo tiempo. Todo asunto grande te lo traerán, pero todo asunto pequeño lo juzgarán ellos mismos. Así aliviarás tu carga, y ellos la llevarán contigo.
rows.current_english_pob: And let them judge the people at all times. Then every great matter they shall bring to you, but every small matter they themselves shall judge. So make it lighter for yourself, and they will bear the burden with you.
rows.spanish_base_english: And let them judge the people at all times. Then every great matter they shall bring to you, but every small matter they themselves shall judge. So it will be lighter for you, and they will bear the burden with you.

rows.spanish: Entonces el monte Sinaí estaba todo cubierto de humo, porque Yahvé había descendido sobre él en fuego, y su humo subió como el humo de un horno, y todo el monte tembló grandemente.
rows.current_english_pob: Mount Sinai was all in smoke because Yahweh had descended on it in fire, and its smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain trembled greatly.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Mount Sinai was all in smoke because Yahweh had descended on it in fire, and its smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain trembled greatly.

rows.spanish: Entonces Moisés descendió al pueblo y les dijo.
rows.current_english_pob: So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.
rows.spanish_base_english: So Moses went down to the people and said to them.

rows.spanish: Y Dios habló todas estas palabras, diciendo,
rows.current_english_pob: And God spoke all these words, saying:
rows.spanish_base_english: And God spoke all these words, saying,

rows.spanish: Yo soy Yahvé, tu Dios, que te saqué de la tierra de Egipto, de la casa de esclavitud.
rows.current_english_pob: I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of servants.
rows.spanish_base_english: I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.

rows.spanish: pero el séptimo día es un sábado para Yahvé tu Dios; no harás ningún trabajo: tú, ni tu hijo, ni tu hija, ni tu esclavo, ni tu esclava, ni tu ganado, ni el residente extranjero que está dentro de tus puertas.
rows.current_english_pob: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to Yahweh your God; you shall not do any work—you, or your son, or your daughter, your male servant, or your female servant, or your livestock, or the sojourner within your gates.
rows.spanish_base_english: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to Yahweh your God; you shall not do any work—you, or your son, or your daughter, your male slave, or your female slave, or your livestock, or the sojourner within your gates.

rows.spanish: No codiciarás la casa de tu prójimo; no codiciarás la mujer de tu prójimo, ni su esclavo varón, ni su esclava, ni su buey, ni su asno, ni cosa alguna que pertenezca a tu prójimo.
rows.current_english_pob: You shall not covet your neighbor’s house; you shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his male servant, or his female servant, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.
rows.spanish_base_english: You shall not covet your neighbor’s house; you shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his male slave, or his female slave, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.

rows.spanish: Y todo el pueblo veía los truenos, los destellos de fuego, el sonido de la trompeta, y el monte humeando; y cuando el pueblo vio esto, temblaron y se mantuvieron a distancia.
rows.current_english_pob: All the people were seeing the thunder and the flashes of fire, and the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking; and when the people saw it, they trembled and stood at a distance.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now all the people were seeing the thunder and the flashes of fire, and the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking; and when the people saw it, they trembled and stood at a distance.

rows.spanish: Estas son las sentencias judiciales que pondrás delante de ellos:
rows.current_english_pob: These are the judgments that you shall set before them:
rows.spanish_base_english: Now these are the ordinances that you shall set before them:

rows.spanish: Si compras un esclavo hebreo, servirá seis años; pero en el séptimo año saldrá libre, sin pago.
rows.current_english_pob: If you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years, but in the seventh he shall go out free, without payment.
rows.spanish_base_english: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he shall serve six years, but in the seventh he shall go out free, without payment.

rows.spanish: Pero si el esclavo dice claramente: «Amo a mi amo, a mi esposa y a mis hijos; no saldré libre»,
rows.current_english_pob: But if the servant plainly says, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,’
rows.spanish_base_english: But if the slave plainly says, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,’

rows.spanish: Y si un hombre vende a su hija como esclava, no saldrá como salen los esclavos varones.
rows.current_english_pob: And if a man sells his daughter as a female servant, she shall not go out as the male servants go out.
rows.spanish_base_english: And if a man sells his daughter as a female slave, she shall not go out as the male slaves go out.

rows.spanish: Pero si un hombre trama matar a su prójimo con engaño, lo quitarás incluso de mi altar para que muera.
rows.current_english_pob: But if a man schemes against his neighbor to kill him by treachery, you shall take him even from my altar to die.
rows.spanish_base_english: But if a man acts presumptuously against his neighbor to kill him by treachery, you shall take him from my altar to die.

rows.spanish: Y si un hombre golpea a su esclavo o a su esclava con una vara, y el esclavo muere bajo su mano, deberá ser vengado sin falta.
rows.current_english_pob: And if a man strikes his male servant or his female servant with a rod, and the servant dies under his hand, he must surely be avenged.
rows.spanish_base_english: And if a man strikes his male slave or his female slave with a rod, and the slave dies under his hand, he must surely be avenged.

rows.spanish: Y si un hombre golpea el ojo de su esclavo o el ojo de su esclava y lo destruye, lo dejará ir libre en compensación por su ojo.
rows.current_english_pob: And if a man strikes the eye of his male servant or the eye of his female servant and destroys it, he shall let him go free in compensation for his eye.
rows.spanish_base_english: And if a man strikes the eye of his male slave or the eye of his female slave and destroys it, he shall let him go free in compensation for his eye.

rows.spanish: Y si le saca un diente a su esclavo, o un diente a su esclava, lo dejará en libertad en compensación por su diente.
rows.current_english_pob: And if he knocks out the tooth of his male servant or the tooth of his female servant, he shall let him go free in compensation for his tooth.
rows.spanish_base_english: And if he knocks out the tooth of his male slave or the tooth of his female slave, he shall let him go free in compensation for his tooth.

rows.spanish: Si el buey cornea a un esclavo o a una esclava, dará treinta siclos de plata a su amo, y el buey será apedreado.
rows.current_english_pob: If the ox gores a male servant or a female servant, he shall give thirty shekels of silver to his master, and the ox shall be stoned.
rows.spanish_base_english: If the ox gores a male slave or a female slave, he shall give thirty shekels of silver to his master, and the ox shall be stoned.

rows.spanish: Si su dueño está con él, no hará restitución; si es un trabajador contratado, vino por su paga.
rows.current_english_pob: If its owner is with it, he shall not make restitution; if it is a hired thing, it came for its hire.
rows.spanish_base_english: If its owner is with it, he shall not make restitution; if he is a hired worker, it came for his hire.

rows.spanish: Pero en el séptimo año la dejarás reposar y la abandonarás, para que coman los pobres de tu pueblo; y lo que ellos dejen, lo comerán los animales del campo. Lo mismo harás con tu viña y con tus olivos.
rows.current_english_pob: But in the seventh year you shall let it rest and leave it alone, so that the poor of your people may eat; and what they leave, the wild animals of the field may eat. You shall do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
rows.spanish_base_english: But in the seventh year you shall let it rest and abandon it, so that the poor of your people may eat; and what they leave, the wild animals of the field may eat. You shall do the same with your vineyard and your olive trees.

rows.spanish: He aquí, yo envío un ángel delante de ti, para guardarte en el camino y para llevarte al lugar que he preparado.
rows.current_english_pob: Behold, I am sending an angel before you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.
rows.spanish_base_english: Behold, I am sending an angel before you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.

rows.spanish: No habrá en tu tierra ninguna mujer que sufra un aborto espontáneo ni ninguna estéril; yo llenaré el número de tus días.
rows.current_english_pob: There shall not be one miscarrying or barren in your land; I will fill up the number of your days.
rows.spanish_base_english: There shall be none miscarrying or barren in your land; I will fulfill the number of your days.

rows.spanish: Entonces Moisés tomó la sangre y la arrojó sobre el pueblo, y dijo: «He aquí la sangre del pacto que Yahvé ha hecho con ustedes acerca de todas estas palabras».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Moses took the blood and threw it on the people, and said, “Behold, the blood of the covenant that Yahweh has made with you concerning all these words.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Moses took the blood and threw it on the people, and said, “Behold, the blood of the covenant that Yahweh has made with you concerning all these words.”

rows.spanish: Y a los ancianos les dijo: «Quédense aquí para nosotros hasta que volvamos a ustedes. Y he aquí, Aarón y Hur están con ustedes. Quien tenga un asunto, que se acerque a ellos».
rows.current_english_pob: And to the elders he said, “Wait here for us until we return to you. And look, Aaron and Hur are with you. Whoever has a dispute, let him approach them.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And to the elders he said, “Wait here for us until we return to you. And behold, Aaron and Hur are with you. Whoever has a matter, let him approach them.”

rows.spanish: Y los querubines extenderán sus alas hacia arriba, cubriendo por encima con sus alas el propiciatorio, y sus rostros estarán el uno frente al otro; los rostros de los querubines estarán hacia el propiciatorio.
rows.current_english_pob: And the cherubim shall spread out their wings upward, overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings, and their faces shall be one toward another; the faces of the cherubim shall be toward the mercy seat.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the cherubim shall spread out their wings upward, overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings, and their faces shall be toward one another; the faces of the cherubim shall be toward the mercy seat.

rows.spanish: y un botón debajo de dos ramas de ella, y un botón debajo de dos ramas de ella, y un botón debajo de dos ramas de ella, para las seis ramas que salen del candelabro.
rows.current_english_pob: and a knob under two branches from it, and a knob under two branches from it, and a knob under two branches from it, for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
rows.spanish_base_english: and a bulb under two branches from it, and a bulb under two branches from it, and a bulb under two branches from it, for the six branches going out from the lampstand.

rows.spanish: Harás sus siete lámparas, y las pondrán de modo que alumbren hacia su frente.
rows.current_english_pob: You shall make its seven lamps, and he shall set up its lamps so that they give light in front of it.
rows.spanish_base_english: You shall make its seven lamps, and they shall set up its lamps so that they give light toward the front of it.

rows.spanish: Harás cincuenta presillas en el borde de una cortina, la más exterior del conjunto unido, y cincuenta presillas en el borde de la segunda cortina que se une a ella.
rows.current_english_pob: And you shall make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain, the outermost one in the set joined together, and fifty loops on the edge of the second curtain that is joined to it.
rows.spanish_base_english: And you shall make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain, the outermost in the first set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set.

rows.spanish: Y el excedente que queda de las cortinas de la tienda, la media cortina que queda, colgará sobre la parte trasera del tabernáculo.
rows.current_english_pob: And the overhang that remains from the tent curtains—the half curtain that remains over—shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the excess that remains from the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remains, shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.

rows.spanish: Cada tabla tendrá dos espigas unidas entre sí; así harás todas las tablas del tabernáculo.
rows.current_english_pob: Each board is to have two tenons joined one to another; this is how you shall make all the boards of the tabernacle.
rows.spanish_base_english: Each board is to have two tenons joined to one another; thus you shall make all the boards of the tabernacle.

rows.spanish: Y para la puerta del atrio habrá una cortina de veinte codos de largo, de azul, púrpura y carmesí, y de lino fino torcido, obra de bordador, con cuatro columnas y cuatro basas.
rows.current_english_pob: And for the gate of the courtyard there shall be a screen twenty cubits long, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twined linen, the work of an embroiderer, with their four pillars and their four bases.
rows.spanish_base_english: And for the gate of the courtyard there shall be a screen twenty cubits long, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twined linen, the work of an embroiderer, with four pillars and four bases.

rows.spanish: Y harás dos cadenas de oro puro, de trabajo trenzado, como cordones; y pondrás las cadenas trenzadas sobre los engastes.
rows.current_english_pob: And make two chains of pure gold, braided like cords; and put the braided chains on the settings.
rows.spanish_base_english: And make two chains of pure gold, braided work like cords; and put the corded chains on the settings.

rows.spanish: Y las piedras serán según los nombres de los hijos de Israel, doce según sus nombres. Serán como grabados de sello, cada cual según su nombre, para las doce tribus.
rows.current_english_pob: And the stones shall correspond to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names. They shall be engraved like a signet, each with his name, for the twelve tribes.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the stones shall be according to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names. They shall be like signet engravings, each according to his name, for the twelve tribes.

rows.spanish: Entonces tomarás las vestiduras y vestirás a Aarón con la túnica, el manto del efod, el efod y el pectoral; y lo ceñirás con la banda hábilmente tejida del efod.
rows.current_english_pob: Then you shall take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastpiece, and you shall skillfully fasten it on him with the woven band of the ephod.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then you shall take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastpiece, and you shall bind it on him with the skillfully woven band of the ephod.

rows.spanish: Les ceñirás cintos a Aarón y a sus hijos, y les pondrás gorros. El sacerdocio será suyo por estatuto perpetuo. Así investirás a Aarón y a sus hijos.
rows.current_english_pob: You shall fasten sashes on them, on Aaron and on his sons, and you shall bind caps on them. The priesthood shall belong to them as a permanent statute. So you shall ordain Aaron and his sons.
rows.spanish_base_english: You shall fasten sashes on them, on Aaron and on his sons, and you shall bind caps on them. The priesthood shall be theirs by a permanent statute. So you shall ordain Aaron and his sons.

rows.spanish: Y sacrificarás el carnero, y tomarás su sangre y la salpicarás contra el altar, todo alrededor.
rows.current_english_pob: And you shall slaughter the ram, and take its blood and throw it against the altar all around.
rows.spanish_base_english: And you shall slaughter the ram, and take its blood and splash it against the altar all around.

rows.spanish: Esto es lo que ofrecerás sobre el altar: dos corderos de un año cada día, de continuo.
rows.current_english_pob: This is what you shall offer on the altar: two one-year-old lambs each day continually.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now this is what you shall offer on the altar: two one-year-old lambs each day continually.

rows.spanish: Y consagraré la tienda de reunión y el altar; y consagraré a Aarón y a sus hijos para servirme como sacerdotes.
rows.current_english_pob: And I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar; and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests.
rows.spanish_base_english: And I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar; and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve as priests to me.

rows.spanish: Y hablarás a los hijos de Israel, diciendo: «Este será aceite de santa unción para mí, a través de sus generaciones»
rows.current_english_pob: And you shall speak to the sons of Israel, saying, ‘This shall be a holy anointing oil to me throughout your generations.’
rows.spanish_base_english: And you shall speak to the sons of Israel, saying, ‘This shall be a holy anointing oil for me throughout your generations.’

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, he puesto con él a Oholiab, hijo de Ahisamach, de la tribu de Dan; y en el corazón de todo sabio de corazón he puesto sabiduría, para que hagan todo lo que te he mandado.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, I have appointed with him Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; and in the heart of everyone wise of heart I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded you.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, I have appointed with him Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; and in the heart of everyone wise of heart I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded you.

rows.spanish: Y Yahvé dijo a Moisés.
rows.current_english_pob: And the LORD said to Moses, saying,
rows.spanish_base_english: And Yahweh said to Moses,

rows.spanish: Cuando el pueblo vio que Moisés tardaba en bajar del monte, el pueblo se reunió alrededor de Aarón y le dijo: «Levántate, haznos unos dioses que vayan delante de nosotros, porque este Moisés, el hombre que nos hizo subir de la tierra de Egipto, no sabemos qué ha sido de él». O «un dios ... que vaya delante de nosotros». Algunos entienden אֱלֹהִים aquí en sentido singular porque el relato pronto se centra en una sola imagen de becerro, pero la forma hebrea y el verbo siguiente son plurales.
rows.current_english_pob: When the people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain, the people gathered around Aaron and said to him, “Get up, make gods for us that will go before us, because this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt—we do not know what has happened to him.”
rows.spanish_base_english: When the people saw that Moses delayed coming down from the mountain, the people gathered around Aaron and said to him, “Get up, make gods for us that will go before us, because this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt—we do not know what has become of him.”

rows.spanish: Yahvé dijo a Moisés: «He visto a este pueblo, y he aquí, es un pueblo de cerviz dura».
rows.current_english_pob: And Yahweh said to Moses, “I have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff-necked people.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Yahweh said to Moses, “I have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff-necked people.”

rows.spanish: Acuérdate de Abraham, Isaac e Israel, tus siervos, a quienes juraste por ti mismo y les dijiste: «Multiplicaré su descendencia como las estrellas de los cielos, y toda esta tierra que dije que daría a su descendencia, y la heredarán para siempre».
rows.current_english_pob: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself and said to them, ‘I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens, and all this land that I have spoken of I will give to your offspring, and they shall inherit it forever.’
rows.spanish_base_english: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself and said to them, ‘I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens, and all this land that I said I would give to your offspring, and they shall inherit it forever.’

rows.spanish: Y las tablas eran la obra de Dios, y la escritura era la escritura de Dios, grabada sobre las tablas.
rows.current_english_pob: The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.

rows.spanish: Y Moisés dijo: «Conságrense hoy a Yahvé, pues cada uno ha estado contra su hijo y contra su hermano, para que él les conceda hoy una bendición».
rows.current_english_pob: And Moses said, “Today ordain yourselves to the LORD, for each man has been against his son and against his brother, so that he may bestow a blessing on you today.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Moses said, “Today fill your hand for Yahweh, for each man has been against his son and against his brother, so that he may bestow a blessing on you today.”

rows.spanish: Pero ahora ve y guía al pueblo al lugar del que te hablé. Mira, mi ángel irá delante de ti; pero el día en que yo les pida cuentas, les pediré cuentas por su pecado.
rows.current_english_pob: But now go, lead the people to where I have spoken to you. Look, my angel will go before you; but on the day when I call them to account, I will call them to account for their sin.
rows.spanish_base_english: But now go, lead the people to where I have spoken to you. Behold, my angel will go before you; but on the day when I punish, I will punish them for their sin.

rows.spanish: Entonces Yahvé hirió al pueblo con una plaga por lo que hicieron con el becerro que Aarón había hecho.
rows.current_english_pob: Then Yahweh struck the people with a plague because of what they did with the calf that Aaron made.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Yahweh struck the people because they made the calf that Aaron made.

rows.spanish: Yahvé dijo a Moisés: «Di a los hijos de Israel: “Ustedes son un pueblo duro de cerviz. Si yo subiera en medio de ustedes por un solo momento, los consumiría. Así que ahora, quítense de encima sus adornos, y sabré qué debo hacer con ustedes”».
rows.current_english_pob: And Yahweh said to Moses, “Say to the sons of Israel, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. In a single moment, if I were to go up in your midst, I would consume you. So now, take off your ornaments from upon you, and I will know what I should do with you.’”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Yahweh said to Moses, “Say to the sons of Israel, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I were to go up in your midst for one moment, I would consume you. So now, take off your ornaments from upon you, that I may know what I will do to you.’”

rows.spanish: Moisés tomaba la tienda y la instalaba para sí fuera del campamento, lejos del campamento, y la llamaba la tienda de reunión. Y todo el que buscaba a Yahvé salía a la tienda de reunión que estaba fuera del campamento.
rows.current_english_pob: Moses would take the tent and pitch it for himself outside the camp, far from the camp, and he called it the tent of meeting. And everyone seeking Yahweh would go out to the tent of meeting that was outside the camp.
