rows.spanish_base_english: He looked, and behold, there was a well in the field, and behold, three flocks of sheep were lying there beside it, because from that well they watered the flocks. And the stone on the mouth of the well was large.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, Laban tenía dos hijas; el nombre de la mayor era Lea, y el nombre de la menor era Raquel.
rows.current_english_pob: Laban had two daughters; the name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Laban had two daughters; the name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.

rows.spanish: Por la mañana, he aquí, era Lea. Y dijo a Labán: «¿Qué es esto que me has hecho? ¿No era por Raquel que trabajé contigo? ¿Por qué entonces me has engañado?»
rows.current_english_pob: In the morning, behold, it was Leah. And he said to Laban, “What is this you have done to me? Was it not for Rachel that I worked with you? So why have you deceived me?”
rows.spanish_base_english: In the morning, behold, it was Leah. And he said to Laban, “What is this you have done to me? Was it not for Rachel that I worked with you? Why then have you deceived me?”

rows.spanish: Completa la semana nupcial de esta, y te la daremos también a cambio del trabajo que trabajarás conmigo por otros siete años.
rows.current_english_pob: Complete this woman's bridal week, and we will give you this one also in return for the work that you will do with me for another seven years.
rows.spanish_base_english: Complete this one's bridal week, and we will give you this one also in return for the work that you will do with me for another seven years.

rows.spanish: Cuando Yahvé vio que Lea era odiada, abrió su matriz, pero Raquel era estéril.
rows.current_english_pob: When the LORD saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.
rows.spanish_base_english: When Yahweh saw that Leah was unloved, he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.

rows.spanish: Bilhá, la esclava de Raquel, concibió de nuevo y le dio a Jacob un segundo hijo.
rows.current_english_pob: Bilhah, Rachel’s female servant, conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.
rows.spanish_base_english: Bilhah, Rachel’s female slave, conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.

rows.spanish: Pero ella le dijo: “¿Es poca cosa que hayas tomado a mi marido? ¿También vas a tomar las mandrágoras de mi hijo?”. Raquel dijo: “Entonces podrá acostarse contigo esta noche a cambio de las mandrágoras de tu hijo.”
rows.current_english_pob: But she said to her, “Was it a small thing that you took my husband, and would you also take my son’s mandrakes?” Rachel said, “Then he may lie with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.”
rows.spanish_base_english: But she said to her, “Was it a small thing that you have taken my husband? Would you also take my son’s mandrakes?” Rachel said, “Then he may lie with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.”

rows.spanish: Y sucedió, cuando Raquel había dado a luz a José, que Jacob dijo a Labán: «Déjame partir, para que vaya a mi lugar y a mi tierra».
rows.current_english_pob: And it happened, when Rachel had borne Joseph, that Jacob said to Laban, “Send me away, that I may go to my own place and to my own land.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And it happened, when Rachel had borne Joseph, that Jacob said to Laban, “Send me away, that I may go to my place and to my land.”

rows.spanish: Porque lo poco que tenías antes de mí ha crecido hasta abundancia, y Yahvé te ha bendecido a mi paso. Y ahora, ¿cuándo proveeré yo también para mi propia casa?
rows.current_english_pob: For the little that you had before me has increased into abundance, and Yahweh has blessed you at my coming. And now, when shall I also provide for my own household?
rows.spanish_base_english: For the little that you had before me has increased to abundance, and Yahweh has blessed you at my foot. And now, when shall I also provide for my own household?

rows.spanish: Y él dijo: «¿Qué te daré?». Y Jacob dijo: «No me darás nada. Si haces esto por mí, volveré a apacentar tu rebaño y a guardarlo».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said, “What shall I give you?” And Jacob said, “You shall not give me anything. If you will do this thing for me, I will again pasture your flock and keep it.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said, “What shall I give you?” And Jacob said, “You shall not give me anything. If you will do this thing for me, I will again pasture your flock and keep it.”

rows.spanish: Así mi honradez responderá por mí en el futuro, cuando vengas a revisar mi salario: toda cabra que no sea moteada ni manchada, y todo cordero que no sea de color oscuro, será considerado robado si se encuentra conmigo.
rows.current_english_pob: So my honesty will answer for me later, when you come to inspect my wages: every goat that is not speckled and spotted, and every lamb that is not dark-colored, will be considered stolen if it is found with me.
rows.spanish_base_english: So my righteousness will answer for me later, when you come concerning my wages before you: every goat that is not speckled and spotted, and every lamb that is not dark, is stolen if it is found with me.

rows.spanish: Labán dijo: «Muy bien, que sea conforme a tu palabra».
rows.current_english_pob: Laban said, “Good—let it be according to your word.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Laban said, “Very well, let it be according to your word.”

rows.spanish: Y puso una distancia de tres días entre él y Jacob, y Jacob pastoreaba el resto del rebaño de Labán.
rows.current_english_pob: And he put a distance of three days between himself and Jacob, and Jacob was shepherding the rest of Laban’s flock.
rows.spanish_base_english: And he set a distance of three days between himself and Jacob, and Jacob was shepherding the rest of Laban’s flock.

rows.spanish: Y el hombre prosperó muchísimo, y llegó a tener muchos rebaños, esclavas y esclavos, camellos y asnos.
rows.current_english_pob: And the man became exceedingly prosperous, and he came to have many flocks and female servants and male servants and camels and donkeys.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the man became exceedingly prosperous, and he came to have many flocks and female slaves and male slaves and camels and donkeys.

rows.spanish: Y oyó las palabras de los hijos de Labán, diciendo: «Jacob ha tomado todo lo que pertenecía a nuestro padre, y de lo que pertenecía a nuestro padre ha adquirido toda esta riqueza».
rows.current_english_pob: He heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying, “Jacob has taken all that belonged to our father, and from what belonged to our father he has gained all this wealth.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Now he heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying, “Jacob has taken all that belonged to our father, and from what belonged to our father he has gained all this wealth.”

rows.spanish: Y vio Jacob el rostro de Labán, y he aquí, no era el mismo con él como antes.
rows.current_english_pob: And Jacob saw Laban’s face, and behold, it was not toward him as before.
rows.spanish_base_english: And Jacob saw Laban’s face, and behold, it was not toward him as before.

rows.spanish: Si decía: «Los moteados serían tu salario», entonces todo el rebaño paría crías moteadas; y si decía: «Los rayados serían tu salario», entonces todo el rebaño paría crías rayadas.
rows.current_english_pob: If he said this, ‘The speckled will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore speckled young; and if he said this, ‘The streaked will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore streaked young.
rows.spanish_base_english: If he said, ‘The speckled will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore speckled young; and if he said, ‘The streaked will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore streaked young.

rows.spanish: Ahora Labán había ido a esquilar su rebaño, y Raquel robó los ídolos domésticos que pertenecían a su padre.
rows.current_english_pob: Laban had gone to shear his flock, and Rachel stole the household idols that belonged to her father.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Laban had gone to shear his flock, and Rachel stole the household idols that belonged to her father.

rows.spanish: Y Jacob engañó a Labán el arameo al no decirle que huía.
rows.current_english_pob: And Jacob deceived Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was fleeing.
rows.spanish_base_english: And Jacob stole the heart of Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was fleeing.

rows.spanish: Y tomó consigo a sus parientes, y lo persiguió por siete días de camino, y lo alcanzó en la región montañosa de Galaad.
rows.current_english_pob: And he took his kinsmen with him, and pursued him for a journey of seven days, and caught up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
rows.spanish_base_english: And he took his kinsmen with him, and pursued him for seven days' journey, and overtook him in the hill country of Gilead.

rows.spanish: Ahora Raquel había tomado los ídolos domésticos, los había puesto en el cojín de la silla de montar del camello y se había sentado sobre ellos. Labán palpó por toda la tienda, pero no los encontró.
rows.current_english_pob: Rachel had taken the household idols, put them in the camel’s saddle cushion, and sat on them. Laban felt through the whole tent, but did not find them.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Rachel had taken the household idols, put them in the camel’s saddle cushion, and sat on them. Laban felt through the whole tent, but did not find them.

rows.spanish: Y Jacob dijo: «Oh Dios de mi padre Abraham y Dios de mi padre Isaac, oh Yahvé, que me dijo: “Vuelve a tu tierra y a tu parentela, y yo te haré bien”»
rows.current_english_pob: And Jacob said, “O God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, O Yahweh, who said to me, ‘Return to your land and to your kindred, and I will do you good,’”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Jacob said, “O God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, O Yahweh, who said to me, ‘Return to your land and to your kindred, and I will do you good,’”

rows.spanish: Y dio instrucciones al primero: «Cuando mi hermano Esaú te encuentre y te pregunte: “¿De quién eres, adónde vas y de quién son estos que van delante de ti?”,
rows.current_english_pob: And he commanded the first one, saying, “When Esau my brother meets you and asks you, ‘Whose are you, and where are you going, and whose are these before you?’...”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he commanded the first one, saying, “When Esau my brother meets you and asks you, saying, ‘To whom do you belong, and where are you going, and to whom do these before you belong?’...”

rows.spanish: Entonces dirás: «Es un regalo enviado a mi señor Esaú desde tu siervo Jacob; y mira, él también está detrás de nosotros».
rows.current_english_pob: Then you shall say, ‘Your servant Jacob's gift is sent to my lord, to Esau; and look, he also is behind us.’
rows.spanish_base_english: Then you shall say, ‘It is a gift sent to my lord Esau from your servant Jacob; and look, he also is behind us.’

rows.spanish: Y él dijo: «Déjame ir, porque ha salido la aurora». Pero él dijo: «No te dejaré ir a menos que me bendigas».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said, “Let me go, for the dawn has risen.” But he said, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said, “Let me go, for the dawn has risen.” But he said, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”

rows.spanish: Y le dijo: «¿Cuál es tu nombre?». Y dijo: «Jacob».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said to him, “What is your name?” And he said, “Jacob.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said to him, “What is your name?” And he said, “Jacob.”

rows.spanish: Entonces Jacob alzó sus ojos y miró, y he aquí, Esaú venía, y con él cuatrocientos hombres. Así dividió a los niños entre Lea, Raquel y las dos siervas.
rows.current_english_pob: Then Jacob lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, Esau was coming, and with him were four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two female servants.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Jacob lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, Esau was coming, and with him were four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two female servants.

rows.spanish: Y dijo: «¿Qué quieres decir con todo este campamento que encontré?» Y dijo: «Para hallar favor a los ojos de mi señor.»
rows.current_english_pob: And he said, “What do you mean by all this camp that I met?” And he said, “To find favor in the eyes of my lord.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said, “What do you mean by all this camp that I met?” And he said, “To find favor in the eyes of my lord.”

rows.spanish: Jacob dijo: «No, por favor. Si he hallado favor en tus ojos, toma mi regalo de mi mano, porque ver tu rostro es como ver el rostro de Dios, y me has recibido favorablemente».
rows.current_english_pob: Jacob said, “No, please. If I have found favor in your eyes, then take my gift from my hand, because seeing your face is like seeing the face of God, and you have received me favorably.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Jacob said, “No, please. If I have found favor in your eyes, then take my gift from my hand, for therefore I have seen your face as one sees the face of God, and you have been pleased with me.”

rows.spanish: Por favor, toma mi bendición que te ha sido traída, porque Dios me ha mostrado favor, y porque tengo todo. Jacob insistió con él, y Esaú la tomó.
rows.current_english_pob: Please take my gift that has been brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have everything. And he urged him, and he took it.
rows.spanish_base_english: Please take my blessing that has been brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have everything. And he urged him, and he took it.

rows.spanish: Entonces Esaú dijo: «Por favor, permíteme dejar contigo a algunos de los hombres que están conmigo». Pero él dijo: «¿Para qué esto? Que halle favor ante los ojos de mi señor».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Esau said, “Please let me leave with you some of the people who are with me.” But he said, “Why is this? Let me find favor in the eyes of my lord.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Esau said, “Please let me leave with you some of the people who are with me.” But he said, “Why this? Let me find favor in the sight of my lord.”

rows.spanish: Dina, la hija de Lea, que ella le había dado a luz a Jacob, salió para ver a las hijas de la tierra.
rows.current_english_pob: Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.

rows.spanish: Y Siquem dijo a Hamor, su padre: «Consígueme a esta muchacha como esposa».
rows.current_english_pob: And Shechem said to Hamor his father, “Get me this girl as a wife.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Shechem said to Hamor his father, “Take this girl for me as a wife.”

rows.spanish: Y Jacob oyó que había mancillado a su hija Dina. Pero sus hijos estaban con su ganado en el campo, y Jacob guardó silencio hasta que ellos llegaron.
rows.current_english_pob: Jacob heard that he had defiled his daughter Dinah. But his sons were with his livestock in the field, so Jacob kept silent until they came.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Jacob heard that he had defiled his daughter Dinah. But his sons were with his livestock in the field, so Jacob kept silent until they came.

rows.spanish: Cuando los hijos de Jacob regresaron del campo y lo oyeron, se entristecieron y se indignaron mucho, porque Siquem había cometido un acto infame en Israel al acostarse con la hija de Jacob; algo así no debía hacerse.
rows.current_english_pob: And Jacob’s sons came in from the field when they heard it, and the men were grieved and very angry, because he had done an outrageous thing in Israel by lying with Jacob’s daughter, for such a thing must not be done.
rows.spanish_base_english: And Jacob’s sons came in from the field when they heard it, and the men were grieved and very angry, because he had done a disgraceful thing in Israel by lying with Jacob’s daughter, and such a thing should not be done.

rows.spanish: Estos hombres están en paz con nosotros. Que habiten en la tierra y comercien en ella, porque, como ven, la tierra es suficientemente amplia para ellos. Tomaremos a sus hijas por esposas y les daremos nuestras hijas.
rows.current_english_pob: These men are at peace with us. Let them dwell in the land and trade in it, for, you see, the land is broad enough for them. We will take their daughters for wives for ourselves, and we will give our daughters to them.
rows.spanish_base_english: These men are at peace with us. Let them dwell in the land and trade in it, for behold, the land is wide enough before them. We will take their daughters for ourselves as wives, and we will give our daughters to them.

rows.spanish: Al tercer día, mientras estaban con dolor, dos de los hijos de Jacob, Simeón y Leví, hermanos de Dina, cada uno tomó su espada; cayeron sobre la ciudad sin sospecharlo, y mataron a todo varón.
rows.current_english_pob: On the third day, while they were in pain, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword, came against the city while it felt secure, and killed every male.
rows.spanish_base_english: On the third day, while they were in pain, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword, came upon the city unsuspecting, and killed every male.

rows.spanish: Y Dios le dijo: «Tu nombre es Jacob. Tu nombre ya no será llamado Jacob, sino Israel será tu nombre». Y lo llamó Israel.
rows.current_english_pob: And God said to him, “Your name is Jacob. Your name will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel will be your name.” So he called his name Israel.
rows.spanish_base_english: And God said to him, “Your name is Jacob. Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name.” And he called his name Israel.

rows.spanish: Y aconteció, mientras Israel habitaba en aquella tierra, que Rubén fue y se acostó con Bilha, concubina de su padre, e Israel se enteró. Ahora bien, los hijos de Jacob eran doce.
rows.current_english_pob: And it happened, while Israel was dwelling in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and Israel heard of it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve.
rows.spanish_base_english: And it happened, while Israel was dwelling in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and Israel heard of it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, estas son las generaciones de Esaú —es decir, Edom—.
rows.current_english_pob: These are the generations of Esau (that is, Edom).
rows.spanish_base_english: Now these are the generations of Esau (that is, Edom).

rows.spanish: Y Esaú tomó a sus esposas, a sus hijos, a sus hijas, y a todas las personas de su casa, junto con su ganado, todos sus animales y todas sus posesiones que había adquirido en la tierra de Canaán, y se fue a una tierra lejos de su hermano Jacob.
rows.current_english_pob: And Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, and all the persons of his household, along with his livestock, all his animals, and all his possessions that he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and went to a land because of his brother Jacob.
rows.spanish_base_english: And Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, and all the persons of his household, along with his livestock, all his animals, and all his possessions that he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and went to a land away from his brother Jacob.

rows.spanish: Jeque Koraj, jeque Gatam, jeque Amalec—estos son los jeques de Elifaz en la tierra de Edom; estos son los hijos de Adá.
rows.current_english_pob: Chief Korah, chief Gaatham, chief Amalek—these are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah.
rows.spanish_base_english: Chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek—these are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah.

rows.spanish: Y estos eran los hijos de Anah: Dishón y Oholibamá, hija de Anah.
rows.current_english_pob: And these were the sons of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah daughter of Anah.
rows.spanish_base_english: And these were the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah daughter of Anah.

rows.spanish: Estos son los hijos de Ezer: Bilhan, Zaaván y Akan.
rows.current_english_pob: These are the sons of Etser: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
rows.spanish_base_english: These are the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.

rows.spanish: Ahora Jacob habitó en la tierra donde su padre había vivido como forastero, en la tierra de Canaán.
rows.current_english_pob: Jacob lived in the land of his father's sojournings, in the land of Canaan.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Jacob lived in the land of his father's sojournings, in the land of Canaan.

rows.spanish: Israel amó a José más que a todos sus hijos, porque era el hijo de su vejez; y le hizo una túnica ricamente ornamentada.
rows.current_english_pob: Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was the son of his old age; and he made for him a richly ornamented robe.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was the son of his old age; and he made for him a richly ornamented robe.

rows.spanish: Entonces José tuvo un sueño, y se lo contó a sus hermanos, y ellos lo odiaron todavía más.
rows.current_english_pob: Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brothers, and they hated him even more.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brothers, and they hated him even more.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, nosotros estábamos atando gavillas en medio del campo; y he aquí, mi gavilla se levantó y además quedó en pie; y he aquí, sus gavillas se juntaron alrededor y se inclinaron ante mi gavilla.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, we were binding sheaves in the midst of the field, and behold, my sheaf rose and also stood upright; and behold, your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to my sheaf.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, we were binding sheaves in the midst of the field, and behold, my sheaf rose and also stood upright; and behold, your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to my sheaf.

rows.spanish: Sus hermanos le dijeron: «¿De veras reinarás sobre nosotros? ¿De veras gobernarás sobre nosotros?» Y lo odiaron aún más por causa de sus sueños y por causa de sus palabras.
rows.current_english_pob: His brothers said to him, “Will you really reign over us? Will you really rule over us?” So they hated him even more because of his dreams and because of his words.
rows.spanish_base_english: His brothers said to him, “Will you indeed reign over us? Will you indeed rule over us?” So they hated him even more because of his dreams and because of his words.

rows.spanish: Ahora sus hermanos fueron a pastorear el rebaño de su padre en Siquem.
rows.current_english_pob: His brothers went to pasture their father's flock at Shechem.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now his brothers went to pasture their father's flock at Shechem.

rows.spanish: Entonces Israel dijo a José: «¿No están tus hermanos pastoreando en Siquem? Ven, y te enviaré a ellos». Y él le dijo: «Aquí estoy».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Are not your brothers shepherding at Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them.” And he said to him, “Here I am.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Are not your brothers shepherding at Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them.” And he said to him, “Here I am.”

rows.spanish: Entonces se sentaron a comer pan, y alzaron sus ojos y miraron; y he aquí, una caravana de ismaelitas venía de Galaad, con sus camellos cargados de goma aromática, bálsamo y ládano, y ellos iban a llevarlo a Egipto.
rows.current_english_pob: Then they sat down to eat bread, and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and behold, a caravan of Ishmaelites was coming from Gilead, with their camels carrying gum, balm, and myrrh, on their way to take it down to Egypt.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then they sat down to eat bread, and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and behold, a caravan of Ishmaelites was coming from Gilead, with their camels carrying gum, balm, and ladanum, going to take it down to Egypt.

rows.spanish: La reconoció y dijo: «Es la túnica de mi hijo. Un animal salvaje lo ha devorado. Yosef ciertamente ha sido despedazado.»
rows.current_english_pob: He recognized it and said, “It is my son’s tunic. A wild animal has devoured him. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces.”
rows.spanish_base_english: He recognized it and said, “It is my son’s tunic. A wild animal has devoured him. Yosef has surely been torn to pieces.”

rows.spanish: Er, el primogénito de Judá, era malvado a los ojos de Yahvé, y Yahvé lo hizo morir.
rows.current_english_pob: Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil in the sight of Yahweh, and Yahweh put him to death.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil in the sight of Yahweh, and Yahweh put him to death.

rows.spanish: Entonces ella se quitó sus vestidos de viudez, se envolvió en un velo y se sentó a la entrada de Enaim, que está en el camino a Timnat. Pues vio que Selá había crecido, pero no le había sido dada por esposa.
rows.current_english_pob: So she took off her widow’s garments from herself, and wrapped herself in a veil, and sat at the entrance to Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah. For she saw that Shelah had grown up, yet she had not been given to him as a wife.
rows.spanish_base_english: So she took off her widow’s garments, covered herself with a veil, wrapped herself up, and sat at the entrance of Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah. For she saw that Shelah had grown up, yet she had not been given to him as a wife.

rows.spanish: Entonces se apartó hacia ella, junto al camino, y dijo: «Por favor, déjame llegarme a ti», pues no sabía que ella era su nuera. Y ella dijo: «¿Qué me darás, para que te llegues a mí?»
rows.current_english_pob: So he turned aside to her by the road and said, “Please, let me come in to you,” for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, “What will you give me, that you may come in to me?”
rows.spanish_base_english: So he turned aside to her by the road and said, “Please, let me come in to you,” for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, “What will you give me, that you may come in to me?”

rows.spanish: Y él dijo: «Yo enviaré un cabrito del rebaño». Y ella dijo: «Si das una prenda hasta que lo envíes».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said, “I will send a young goat from the flock.” And she said, “If you will give a pledge until you send it.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said, “I will send a young goat from the flock.” And she said, “If you will give a pledge until you send it.”

rows.spanish: Él dijo: «¿Qué prenda te daré?». Y ella dijo: «Tu sello, tu cordón y tu vara que está en tu mano». Entonces se los dio, se llegó a ella y ella quedó encinta de él.
rows.current_english_pob: He said, “What pledge shall I give you?” And she said, “Your seal, your cord, and your staff that is in your hand.” So he gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
rows.spanish_base_english: He said, “What pledge shall I give you?” And she said, “Your seal, your cord, and your staff that is in your hand.” So he gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, cuando era tiempo de dar a luz, he aquí que había gemelos en su vientre.
rows.current_english_pob: When it was time for her to give birth, behold, there were twins in her womb.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when it was time for her to give birth, behold, there were twins in her womb.

rows.spanish: Y José había sido llevado a Egipto, y Potifar, oficial de Faraón, capitán de la guardia, un egipcio, lo compró a los ismaelitas que lo habían llevado allá.
rows.current_english_pob: Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.

rows.spanish: Y después de estas cosas, la esposa de su amo puso sus ojos en Yosef y dijo: «Acuéstate conmigo».
rows.current_english_pob: And after these things, his master's wife cast her eyes on Joseph and said, “Lie with me.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And after these things, his master's wife cast her eyes on Yosef and said, “Lie with me.”

rows.spanish: Y sucedió que, como ella le hablaba a Yosef día tras día, él no le hizo caso, para acostarse junto a ella ni para estar con ella.
rows.current_english_pob: And it happened, as she spoke to Joseph day after day, that he did not listen to her, to lie beside her or to be with her.
rows.spanish_base_english: And it happened, as she spoke to Yosef day after day, that he did not listen to her, to lie beside her or to be with her.

rows.spanish: Entonces guardó su prenda junto a ella, hasta que su amo vino a su casa.
rows.current_english_pob: So she kept his garment beside her until his master came home.
rows.spanish_base_english: So she kept his garment beside her until his master came into his house.

rows.spanish: Entonces ella le habló con palabras como estas, diciendo: «El esclavo hebreo que nos trajiste vino a mí para burlarse de mí».
rows.current_english_pob: Then she spoke to him with words like these, saying, “The Hebrew servant whom you brought to us came to me to mock me.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then she spoke to him with words like these, saying, “The Hebrew slave whom you brought to us came to me to mock me.”

rows.spanish: Sucedió que, cuando su amo oyó las palabras que su esposa le dijo, diciendo: «Según estas palabras me hizo a mí tu esclavo», se encendió su ira.
rows.current_english_pob: And it happened that when his master heard the words of his wife that she spoke to him, saying, “According to these words your servant did to me,” his anger burned.
rows.spanish_base_english: And it happened that when his master heard the words of his wife that she spoke to him, saying, “According to these words your slave did to me,” his anger burned.

rows.spanish: Pero Yahvé estaba con José, le mostró fidelidad al pacto y le concedió favor ante el jefe de la cárcel.
rows.current_english_pob: But Yahweh was with Joseph and extended covenant faithfulness to him, and he gave him favor in the eyes of the chief of the prison.
rows.spanish_base_english: But Yahweh was with Joseph and showed him steadfast love, and he gave him favor in the eyes of the chief of the prison.

rows.spanish: Y el jefe de la cárcel puso en la mano de Yosef a todos los presos que estaban en la cárcel, y todo lo que allí se hacía, él era quien lo hacía.
rows.current_english_pob: And the chief of the prison put into Joseph’s hand all the prisoners who were in the prison, and whatever was done there, he was the one doing it.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the chief of the prison put into Yosef’s hand all the prisoners who were in the prison, and whatever was done there, he was the one doing it.

rows.spanish: Entonces el capitán de la guardia designó a José para atenderlos, y les sirvió; y estuvieron en custodia por algún tiempo.
rows.current_english_pob: So the captain of the guard assigned Joseph to them, and he attended them; and they were in custody for some time.
rows.spanish_base_english: So the captain of the guard appointed Joseph to attend them, and he served them; and they were in custody for some time.

rows.spanish: José vino a ellos por la mañana y los vio, y he aquí, estaban afligidos.
rows.current_english_pob: Joseph came to them in the morning and saw them, and behold, they were troubled.
rows.spanish_base_english: Joseph came to them in the morning and saw them, and behold, they were troubled.

rows.spanish: Entonces el jefe de los coperos contó su sueño a José y le dijo: «En mi sueño, he aquí, había una vid delante de mí».
rows.current_english_pob: So the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph and said to him, “In my dream, behold, a vine was before me.”
rows.spanish_base_english: So the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph and said to him, “In my dream, behold, a vine was before me.”

rows.spanish: Ahora la copa de Faraón estaba en mi mano, y tomé las uvas y las exprimí en la copa de Faraón, y puse la copa en la mano de Faraón.
rows.current_english_pob: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes and squeezed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I placed the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes and squeezed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I placed the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.

rows.spanish: Cuando el panadero principal vio que había interpretado bien, le dijo a Yosef: «Yo también tuve un sueño, y he aquí que tres canastas de pan blanco estaban sobre mi cabeza».
rows.current_english_pob: When the chief baker saw that he had interpreted well, he said to Yoseph, “I also had a dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.”
rows.spanish_base_english: When the chief baker saw that he had interpreted well, he said to Yoseph, “I also had a dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.”

rows.spanish: Al cabo de dos años completos, el faraón soñó, y he aquí que estaba de pie junto al Nilo.
rows.current_english_pob: At the end of two full years, Pharaoh dreamed, and behold, he was standing by the Nile.
rows.spanish_base_english: At the end of two full years, Pharaoh dreamed, and behold, he was standing by the Nile.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, siete vacas subían del Nilo, hermosas en apariencia y gordas de carne, y pastaban entre los juncos.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, seven cows were coming up from the Nile, beautiful in appearance and fat in flesh, and they were grazing in the reed grass.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, seven cows were coming up from the Nile, beautiful in appearance and fat in flesh, and they were grazing in the reed grass.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, otras siete vacas subían detrás de ellas desde el Nilo, feas de aspecto y delgadas de carne, y se pararon junto a las vacas a la orilla del Nilo.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, seven other cows came up after them from the Nile, ugly in appearance and thin in flesh, and they stood beside the cows on the bank of the Nile.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, seven other cows came up after them from the Nile, ugly in appearance and thin in flesh, and they stood beside the cows on the bank of the Nile.

rows.spanish: Entonces durmió y soñó por segunda vez; y he aquí, siete espigas subían en un solo tallo, llenas y buenas.
rows.current_english_pob: Then he slept and dreamed a second time, and behold, seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, plump and good.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then he slept and dreamed a second time, and behold, seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, plump and good.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, siete espigas delgadas, abrasadas por el viento del oriente, brotaban tras ellas.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, seven thin ears of grain, scorched by the east wind, were sprouting up after them.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, seven thin ears of grain, scorched by the east wind, were sprouting up after them.

rows.spanish: Y las espigas delgadas se tragaron las siete espigas sanas y llenas. Entonces Faraón despertó, y he aquí, era un sueño.
rows.current_english_pob: And the thin ears swallowed up the seven healthy and full ears. Then Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the thin ears swallowed up the seven healthy and full ears. Then Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.

rows.spanish: Y allí con nosotros estaba un joven hebreo, esclavo del capitán de la guardia; le contamos nuestros sueños, y nos interpretó los sueños; a cada uno le interpretó según su sueño.
rows.current_english_pob: And there with us was a young Hebrew man, a servant of the captain of the guard, and we told him, and he interpreted our dreams for us; he interpreted each man's dream according to his dream.
rows.spanish_base_english: And there with us was a young Hebrew man, a slave of the captain of the guard, and we told him, and he interpreted our dreams for us; he interpreted each man's dream according to his dream.

rows.spanish: Y el faraón dijo a José: «He tenido un sueño y no hay quien lo interprete. Pero he oído decir de ti que, cuando oyes un sueño, puedes interpretarlo».
rows.current_english_pob: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it. But I have heard it said about you that when you hear a dream, you can interpret it.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it. But I have heard about you, saying, ‘You hear a dream to interpret it.’”

rows.spanish: Entonces el faraón le dijo a José: «En mi sueño, he aquí, yo estaba de pie en la orilla del Nilo».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “In my dream, behold, I was standing on the bank of the Nile.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “In my dream, behold, I was standing on the bank of the Nile.”

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, siete vacas subían del Nilo, saludables de cuerpo y hermosas de figura, y pastaban entre los juncos.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, seven cows were coming up from the Nile, healthy in flesh and beautiful in form, and they grazed in the reeds.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, seven cows were coming up from the Nile, healthy in flesh and beautiful in form, and they grazed in the reeds.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, siete otras vacas subieron tras ellas, flacas y muy feas de aspecto, y delgadas de carne. Nunca había visto otras semejantes a ellas en toda la tierra de Egipto, por su fealdad.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, seven other cows came up after them, poor and very ugly in appearance and thin in flesh. I had not seen any like them in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, seven other cows came up after them, poor and very ugly in appearance and thin in flesh. I had not seen any like them in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.

rows.spanish: Y vi en mi sueño, y he aquí, siete espigas subían en un solo tallo, llenas y buenas.
rows.current_english_pob: And I saw in my dream, and behold, seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, full and good.
rows.spanish_base_english: And I saw in my dream, and behold, seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, full and good.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, siete espigas, marchitas, delgadas y quemadas por el viento del oriente, brotaban después de ellas.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, seven ears, thin and scorched by the east wind, were sprouting after them.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, seven ears, thin and scorched by the east wind, were sprouting after them.

rows.spanish: Y ese alimento será una reserva para la tierra, para los siete años de hambre que habrá en la tierra de Egipto, para que la tierra no perezca por el hambre.
rows.current_english_pob: That food shall be a reserve for the land for the seven years of famine that will be in the land of Egypt, so that the land may not be cut off by the famine.
rows.spanish_base_english: That food shall be a reserve for the land for the seven years of famine that will be in the land of Egypt, so that the land may not perish through the famine.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, José tenía treinta años cuando estuvo ante Faraón, rey de Egipto. Y José salió de la presencia de Faraón y pasó por toda la tierra de Egipto.
rows.current_english_pob: Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from before Pharaoh and traveled through all the land of Egypt.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from before Pharaoh and traveled through all the land of Egypt.

rows.spanish: José era el gobernante del país; él era quien vendía grano a toda la gente del país. Cuando llegaron los hermanos de José, se inclinaron ante él, con el rostro en tierra.
rows.current_english_pob: Joseph was the ruler over the land; he was the one who sold grain to all the people of the land. And Joseph’s brothers came and bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Joseph was the ruler over the land; he was the one who sold grain to all the people of the land. And Joseph’s brothers came and bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.

rows.spanish: Cuando José vio a sus hermanos, los reconoció, pero se hizo pasar por un extraño ante ellos y les habló con dureza. Les dijo: «¿De dónde han venido?». Ellos respondieron: «De la tierra de Canaán, para comprar alimento».
rows.current_english_pob: When Joseph saw his brothers, he recognized them, but he acted like a stranger toward them and spoke harshly with them. He said to them, “Where have you come from?” And they said, “From the land of Canaan, to buy food.”
rows.spanish_base_english: When Joseph saw his brothers, he recognized them, but he disguised himself to them and spoke harshly to them. He said to them, “Where have you come from?” And they said, “From the land of Canaan, to buy food.”

rows.spanish: Y dijeron: “Nosotros, tus siervos, somos doce hermanos, hijos de un solo hombre en la tierra de Canaán. Y he aquí, el menor está hoy con nuestro padre, y uno ya no está.”
rows.current_english_pob: And they said, “We, your servants, are twelve brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan. And behold, the youngest is with our father today, and one is no more.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And they said, “We, your servants, are twelve brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan. And behold, the youngest is with our father today, and one is no more.”

rows.spanish: Entonces Rubén les respondió, diciendo: «¿No les dije yo, diciendo: “No pequen contra el muchacho”? Pero ustedes no escucharon. Y ahora, he aquí, su sangre está siendo requerida».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Reuben answered them, saying, “Did I not tell you, ‘Do not sin against the boy’? But you did not listen. And now, look, his blood is being required.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Reuben answered them, saying, “Did I not tell you, saying, ‘Do not sin against the boy’? But you did not listen. And now, behold, his blood is being required.”

rows.spanish: Entonces uno de ellos abrió su saco para dar forraje a su asno en el lugar donde se alojaban, y vio su plata, y he aquí, allí estaba en la boca de su bolsa.
rows.current_english_pob: Then one of them opened his sack to give fodder to his donkey at the lodging place, and he saw his silver—and behold, it was in the mouth of his bag.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then one of them opened his sack to give fodder to his donkey at the lodging place, and he saw his silver—and behold, it was in the mouth of his bag.

rows.spanish: El hombre, el señor de la tierra, nos habló duramente y nos trató como espías del país.
rows.current_english_pob: The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly with us and treated us as spies of the land.
rows.spanish_base_english: The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly to us and treated us as spies of the land.

rows.spanish: Y mientras vaciaban sus sacos, he aquí, el atado de plata de cada uno estaba en su saco; y vieron sus atados de plata, ellos y su padre, y tuvieron miedo.
rows.current_english_pob: And as they were emptying their sacks, behold, each man’s bundle of silver was in his sack; and they saw their bundles of silver, they and their father, and they were afraid.
rows.spanish_base_english: And as they were emptying their sacks, behold, each man’s bundle of silver was in his sack; and they saw their bundles of silver, they and their father, and they were afraid.

rows.spanish: Y la hambruna era severa en el país.
rows.current_english_pob: The famine was severe in the land.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the famine was severe in the land.

rows.spanish: Ellos dijeron: “El hombre nos preguntó con insistencia acerca de nosotros mismos y de nuestra familia, diciendo: ‘¿Sigue vivo su padre? ¿Tienen ustedes otro hermano?’ Así le dijimos conforme a estas palabras. ¿Acaso podíamos saber que él diría: ‘Hagan bajar a su hermano’?”
rows.current_english_pob: They said, “The man questioned us closely about us and about our family, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?’ So we told him according to these words. How could we possibly know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother down’?”
rows.spanish_base_english: They said, “The man questioned us closely about ourselves and our family, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?’ So we told him according to these words. Could we possibly know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother down’?”

rows.spanish: Los hombres tuvieron miedo porque habían sido llevados a la casa de José, y dijeron: «Es por el dinero que fue devuelto en nuestros sacos la primera vez que nos están haciendo entrar, para que él busque un pretexto contra nosotros, caiga sobre nosotros, y nos tome como esclavos, junto con nuestros asnos».
rows.current_english_pob: The men were afraid because they had been brought into Joseph’s house, and they said, “It is because of the money that was returned in our sacks the first time that we are being brought in, so that he may make a pretext against us and fall upon us and take us as servants, along with our donkeys.”
rows.spanish_base_english: The men were afraid because they had been brought into Joseph’s house, and they said, “It is because of the money that was returned in our sacks the first time that we are being brought in, so that he may make a pretext against us and fall upon us and take us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”

rows.spanish: Y cuando llegamos al lugar de hospedaje y abrimos nuestros costales, he aquí, la plata de cada uno estaba en la boca de su costal: nuestra plata, con su peso completo; y la devolvimos en nuestras manos.
rows.current_english_pob: And when we came to the lodging place and opened our sacks, behold, each man's silver was in the mouth of his sack—our silver in its full weight—and we brought it back in our hand.
rows.spanish_base_english: And when we came to the lodging place and opened our sacks, behold, each man's silver was in the mouth of his sack—our silver in its full weight—and we brought it back in our hand.

rows.spanish: Y prepararon el regalo hasta que llegó Yosef al mediodía, porque habían oído que allí comerían pan.
rows.current_english_pob: And they prepared the gift until Joseph came at noon, because they had heard that they would eat bread there.
rows.spanish_base_english: And they prepared the gift until Yosef came at noon, because they had heard that they would eat bread there.

rows.spanish: Les preguntó por su bienestar y dijo: «¿Está bien su padre anciano, de quien hablaron? ¿Todavía vive?»
rows.current_english_pob: He asked them about their well-being and said, “Is your elderly father, whom you spoke of, well? Is he still alive?”
rows.spanish_base_english: He asked them about their welfare and said, “Is your aged father, of whom you spoke, well? Is he still alive?”

rows.spanish: Alzó la vista y vio a Benjamín, su hermano, hijo de su madre, y dijo: «¿Es este su hermano menor, del que me hablaron?» Luego dijo: «Dios te muestre gracia, hijo mío».
rows.current_english_pob: He lifted up his eyes and saw Benjamin, his brother, his mother's son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” Then he said, “May God be gracious to you, my son.”
rows.spanish_base_english: He lifted up his eyes and saw Benjamin, his brother, his mother's son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” Then he said, “May God be gracious to you, my son.”

rows.spanish: Cualquiera de tus siervos con quien se encuentre, que muera; y nosotros también seremos esclavos de mi señor.
rows.current_english_pob: Whichever of your servants it is found with, let him die, and we also will become servants to my lord.
rows.spanish_base_english: Whichever of your servants it is found with, let him die, and we also will become slaves to my lord.

rows.spanish: Y él dijo: «Incluso ahora, sea conforme a sus palabras. El que sea hallado con ella será mi esclavo, y ustedes quedarán inocentes».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said, “Even now, let it be according to your words. The one with whom it is found will be my servant, and you will be innocent.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said, “Even now, let it be according to your words. The one with whom it is found will be my slave, and you will be innocent.”

rows.spanish: Y Judá dijo: «¿Qué diremos a mi señor? ¿Qué hablaremos? ¿O cómo nos justificaremos? Dios ha hallado la culpa de tus siervos. Aquí estamos, esclavos de mi señor, tanto nosotros como aquel en cuya mano fue hallada la copa».
rows.current_english_pob: And Judah said, “What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak? Or how shall we justify ourselves? God has found out the guilt of your servants. Here we are, my lord’s servants, both we and the one in whose hand the cup was found.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Judah said, “What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak? Or how shall we justify ourselves? God has found out the guilt of your slaves. Here we are, my lord’s slaves, both we and the one in whose hand the cup was found.”

rows.spanish: Pero él dijo: «¡Lejos de mí hacer esto! El hombre en cuya mano fue hallada la copa será mi esclavo, pero ustedes pueden subir en paz a su padre».
rows.current_english_pob: But he said, "Far be it from me to do this. The man in whose hand the cup was found—he shall be my servant, but you may go up in peace to your father."
rows.spanish_base_english: But he said, "Far be it from me to do this. The man in whose hand the cup was found—he shall be my slave, but you may go up in peace to your father."

rows.spanish: Uno salió de mí, y yo dije: «Ciertamente ha sido despedazado», y no lo he visto hasta ahora.
rows.current_english_pob: One left me, and I said, ‘Surely he has been torn to pieces,’ and I have not seen him until now.
rows.spanish_base_english: The one went out from me, and I said, ‘Surely he has been torn to pieces,’ and I have not seen him until now.

rows.spanish: Y ahora, por favor, deja que tu siervo permanezca en lugar del muchacho como esclavo de mi señor, y que el muchacho suba con sus hermanos.
rows.current_english_pob: So now, please let your servant remain instead of the boy as a servant to my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers.
rows.spanish_base_english: So now, please let your servant remain instead of the boy as a slave to my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers.

rows.spanish: Porque, ¿cómo volveré a mi padre si el muchacho no está conmigo? No sea que vea la desgracia que vendría sobre mi padre.
rows.current_english_pob: For how can I go up to my father if the boy is not with me? Otherwise, I would have to see the disaster that would come upon my father.
rows.spanish_base_english: For how can I go up to my father if the boy is not with me? Lest I see the disaster that would come upon my father.

rows.spanish: Entonces José dijo a sus hermanos: «Acérquense a mí, por favor». Y ellos se acercaron. Entonces dijo: «Yo soy José, el hermano de ustedes, a quien ustedes vendieron a Egipto».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Please come near to me.” And they came near. Then he said, “I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Please come near to me.” And they came near. Then he said, “I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.”

rows.spanish: Allí te proveeré, pues aún quedan cinco años de hambre, para que no queden en la miseria tú, tu casa y todo lo que te pertenece.
rows.current_english_pob: There I will provide for you, because there are still five years of famine, lest you and your household and all that belongs to you become destitute.
rows.spanish_base_english: There I will provide for you, for there are still five years of famine, lest you and your household and all that belongs to you become destitute.

rows.spanish: Y cuéntenle a mi padre toda mi gloria en Egipto y todo lo que han visto. Apresúrense y traigan aquí a mi padre.
rows.current_english_pob: And tell my father about all my honor in Egypt and everything you have seen. Hurry and bring my father down here.
rows.spanish_base_english: And tell my father about all my glory in Egypt and all that you have seen. Hurry and bring my father down here.

rows.spanish: Y le contaron todas las palabras que Yosef les había dicho, y él vio las carretas que Yosef había enviado para llevarlo, y el espíritu de su padre Yaakov revivió.
rows.current_english_pob: And they told him all the words of Joseph that he had spoken to them, and he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him, and the spirit of their father Jacob revived.
rows.spanish_base_english: And they told him all the words of Yosef that he had spoken to them, and he saw the wagons that Yosef had sent to carry him, and the spirit of their father Yaakov revived.

rows.spanish: Y Dios habló a Israel en visiones de la noche, y dijo: «Jacob, Jacob». Y él dijo: «Aquí estoy».
rows.current_english_pob: And God spoke to Israel in visions of the night and said, “Jacob, Jacob.” And he said, “Here I am.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And God spoke to Israel in visions of the night and said, “Jacob, Jacob.” And he said, “Here I am.”

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, estos son los nombres de los hijos de Israel que vinieron a Egipto: Jacob y sus hijos. El primogénito de Jacob fue Rubén.
rows.current_english_pob: These are the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt: Jacob and his sons. Jacob’s firstborn was Reuben.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt: Jacob and his sons. Jacob’s firstborn was Reuben.

rows.spanish: Entonces Israel dijo a José: «Ahora déjame morir, porque he visto tu rostro y que todavía estás vivo».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Now I can die, since I have seen your face and know that you are still alive.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Now let me die, since I have seen your face, that you are still alive.”

rows.spanish: Entonces dirán: «Tus siervos han sido cuidadores de ganado desde nuestra juventud hasta ahora, tanto nosotros como nuestros padres, para que habiten en la tierra de Gosén, porque todo pastor es detestable para los egipcios».
rows.current_english_pob: then you shall say, ‘Your servants have been men of livestock from our youth until now, both we and our fathers,’ so that you may live in the land of Goshen, for every shepherd is detestable to the Egyptians.
rows.spanish_base_english: then you shall say, ‘Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth until now, both we and our fathers,’ so that you may dwell in the land of Goshen, for every shepherd is detestable to the Egyptians.

rows.spanish: Ahora no había alimento en toda la tierra, porque la hambruna era muy severa; y la tierra de Egipto y la tierra de Canaán languidecían a causa de la hambruna.
rows.current_english_pob: There was no food in all the land, because the famine was very severe; and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished because of the famine.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now there was no food in all the land, because the famine was very severe; and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished because of the famine.

rows.spanish: ¿Por qué habríamos de morir delante de tus ojos, tanto nosotros como nuestra tierra? Cómpranos, a nosotros y a nuestra tierra, por pan, y nosotros y nuestra tierra seremos esclavos de Faraón. Da semilla, para que vivamos y no muramos, y la tierra no quede desolada.
rows.current_english_pob: Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh. Give seed, so that we may live and not die, and the land may not become desolate.
rows.spanish_base_english: Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be slaves to Pharaoh. Give seed, so that we may live and not die, and the land may not become desolate.

rows.spanish: Y en la cosecha, darán una quinta parte a Faraón, y cuatro partes serán para ustedes: para semilla para el campo, para su alimento, para los que están en sus casas, y para alimento de sus pequeños.
rows.current_english_pob: And at the harvest, you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four-fifths shall be yours for seed for the field, for your food, for those in your households, and for food for your little ones.
rows.spanish_base_english: And at the harvest, you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts shall be yours for seed of the field, for your food, for those in your households, and for food for your little ones.

rows.spanish: Y dijeron: «Tú nos has mantenido con vida. Que hallemos favor ante los ojos de mi señor, y seremos esclavos de Faraón».
rows.current_english_pob: And they said, “You have kept us alive. May we find favor in the eyes of my lord, and we will be servants to Pharaoh.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And they said, “You have kept us alive. May we find favor in the eyes of my lord, and we will be slaves to Pharaoh.”

rows.spanish: Así, José lo estableció como estatuto hasta hoy sobre la tierra de Egipto: una quinta parte pertenece a Faraón. Solo la tierra de los sacerdotes no llegó a ser de Faraón.
rows.current_english_pob: So Joseph made it a statute that stands to this day concerning the land of Egypt: the fifth is for Pharaoh. Only the land of the priests alone did not become Pharaoh’s.
rows.spanish_base_english: So Joseph made it a statute to this day concerning the land of Egypt: a fifth belongs to Pharaoh. Only the land of the priests alone did not become Pharaoh’s.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, después de estas cosas, se le dijo a José: «Mira, tu padre está enfermo». Entonces tomó a sus dos hijos consigo, Manasés y Efraín.
rows.current_english_pob: After these things, it was said to Yoseph, “Look, your father is sick.” So he took his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now after these things, it was said to Yoseph, “Look, your father is sick.” So he took his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim.

rows.spanish: Y me dijo: «Mira, yo te haré fecundo y te multiplicaré, y te convertiré en una asamblea de pueblos, y daré esta tierra a tu descendencia después de ti como posesión perpetua».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said to me, ‘Look, I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make you into an assembly of peoples, and I will give this land to your offspring after you as an everlasting possession.’
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said to me, ‘Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make you into an assembly of peoples, and I will give this land to your offspring after you as an everlasting possession.’

rows.spanish: Y José dijo a su padre: «Estos son mis hijos, los que Dios me ha dado aquí». Y él dijo: «Por favor, tráemelos, y los bendeciré».
rows.current_english_pob: And Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom God has given me here.” And he said, “Please bring them to me, and I will bless them.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom God has given me here.” And he said, “Please bring them to me, and I will bless them.”

rows.spanish: Ahora los ojos de Israel estaban debilitados por la vejez; no podía ver. Entonces los acercó hacia sí, y los besó y los abrazó.
rows.current_english_pob: Israel’s eyes were dim with age; he could not see. So he brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Israel’s eyes were dim with age; he could not see. So he brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.

rows.spanish: Y José tomó a los dos: a Efraín en su mano derecha, al lado izquierdo de Israel, y a Manasés en su mano izquierda, al lado derecho de Israel, y los acercó a él.
rows.current_english_pob: And Joseph took the two of them—Ephraim in his right hand, at Israel’s left, and Manasseh in his left hand, at Israel’s right—and brought them near to him.
rows.spanish_base_english: And Joseph took the two of them—Ephraim in his right hand, from Israel’s left, and Manasseh in his left hand, from Israel’s right—and brought them near to him.

rows.spanish: Y bendijo a José y dijo: «El Dios delante de quien caminaron mis padres Abraham e Isaac, el Dios que ha sido mi pastor desde mi nacimiento hasta hoy»
rows.current_english_pob: And he blessed Joseph and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has shepherded me from my beginning to this day,”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he blessed Joseph and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has been my shepherd from my birth to this day,”

rows.spanish: Cuando José vio que su padre había puesto su mano derecha sobre la cabeza de Efraín, le desagradó, y sostuvo la mano de su padre para quitarla de la cabeza de Efraín y ponerla sobre la cabeza de Manasés.
rows.current_english_pob: When Joseph saw that his father had placed his right hand on Ephraim’s head, it was displeasing in his eyes, and he took hold of his father’s hand to remove it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.
rows.spanish_base_english: When Joseph saw that his father had placed his right hand on Ephraim’s head, it was displeasing in his sight, and he took hold of his father’s hand to remove it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.

rows.spanish: Entonces Israel dijo a José: «He aquí, estoy a punto de morir, pero Dios estará con ustedes y los hará volver a la tierra de sus padres».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I am about to die, but God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your fathers.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I am about to die, but God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your fathers.”

rows.spanish: Rubén, tú eres mi primogénito, mi fuerza y las primicias de mi vigor, sobresaliente en honor y sobresaliente en poder.
rows.current_english_pob: Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength and the firstfruits of my vigor, excelling in honor and excelling in power.
rows.spanish_base_english: Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength and the firstfruits of my vigor, preeminent in dignity and preeminent in power.

rows.spanish: Sin embargo, su arco permaneció firme, y los brazos de sus manos se volvieron ágiles por las manos del Poderoso de Jacob; de allí viene el Pastor, la Piedra de Israel.
rows.current_english_pob: Yet his bow remained steady, and his arms were made agile by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob; from there is the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel.
rows.spanish_base_english: Yet his bow remained firm, and the arms of his hands were made agile by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob; from there is the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel.

rows.spanish: Todas estas son las doce tribus de Israel, y esto es lo que su padre les dijo cuando los bendijo: a cada uno lo bendijo con la bendición que le correspondía.
rows.current_english_pob: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father spoke to them when he blessed them: he blessed each one with the blessing appropriate to him.
rows.spanish_base_english: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father said to them, and he blessed them; each according to his blessing he blessed them.

rows.spanish: Mi padre me hizo jurar, diciendo: «Mira, yo estoy muriendo. En mi sepulcro que cavé para mí en la tierra de Canaán, allí me sepultarás». Ahora, pues, te ruego que me permitas subir para sepultar a mi padre; luego volveré.
rows.current_english_pob: My father made me swear, saying, ‘Look, I am dying. In my grave that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me.’ So now, please let me go up and bury my father; then I will return.
rows.spanish_base_english: My father made me swear, saying, ‘Behold, I am dying. In my grave that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me.’ So now, please let me go up and bury my father; then I will return.

rows.spanish: También subieron con él carros y jinetes, y la comitiva llegó a ser muy grande.
rows.current_english_pob: Chariots and horsemen also went up with him, and the company became very large.
rows.spanish_base_english: Chariots and horsemen also went up with him, and the camp was very large.

rows.spanish: Cuando los habitantes de la tierra, los cananeos, vieron el duelo en la era de Atad, dijeron: «Este es un duelo muy grave para los egipcios». Por eso aquel lugar se llamó Abel-mizraim, el cual está al otro lado del Jordán.
rows.current_english_pob: When the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, “This is a grievous mourning for the Egyptians.” Therefore its name was called Abel-mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.
rows.spanish_base_english: When the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, “This is a grievous mourning for the Egyptians.” Therefore it was named Abel-mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.

rows.spanish: Cuando los hermanos de José vieron que su padre había muerto, dijeron: «Tal vez José nos odie y ciertamente nos pague todo el mal que le hicimos».
rows.current_english_pob: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “What if Joseph hates us and fully repays us for all the evil that we did to him?”
rows.spanish_base_english: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “Perhaps Joseph will hate us and surely repay us for all the evil that we did to him.”

rows.spanish: Esto es lo que le dirán a Yosef: “Por favor, perdona la transgresión de tus hermanos y su pecado, porque te pagaron con mal. Y ahora, por favor, perdona la transgresión de los siervos del Dios de tu padre”. Y Yosef lloró cuando le hablaron.
rows.current_english_pob: This is what you shall say to Joseph: ‘Please forgive the transgression of your brothers and their sin, because they repaid you with evil. And now, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father.’ And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
rows.spanish_base_english: This is what you shall say to Yosef: ‘Please forgive the transgression of your brothers and their sin, for they repaid you with evil. And now, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father.’ And Yosef wept when they spoke to him.

rows.spanish: Entonces sus hermanos también vinieron y se postraron delante de él y dijeron: «Aquí estamos, tus esclavos».
rows.current_english_pob: Then his brothers also came and fell down before him and said, “Here we are, your servants.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then his brothers also came and fell down before him and said, “Here we are, your slaves.”

rows.spanish: En cuanto a ustedes, ustedes intentaron hacerme mal contra mí, pero Dios lo tuvo pensado para bien, para hacer como en este día—mantener con vida a muchas personas.
rows.current_english_pob: As for you, you intended evil against me, but God intended it for good, in order to bring about what is happening this day—to keep many people alive.
rows.spanish_base_english: As for you, you intended evil against me, but God intended it for good, in order to do as it is this day—to keep many people alive.

rows.spanish: Entonces José hizo jurar a los hijos de Israel, diciendo: «Dios ciertamente los visitará, y ustedes harán subir mis huesos de aquí».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, “God will surely attend to you, and you must bring up my bones from here.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall bring up my bones from here.”

rows.spanish: habiendo llegado a ser tan superior a los ángeles como más excelente es el nombre que ha heredado que el suyo.
rows.current_english_pob: having become as much superior to the angels as the name he has inherited is more excellent than theirs.
rows.spanish_base_english: having become as much better than the angels as the name he has inherited is more excellent than theirs.

rows.spanish: ¿No son todos espíritus ministradores, enviados para servicio en favor de los que están por heredar la salvación?
rows.current_english_pob: Are they not all ministering spirits, being sent out for service for the sake of those who are about to inherit salvation?
rows.spanish_base_english: Are they not all ministering spirits sent out for service for the sake of those who are about to inherit salvation?

rows.spanish: mientras Dios también dio testimonio por medio de señales y prodigios y diversos milagros y repartos del Espíritu Santo, conforme a su voluntad.
rows.current_english_pob: while God also bore witness with signs and wonders and various miracles and distributions of the Holy Spirit according to his will.
rows.spanish_base_english: while God also bore witness by signs and wonders and various miracles and distributions of the Holy Spirit according to his will.

rows.spanish: Y de nuevo: «Yo confiaré en él». Y de nuevo: «He aquí, yo y los niños que Dios me ha dado».
rows.current_english_pob: And again, “I will put my trust in him.” And again, “Behold, I and the children whom God has given me.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And again, “I will put my trust in him.” And again, “Behold, I and the children whom God has given me.”

rows.spanish: Porque este ha sido considerado digno de más gloria que Moisés, en la medida en que el que construyó la casa tiene mayor honor que ella.
rows.current_english_pob: For this one has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, just as the one who built the house has greater honor than the house.
rows.spanish_base_english: For this one has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, insofar as the one who built the house has greater honor than it.

rows.spanish: Porque hemos llegado a ser partícipes del Mesías, si en verdad mantenemos firme hasta el fin el comienzo de nuestra confianza.
rows.current_english_pob: For we have become sharers in the Messiah, if indeed we hold the beginning of our assurance firm to the end.
rows.spanish_base_english: For we have become partakers of the Messiah, if indeed we hold firm to the end the beginning of our confidence.

rows.spanish: Porque no tenemos un sumo sacerdote que no pueda compadecerse de nuestras debilidades, sino uno que ha sido probado en todo, de la misma manera que nosotros, pero sin pecado.
rows.current_english_pob: For we do not have a high priest unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who has been tested in every way according to likeness, yet without sin.
rows.spanish_base_english: For we do not have a high priest unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who has been tested in every way as we are, yet without sin.

rows.spanish: Porque aunque ya deberían ser maestros a estas alturas, otra vez tienen necesidad de que alguien les enseñe los principios básicos del comienzo de los oráculos de Dios, y han llegado a tener necesidad de leche, no de alimento sólido.
rows.current_english_pob: For although by this time you ought to be teachers, you again need someone to teach you the basic elements of the beginning of the oracles of God, and you have come to need milk, not solid food.
rows.spanish_base_english: For although by this time you ought to be teachers, you again need someone to teach you the basic principles of the beginning of the oracles of God, and you have come to need milk, not solid food.

rows.spanish: Consideren ahora cuán grande era este hombre, a quien Abraham el patriarca dio la décima parte de los despojos.
rows.current_english_pob: Consider how great this man was, to whom Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth of the spoils.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now consider how great this man was, to whom Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth of the spoils.

rows.spanish: Y los que provienen de los hijos de Leví, los que reciben el sacerdocio, tienen el mandato, según la ley, de cobrar los diezmos del pueblo, es decir, de sus hermanos, aunque ellos también han salido de los lomos de Abraham.
rows.current_english_pob: And those from the sons of Levi who receive the priesthood have a commandment according to the law to collect a tenth from the people—that is, from their brothers—though they also have come from Abraham’s loins.
rows.spanish_base_english: And those from the sons of Levi who receive the priesthood have a command according to the law to collect a tenth from the people—that is, from their brothers—though they also have come from Abraham’s loins.

rows.spanish: Pero el que no es contado por genealogía de ellos ha recibido un diezmo de Abraham, y ha bendecido al que tiene las promesas.
rows.current_english_pob: But the one who is not traced by genealogy from them has taken a tenth from Abraham and has blessed the one who had the promises.
rows.spanish_base_english: But the one not traced by genealogy from them has taken a tenth from Abraham and has blessed the one who has the promises.

rows.spanish: Y, más allá de toda disputa, el menor recibe bendición del mayor.
rows.current_english_pob: Beyond all dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now beyond all dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.

rows.spanish: Y aquí reciben los diezmos hombres mortales, pero allí se da testimonio de que uno vive.
rows.current_english_pob: And here mortal men receive tithes, but there he is testified to be living.
rows.spanish_base_english: And here mortal men receive tithes, but there one receives them of whom it is testified that he lives.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, si la perfección hubiera sido por medio del sacerdocio levítico —porque sobre esa base el pueblo había recibido la ley—, ¿qué más necesidad había de que surgiera otro sacerdote según el orden de Melquisedec y no fuera llamado según el orden de Aarón?
rows.current_english_pob: If perfection had been through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people had received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek and not be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
rows.spanish_base_english: Now if perfection had been through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people had received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek and not be called according to the order of Aaron?

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, el punto principal de lo que se está diciendo es este: tenemos tal sumo sacerdote, que se sentó a la derecha del trono de la Majestad en los cielos,
rows.current_english_pob: The main point in what is being said is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the main point in what is being said is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,

rows.spanish: Porque todo sumo sacerdote es constituido para ofrecer tanto dones como sacrificios; por tanto, es necesario que este también tenga algo que ofrecer.
rows.current_english_pob: For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices; therefore it is necessary for this one also to have something that he may offer.
rows.spanish_base_english: For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices; therefore it is necessary for this one also to have something that he may offer.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, si él estuviera en la tierra, ni siquiera sería sacerdote, pues hay quienes ofrecen los dones conforme a la ley.
rows.current_english_pob: If he were on earth, he would not even be a priest, since there are those who offer the gifts according to the law.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now if he were on earth, he would not even be a priest, since there are those who offer the gifts according to the law.

rows.spanish: Porque, al encontrar falta en ellos, dice: «He aquí, vienen días, dice Yahvé, en que estableceré un nuevo pacto con la casa de Israel y con la casa de Judá»
rows.current_english_pob: For in finding fault with them he says, “Look, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will establish a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,”
rows.spanish_base_english: For in finding fault with them he says, “Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will establish a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,”

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, el primer pacto tenía regulaciones para el culto y un santuario terrenal.
rows.current_english_pob: Even the first covenant had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now even the first covenant had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.

rows.spanish: Y encima de ella estaban los querubines de gloria, que hacían sombra sobre el propiciatorio; acerca de estas cosas no es posible hablar ahora en detalle.
rows.current_english_pob: And above it were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the atoning sacrifice; about these things it is not now possible to speak in detail.
rows.spanish_base_english: And above it were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat; about these things it is not now possible to speak in detail.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, con estas cosas preparadas de esta manera, los sacerdotes entran continuamente en el primer tabernáculo, realizando los servicios.
rows.current_english_pob: With these things prepared in this way, the priests continually enter the first tabernacle, performing the services,
rows.spanish_base_english: Now with these things prepared in this way, the priests continually enter the first tabernacle, performing the services,

rows.spanish: Por esto el Espíritu Santo indica que el camino al santuario aún no ha sido revelado, mientras el primer tabernáculo todavía está en pie.
rows.current_english_pob: By this the Holy Spirit is indicating that the way into the holy places has not yet been revealed while the first tabernacle still has standing,
rows.spanish_base_english: By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been revealed while the first tabernacle still has standing,

rows.spanish: lo cual es una parábola para el tiempo presente, según la cual se ofrecen tanto dones como sacrificios que no pueden perfeccionar, en cuanto a la conciencia, al que rinde culto.
rows.current_english_pob: which is a parable for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that are not able to perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience,
rows.spanish_base_english: which is a parable for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience,
