rows.spanish: Pero Jesús respondió: «¡Oh generación incrédula y perversa, hasta cuándo estaré con ustedes y tendré paciencia con ustedes? Trae aquí a tu hijo»
rows.current_english_pob: But Jesus answered, “O unbelieving and twisted generation, how long will I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.”
rows.spanish_base_english: But Jesus answered, “O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long will I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.”

rows.spanish: Entonces sucedió, cuando se cumplían los días de ser llevado arriba, que fijó su rostro para ir a Jerusalén.
rows.current_english_pob: It happened, when the days of his being taken up were being fulfilled, that he set his face to go to Jerusalem.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now it happened, when the days of his being taken up were being fulfilled, that he set his face to go to Jerusalem.

rows.spanish: Entonces dijo a otro: «Sígueme». Pero él dijo: «Señor, permíteme ir primero y enterrar a mi padre».
rows.current_english_pob: Then he said to another, “Follow me.” But he said, “Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then he said to another, “Follow me.” But he said, “Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.”

rows.spanish: Sin embargo, no se alegren de esto, que los espíritus se les sujetan; alégrense más bien de que sus nombres están escritos en los cielos.
rows.current_english_pob: Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names have been written in the heavens.
rows.spanish_base_english: Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.

rows.spanish: Y él respondió: «Amarás a Yahvé tu Dios con todo tu corazón, y con toda tu alma, y con toda tu fuerza, y con toda tu mente, y a tu prójimo como a ti mismo».
rows.current_english_pob: And he answered, “You shall love the Lord your God from all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself.”

rows.spanish: Jesús respondió: «Cierto hombre iba descendiendo de Jerusalén a Jericó, y cayó entre ladrones, quienes también lo despojaron, lo golpearon y se fueron, dejándolo medio muerto».
rows.current_english_pob: Jesus replied, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who also stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Jesus replied, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.”

rows.spanish: Y por casualidad cierto sacerdote bajaba por aquel camino, y al verlo, pasó por el lado opuesto.
rows.current_english_pob: By chance a certain priest was going down on that road, and when he saw him, he passed by on the opposite side.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now by chance a certain priest was going down on that road, and when he saw him, he passed by on the opposite side.

rows.spanish: Él dijo: «El que tuvo misericordia de él». Entonces Jesús le dijo: «Ve, y tú haz lo mismo».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said, “The one who showed mercy to him.” Then Jesus said to him, “Go, and you do likewise.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said, “The one who showed mercy to him.” Then Jesus said to him, “Go, and you do likewise.”

rows.spanish: Ahora, mientras ellos iban de camino, él entró en una aldea, y una mujer llamada Marta lo recibió.
rows.current_english_pob: As they were traveling along, he entered a certain village, and a woman named Martha welcomed him.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now as they were traveling along, he entered a certain village, and a woman named Martha welcomed him.

rows.spanish: y él, respondiendo desde dentro, dice: «No me causes molestias. La puerta ya ha sido cerrada, y mis hijos están conmigo en la cama. No puedo levantarme y darte».
rows.current_english_pob: and he from inside answers and says, ‘Do not trouble me. The door has already been shut, and my children are with me in bed. I am not able to get up and give you anything.’
rows.spanish_base_english: and he from inside answers and says, ‘Do not trouble me. The door has already been shut, and my children are with me in bed. I am not able to get up and give you.’

rows.spanish: La reina del Sur se levantará en el juicio con los hombres de esta generación y los condenará, porque vino desde los confines de la tierra para oír la sabiduría de Salomón, y he aquí algo mayor que Salomón está presente aquí.
rows.current_english_pob: The queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.
rows.spanish_base_english: The queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.

rows.spanish: Los hombres de Nínive se levantarán en el juicio junto con esta generación y la condenarán, porque se arrepintieron a la proclamación de Jonás, y he aquí, algo mayor que Jonás está aquí.
rows.current_english_pob: The men of Nineveh will rise up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.
rows.spanish_base_english: The men of Nineveh will rise up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.

rows.spanish: Pero el fariseo, al verlo, se asombró de que no se había lavado primero antes de la comida.
rows.current_english_pob: But the Pharisee, when he saw it, was astonished that he had not first washed before the meal.
rows.spanish_base_english: But the Pharisee, seeing it, was astonished that he had not first washed before the meal.

rows.spanish: Pero el Señor le dijo: «Ahora ustedes, los fariseos, limpian por fuera la copa y el plato, pero por dentro están llenos de codicia y de maldad.»
rows.current_english_pob: But the Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but your inside is full of greed and wickedness.”
rows.spanish_base_english: But the Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.”

rows.spanish: Pero den como limosna lo que está dentro, y he aquí, todo es limpio para ustedes.
rows.current_english_pob: But give as alms the things that are within, and behold, everything is clean for you.
rows.spanish_base_english: But give as alms the things that are within, and behold, everything is clean for you.

rows.spanish: Pero ¡ay de ustedes, fariseos!, porque diezman la menta, la ruda y toda hortaliza, y descuidan la justicia y el amor de Dios. Estas cosas debían hacer, sin descuidar aquellas.
rows.current_english_pob: But woe to you Pharisees, because you tithe mint and rue and every herb, and you pass by justice and the love of God. These things you ought to have done, without neglecting those things.
rows.spanish_base_english: But woe to you Pharisees, because you tithe mint and rue and every herb, and you neglect justice and the love of God. These things you ought to have done, without neglecting those things.

rows.spanish: ¡Ay de ustedes, porque son como tumbas sin marcar, y las personas que caminan sobre ellas no lo saben.
rows.current_english_pob: Woe to you, because you are like unmarked tombs, and the men walking over them do not know it.
rows.spanish_base_english: Woe to you, because you are like unmarked tombs, and the people walking over them do not know it.

rows.spanish: Entonces les dijo: «Estén atentos y guárdense de toda clase de avaricia, porque la vida de uno no consiste en la abundancia de sus bienes».
rows.current_english_pob: Then he said to them, “Watch out and guard yourselves from every kind of greed, because a person’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then he said to them, “Watch out and guard yourselves from every kind of greed, because one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”

rows.spanish: Pero Dios le dijo: «¡Necio! Esta misma noche te reclaman la vida, y lo que has preparado, ¿para quién será?»
rows.current_english_pob: But God said to him, ‘Fool! This very night your life is being demanded back from you, and the things you prepared—whose will they be?’
rows.spanish_base_english: But God said to him, ‘Fool! This very night your life is demanded from you, and the things you prepared—whose will they be?’

rows.spanish: ¿Y quién de ustedes, por preocuparse, puede añadir un codo a su vida?
rows.current_english_pob: And which of you, by worrying, is able to add a cubit to his lifespan?
rows.spanish_base_english: And which of you by worrying can add a cubit to his lifespan?

rows.spanish: Y ustedes, sean como hombres que esperan a su señor cuando vuelva de las bodas, para que, cuando venga y toque, le abran en seguida.
rows.current_english_pob: And you, be like men waiting for their lord when he returns from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him at once.
rows.spanish_base_english: And you, be like men waiting for their master when he returns from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him at once.

rows.spanish: Bienaventurados esos esclavos, a quienes, cuando venga el Señor, encuentre velando. En verdad les digo que se ceñirá y hará que se reclinen a la mesa, y acercándose, les servirá.
rows.current_english_pob: Blessed are those servants whom the Lord, when he comes, will find staying awake. Truly I say to you, he will dress himself for service and have them recline at the table, and he will come and serve them.
rows.spanish_base_english: Blessed are those slaves whom the Lord, when he comes, will find staying awake. Truly I say to you, he will dress himself for service and have them recline at the table, and he will come and serve them.

rows.spanish: Pero si ese esclavo dice en su corazón: «Mi amo tarda en venir», y empieza a golpear a los esclavos varones y a las esclavas, y a comer y beber y emborracharse,
rows.current_english_pob: But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My master delays in coming,’ and begins to beat the male servants and the female servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
rows.spanish_base_english: But if that slave says in his heart, ‘My master delays in coming,’ and begins to beat the male slaves and the female servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,

rows.spanish: Vendrá el amo de aquel esclavo en un día en que no lo espera y a una hora que no conoce, y lo despedazará y asignará su lugar con los infieles.
rows.current_english_pob: the master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in pieces and assign his place with the unfaithful.
rows.spanish_base_english: the master of that slave will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in pieces and assign his place with the unfaithful.

rows.spanish: Pero aquel esclavo, que sabía la voluntad de su amo y no se preparó o actuó conforme a su voluntad, será azotado con muchos golpes.
rows.current_english_pob: But that servant, who knew his master's will and did not prepare or act according to his will, will be beaten with many blows.
rows.spanish_base_english: But that slave, who knew his master's will and did not prepare or act according to his will, will be beaten with many blows.

rows.spanish: En ese mismo momento, algunos estaban presentes informándole acerca de los galileos, cuya sangre Pilato había mezclado con sus sacrificios.
rows.current_english_pob: Some were present at that very time reporting to him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now some were present at that very time reporting to him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

rows.spanish: Y respondiendo, les dijo: «¿Piensan que estos galileos eran pecadores más que todos los demás galileos, porque han padecido estas cosas?»
rows.current_english_pob: And answering, he said to them, “Do you think that these Galileans became sinners beyond all the Galileans, because they have suffered these things?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And answering, he said to them, “Do you think that these Galileans were sinners beyond all the Galileans, because they have suffered these things?”

rows.spanish: No, les digo; pero, a menos que cambien su manera de pensar, todos ustedes perecerán de la misma manera.
rows.current_english_pob: No, I tell you; but unless you change your thinking, you will all likewise perish.
rows.spanish_base_english: No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.

rows.spanish: ¿O aquellos dieciocho sobre quienes cayó la torre en Siloé y los mató? ¿Piensan ustedes que ellos se hicieron más culpables que todos los habitantes de Jerusalén?
rows.current_english_pob: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think that they became debtors beyond all the men living in Jerusalem?
rows.spanish_base_english: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think that they became worse offenders than all the people living in Jerusalem?

rows.spanish: Entonces le dijo al viñador: «Mira, desde hace tres años vengo buscando fruto en esta higuera y no lo encuentro. Córtala. ¿Por qué ha de seguir desperdiciando la tierra?»
rows.current_english_pob: Then he said to the vine-dresser, ‘Look, for three years now I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree and have found none. Cut it down. Why should it even keep using up the ground?’
rows.spanish_base_english: Then he said to the vine-dresser, ‘Look, for three years now I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree and find none. Cut it down. Why should it even use up the ground?’

rows.spanish: Estaba enseñando en una de las sinagogas un sábado.
rows.current_english_pob: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí una mujer que tenía un espíritu de infirmidad desde hacía dieciocho años; y estaba encorvada y no podía enderezarse por completo.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years, and she was bent over and unable to straighten up completely.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years, and she was bent over and unable to straighten up completely.

rows.spanish: Y le puso las manos sobre ella, e inmediatamente quedó derecha, y glorificaba a Dios.
rows.current_english_pob: And he laid his hands on her, and immediately she was made straight again, and she glorified God.
rows.spanish_base_english: And he laid his hands on her, and immediately she was made straight, and she glorified God.

rows.spanish: ¿Y no era necesario que esta mujer, hija de Abraham, a quien Satanás ató durante dieciocho años, fuera desatada de esta atadura en el día de sábado?
rows.current_english_pob: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound for eighteen years—look—be released from this bond on the Sabbath day?
rows.spanish_base_english: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound for eighteen years—be released from this bond on the Sabbath day?

rows.spanish: Y alguien le dijo: «Señor, ¿son solo unos pocos los que están siendo salvados?» Y él les dijo:
rows.current_english_pob: And someone said to him, “Lord, are only a few being saved?” And he said to them,
rows.spanish_base_english: And someone said to him, “Lord, are only a few being saved?” And he said to them,

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, hay últimos que serán primeros, y hay primeros que serán últimos.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.

rows.spanish: Y les dijo: «Vayan y díganle a ese zorro: “Mira, expulso demonios y realizo sanidades hoy y mañana, y al tercer día habré llegado a mi meta”».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Look, I cast out demons and accomplish healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am brought to completion.’”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Look, I cast out demons and perform healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am perfected.’”

rows.spanish: He aquí, la casa de ustedes les es dejada. Y les digo que no me verán de ningún modo hasta que llegue el tiempo en que digan: «Bendito el que viene en el nombre del Señor».
rows.current_english_pob: Look, your house is left to you. And I tell you, you will certainly not see me until the time comes when you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.’
rows.spanish_base_english: Look, your house is left to you. And I tell you, you will certainly not see me until the time comes when you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.’

rows.spanish: Y he aquí cierto hombre con hidropesía estaba delante de él.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, a certain man with dropsy was before him.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, a certain man with dropsy was before him.

rows.spanish: Les decía una parábola a los invitados, observando cómo escogían los lugares de honor, diciéndoles:
rows.current_english_pob: He was telling a parable to those who had been invited, noticing how they were choosing the places of honor, saying to them:
rows.spanish_base_english: Now he was telling a parable to those who had been invited, noticing how they were choosing the places of honor, saying to them:

rows.spanish: Cuando seas invitado por alguien a una fiesta de bodas, no te reclines en el lugar de honor, no sea que por él haya sido invitado alguien más honrado que tú.
rows.current_english_pob: When you are invited by someone to a wedding feast, do not recline in the place of honor, lest someone more honored than you has been invited by him.
rows.spanish_base_english: When you are invited by someone to a wedding feast, do not recline in the place of honor, lest someone more honored than you may have been invited by him.

rows.spanish: Y el amo dijo al esclavo: «Sal a los caminos y cercas, y obliga a la gente a entrar, para que mi casa se llene».
rows.current_english_pob: And the master said to the servant, ‘Go out into the roads and hedges, and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled.’
rows.spanish_base_english: And the master said to the slave, ‘Go out into the roads and hedges, and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled.’

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, grandes multitudes iban con él, y volviéndose, les dijo:
rows.current_english_pob: Large crowds were traveling with him, and turning, he said to them:
rows.spanish_base_english: Now large crowds were traveling with him, and turning, he said to them:

rows.spanish: Y todos los recaudadores de impuestos y los pecadores se acercaban a él para oírle.
rows.current_english_pob: All the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to hear him.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to hear him.

rows.spanish: ¿Qué hombre entre ustedes, teniendo cien ovejas y perdiendo una de ellas, no deja las noventa y nueve en el desierto y va tras la oveja perdida hasta encontrarla?
rows.current_english_pob: What man among you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the open country and go after the lost one until he finds it?
rows.spanish_base_english: What man among you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?

rows.spanish: Y cuando llega a la casa, convoca a sus amigos y vecinos, diciéndoles: «Alégrense conmigo, porque he encontrado mi oveja perdida».
rows.current_english_pob: And when he comes into the house, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost.’
rows.spanish_base_english: And when he comes into the house, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found my lost sheep.’

rows.spanish: Les digo que, de la misma manera, habrá más alegría en el cielo por un pecador que cambia su manera de pensar que por noventa y nueve justos que no necesitan hacerlo.
rows.current_english_pob: I tell you, in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who has a change of mind than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of one.
rows.spanish_base_english: I tell you, in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of repentance.

rows.spanish: Pero el padre dijo a sus esclavos: «Rápidamente, saquen la mejor túnica y vístanlo, y pónganle un anillo en su mano y sandalias en sus pies».
rows.current_english_pob: But the father said to his servants, ‘Quickly, bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.’
rows.spanish_base_english: But the father said to his slaves, ‘Quickly, bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.’

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, su hijo mayor estaba en el campo; y cuando venía y se acercó a la casa, oyó música y bailes.
rows.current_english_pob: His older son was in the field; and as he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing,
rows.spanish_base_english: Now his older son was in the field; and as he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing,

rows.spanish: Y él dijo: «Cien batos de aceite de oliva». Entonces le dijo: «Toma tu cuenta, siéntate enseguida y escribe cincuenta».
rows.current_english_pob: He said, ‘A hundred baths of olive oil.’ Then he said to him, ‘Take your bill, sit down quickly, and write fifty.’
rows.spanish_base_english: He said, ‘A hundred baths of olive oil.’ Then he said to him, ‘Take your bill, sit down quickly, and write fifty.’

rows.spanish: Entonces dijo a otro: «¿Y tú, cuánto debes?». Él dijo: «Cien coros de trigo». Le dice: «Toma tu cuenta y escribe ochenta».
rows.current_english_pob: Then he said to another, ‘And you, how much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He says to him, ‘Take your bill and write eighty.’
rows.spanish_base_english: Then he said to another, ‘And you, how much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He says to him, ‘Take your bill and write eighty.’

rows.spanish: Ahora los fariseos, que eran amantes del dinero, oían todas estas cosas y se burlaban de él.
rows.current_english_pob: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, were hearing all these things and were ridiculing him.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, were hearing all these things and were ridiculing him.

rows.spanish: La Ley y los Profetas fueron hasta Juan; desde entonces el reino de Dios se proclama como buena noticia, y todos se abren paso para entrar en él.
rows.current_english_pob: The Law and the Prophets were until John; from then on the kingdom of God is being proclaimed as good news, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
rows.spanish_base_english: The Law and the Prophets were until John; from then on the kingdom of God is proclaimed as good news, and everyone is forcing his way into it.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, había un hombre rico, que se vestía de púrpura y de lino fino, celebrando banquetes espléndidamente todos los días.
rows.current_english_pob: There was a certain rich man, and he used to dress in purple and fine linen, feasting splendidly every day.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now there was a certain rich man, and he used to dress in purple and fine linen, feasting splendidly every day.

rows.spanish: Y sucedió que el pobre murió y fue llevado por los ángeles al seno de Abraham. Y el rico también murió y fue sepultado.
rows.current_english_pob: It happened that the poor man died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. And the rich man also died and was buried.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now it happened that the poor man died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. And the rich man also died and was buried.

rows.spanish: Pero él dijo: «No, padre Abraham; pero si alguien va a ellos de entre los muertos, cambiarán su manera de pensar».
rows.current_english_pob: But he said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if someone goes to them from among the dead, they will change their thinking.’
rows.spanish_base_english: But he said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’

rows.spanish: Pero ¿quién de ustedes, teniendo un esclavo que ara o pastorea, le dirá cuando vuelva del campo: «Pasa enseguida y recuéstate a la mesa»?
rows.current_english_pob: But which of you, having a servant plowing or shepherding, will say to him when he has come in from the field, ‘Come at once and recline at the table’?
rows.spanish_base_english: But which of you, having a slave plowing or shepherding, will say to him when he has come in from the field, ‘Come at once and recline at the table’?

rows.spanish: ¿Acaso le agradece al esclavo porque hizo lo que se le había ordenado?
rows.current_english_pob: Does he thank the servant because he did what was commanded?
rows.spanish_base_english: Does he thank the slave because he did what was commanded?

rows.spanish: Así también ustedes, cuando hayan hecho todo lo que se les ha mandado, digan: «Somos esclavos indignos; hemos hecho lo que debíamos hacer».
rows.current_english_pob: So also you, when you have done all that was commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have done what we were obligated to do.’
rows.spanish_base_english: So also you, when you have done all that was commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy slaves; we have done what we were obligated to do.’

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, cuando los fariseos le preguntaron cuándo venía el reino de Dios, les respondió: «El reino de Dios no viene con señales visibles».
rows.current_english_pob: When he was asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God was coming, he answered them and said, “The kingdom of God does not come with observable signs,”
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when he was asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God was coming, he answered them and said, “The kingdom of God does not come with observable signs,”

rows.spanish: Ni dirán: «¡Miren, aquí!» o «¡Allí!»; pues he aquí, el reino de Dios está en medio de ustedes.
rows.current_english_pob: Nor will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘There!’ For behold, the kingdom of God is in your midst.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Nor will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘There!’ For behold, the kingdom of God is in your midst.”

rows.spanish: Porque, así como el relámpago resplandece de un extremo del cielo al otro, así será el Hijo del Hombre en su día.
rows.current_english_pob: For just as lightning, flashing from one part under heaven to the other part under heaven, shines, so will the Son of Man be in his day.
rows.spanish_base_english: For just as lightning flashes from under heaven to under heaven and shines, so will the Son of Man be in his day.

rows.spanish: Aquel día, el que esté en la azotea, con sus pertenencias en la casa, no baje a tomarlas; y asimismo, el que esté en el campo no vuelva atrás.
rows.current_english_pob: On that day, whoever is on the housetop, with his belongings in the house, must not go down to take them away; and likewise, the one in the field must not turn back to the things behind.
rows.spanish_base_english: On that day, whoever is on the housetop, with his belongings in the house, must not go down to take them away; and likewise, the one in the field must not turn back.

rows.spanish: Y les decía una parábola acerca de la necesidad de orar siempre y no perder el ánimo.
rows.current_english_pob: He was telling them a parable about their need to pray always and not lose heart,
rows.spanish_base_english: Now he was telling them a parable about the need for them to pray always and not lose heart,

rows.spanish: pero porque esta viuda me causa problemas, le haré justicia, para que, viniendo continuamente, no me agote”.
rows.current_english_pob: yet because this widow keeps causing me trouble, I will give her justice, so that by continually coming she may not wear me out.”
rows.spanish_base_english: yet because this widow is causing me trouble, I will give her justice, so that by continually coming she may not wear me out.”

rows.spanish: Y les dijo también esta parábola a algunos que confiaban en sí mismos que eran justos, y trataban con desprecio a los demás:
rows.current_english_pob: And he also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and treated the rest with contempt:
rows.spanish_base_english: And he also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and treated the others with contempt:

rows.spanish: Le traían incluso a los infantes para que él los tocara; pero cuando los discípulos vieron esto, los reprendieron.
rows.current_english_pob: They were even bringing infants to him so that he might touch them, but when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now they were even bringing infants to him so that he might touch them, but when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.

rows.spanish: Cuando Jesús oyó esto, le dijo: «Todavía te falta una cosa: vende todo lo que tienes y repártelo entre los pobres, y tendrás un tesoro en el cielo; y ven, sígueme».
rows.current_english_pob: When Jesus heard this, he said to him, “One thing still lacks for you: sell all that you have and distribute it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”
rows.spanish_base_english: When Jesus heard this, he said to him, “One thing still is lacking for you: sell all that you have and distribute it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”

rows.spanish: Y les dijo: «En verdad les digo que no hay nadie que haya dejado casa o esposa o hermanos o padres o hijos por causa del reino de Dios».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said to them, “Truly I say to you, there is no one who has left a house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God,”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said to them, “Truly I say to you, there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God,”

rows.spanish: Sucedió que, cuando se acercaba a Jericó, un ciego estaba sentado junto al camino, pidiendo limosna.
rows.current_english_pob: As he was approaching Jericho, a certain blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now as he was approaching Jericho, a certain blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí un hombre de nombre Zaqueo; era jefe de los recaudadores de impuestos y era rico.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, a man named Zacchaeus; he was a chief tax collector and was rich.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, a man named Zacchaeus; he was a chief tax collector and was rich.

rows.spanish: Después de llamar a diez de sus propios esclavos, les dio diez minas y les dijo: «Hagan negocios hasta que yo venga».
rows.current_english_pob: After calling ten of his own servants, he gave them ten minas and said to them, “Do business until I come.”
rows.spanish_base_english: After calling ten of his own slaves, he gave them ten minas and said to them, “Do business until I come.”

rows.spanish: Y sucedió que, cuando volvió después de recibir el reino, mandó llamar ante él a estos esclavos, a quienes había dado el dinero, para saber qué habían ganado al negociar.
rows.current_english_pob: And it happened, when he returned after receiving the kingdom, that he ordered these servants to whom he had given the money to be called to him, so that he might know what they had gained by trading.
rows.spanish_base_english: And it happened, when he returned after receiving the kingdom, that he ordered these slaves to whom he had given the money to be called to him, so that he might know what they had gained by trading.

rows.spanish: Entonces vino el primero, diciendo: «Señor, tu mina ha producido diez minas más».
rows.current_english_pob: Then the first came, saying, ‘Lord, your mina has earned ten minas.’
rows.spanish_base_english: Then the first came, saying, ‘Lord, your mina has made ten minas more.’

rows.spanish: Y llegó el segundo, diciendo: «Tu mina, señor, ha producido cinco minas».
rows.current_english_pob: And the second came, saying, ‘Your mina, Lord, has made five minas.’
rows.spanish_base_english: And the second came, saying, ‘Your mina, lord, has made five minas.’

rows.spanish: Él le dijo: “Por tu propia boca te juzgaré, esclavo malvado. ¿Sabías que yo soy un hombre severo, que recojo lo que no puse y cosecho lo que no sembré?”
rows.current_english_pob: He said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth I will judge you, wicked servant. You knew that I am a harsh man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow?’
rows.spanish_base_english: He said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth I will judge you, wicked slave. You knew that I am a harsh man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow?’

rows.spanish: diciendo: «Vayan a la aldea que está enfrente de ustedes; al entrar en ella, hallarán un pollino atado, sobre el cual nadie de entre los hombres se ha sentado jamás. Desátenlo y tráiganlo».
rows.current_english_pob: saying, “Go into the village opposite you, in which, as you enter, you will find a colt tied up, on which no one among men has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.”
rows.spanish_base_english: saying, “Go into the village opposite you, in which, as you enter, you will find a colt tied, on which no one among men has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.”

rows.spanish: Y no hallaban qué podían hacer, porque todo el pueblo escuchaba pendiente de sus palabras.
rows.current_english_pob: And they could not find what they might do, because all the people were hanging on his words as they listened.
rows.spanish_base_english: And they could not find what they might do, because all the people were hanging on him, listening.

rows.spanish: Pero si decimos: «De parte de los hombres», todo el pueblo nos apedreará, porque todos están convencidos de que Juan es profeta.
rows.current_english_pob: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet.
rows.spanish_base_english: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John is a prophet.

rows.spanish: Y a su debido tiempo envió a un esclavo a los viñadores, para que le dieran algo del fruto de la viña. Pero los viñadores, después de golpearlo, lo enviaron de vuelta con las manos vacías.
rows.current_english_pob: And at the proper time he sent a servant to the vine-growers, so that they would give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. But the vine-growers sent him away empty after beating him.
rows.spanish_base_english: And at the proper time he sent a slave to the vine-growers, so that they would give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. But the vine-growers sent him away empty after beating him.

rows.spanish: Y procedió a enviar otro esclavo; pero también a ese lo golpearon y lo deshonraron, y lo enviaron de vuelta con las manos vacías.
rows.current_english_pob: And he proceeded to send another servant; but they also beat and dishonored that one, and sent him away empty-handed.
rows.spanish_base_english: And he proceeded to send another slave; but they also beat and dishonored that one, and sent him away empty-handed.

rows.spanish: Pero él los miró y dijo: «¿Qué, pues, es esto que está escrito: “La piedra que rechazaron los constructores, esta piedra ha llegado a ser la cabeza del ángulo”?»
rows.current_english_pob: But he looked at them and said, “What then is this that has been written: ‘The stone that the builders rejected, this one has become the head of the corner’?”
rows.spanish_base_english: But he looked at them and said, “What then is this that is written: ‘The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner’?”

rows.spanish: Y no pudieron sorprenderlo en sus palabras ante el pueblo, y, maravillados por su respuesta, callaron.
rows.current_english_pob: And they were not able to seize on his statement before the people, and marveling at his answer, they became silent.
rows.spanish_base_english: And they were not able to catch him in a statement before the people, and marveling at his answer, they became silent.

rows.spanish: Pues había siete hermanos; y el primero, después de casarse, murió sin hijos.
rows.current_english_pob: There were seven brothers; and the first, having taken a wife, died childless.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now there were seven brothers; and the first, having taken a wife, died childless.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, Dios no es Dios de los muertos, sino de los vivos, porque para él todos viven.
rows.current_english_pob: He is not God of the dead, but of the living, for all live to him.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now he is not God of the dead, but of the living, for all live to him.

rows.spanish: Porque todos estos echaron de lo que les sobraba en los dones; pero ella, de su escasez, echó todo el sustento que tenía.
rows.current_english_pob: For all these gave into the gifts out of their abundance, but she, out of her lack, put in all the livelihood she had.
rows.spanish_base_english: For all these gave out of their abundance into the gifts, but she, out of her lack, put in all the livelihood she had.

rows.spanish: Pero cuando oigan hablar de guerras y convulsiones, no se aterroricen; porque es necesario que estas cosas sucedan primero, pero el fin no llega enseguida.
rows.current_english_pob: But when you hear of wars and upheavals, do not be terrified; for these things must happen first, but the end is not at once.
rows.spanish_base_english: But when you hear of wars and upheavals, do not be terrified; for these things must happen first, but the end is not at once.

rows.spanish: Porque yo les daré una boca y sabiduría, a la cual no podrán resistir ni contradecir todos los que se les oponen.
rows.current_english_pob: For I will give you words and wisdom that all who oppose you will not be able to withstand or contradict.
rows.spanish_base_english: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all who oppose you will not be able to withstand or contradict.

rows.spanish: Entonces, los que están en Judea huyan a los montes, y los que están en medio de ella se retiren, y los que están en el campo no entren en ella.
rows.current_english_pob: Then let those in Judea flee to the mountains, and let those in the midst of her depart, and let those in the countryside not enter into her.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then let those in Judea flee to the mountains, and let those in the midst of it depart, and let those in the countryside not enter into it.

rows.spanish: Y durante el día enseñaba en el templo, pero de noche salía y se alojaba en el Monte de los Olivos.
rows.current_english_pob: And during the days he was teaching in the temple, but at night he would go out and lodge on the mountain called the Mount of Olives.
rows.spanish_base_english: And during the days he was teaching in the temple, but at night he would go out and lodge on the mount called Olivet.

rows.spanish: Se acercaba la fiesta de los panes sin levadura, llamada Pascua.
rows.current_english_pob: The Feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called Passover, was drawing near.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the Feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called Passover, was drawing near.

rows.spanish: Pero he aquí, la mano del que me traiciona está conmigo sobre la mesa.
rows.current_english_pob: But look, the hand of the one betraying me is with me on the table.
rows.spanish_base_english: But behold, the hand of the one betraying me is with me on the table.

rows.spanish: Ahora también surgió entre ellos una disputa acerca de cuál de ellos se consideraba mayor.
rows.current_english_pob: A dispute also arose among them as to which of them was considered to be greater.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now a dispute also arose among them as to which of them was considered to be greater.

rows.spanish: Y yo dispongo para ustedes un reino, así como mi Padre dispuso uno para mí,
rows.current_english_pob: And I appoint to you, just as my Father appointed to me, a kingdom.
rows.spanish_base_english: And I confer on you a kingdom, just as my Father conferred one on me,

rows.spanish: Simón, Simón, he aquí, Satanás los ha reclamado a todos ustedes, para zarandearlos como trigo.
rows.current_english_pob: Simon, Simon, look: Satan has demanded to have all of you, to sift you like wheat.
rows.spanish_base_english: Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has demanded to have all of you, to sift you like wheat.

rows.spanish: Porque les digo que es necesario que esto que está escrito se cumpla en mí: «Y fue contado entre los inicuos». Porque lo que me concierne tiene su cumplimiento.
rows.current_english_pob: For I tell you that this which is written must be fulfilled in me: ‘And he was counted with the lawless.’ For what concerns me has its fulfillment.
rows.spanish_base_english: For I tell you that this which is written must be fulfilled in me: ‘And he was counted with the lawless.’ For what concerns me has its fulfillment.

rows.spanish: Y les dijo: «¿Por qué están durmiendo? Levántense y oren, para que no entren en tentación».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray, so that you may not enter into temptation.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Rise and pray, so that you may not enter into temptation.”

rows.spanish: Mientras él todavía hablaba, he aquí que llegó una multitud, y el llamado Judas, uno de los doce, iba delante de ellos, y se acercó a Jesús para besarlo.
rows.current_english_pob: While he was still speaking, behold, a crowd came, and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was going before them, and he came near to Jesus to kiss him.
rows.spanish_base_english: While he was still speaking, behold, a crowd came, and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was going before them, and he came near to Jesus to kiss him.

rows.spanish: Y uno de ellos golpeó al esclavo del sumo sacerdote y le cortó su oreja derecha.
rows.current_english_pob: And one of them struck the high priest’s servant and cut off his right ear.
rows.spanish_base_english: And one of them struck the high priest’s slave and cut off his right ear.

rows.spanish: Pero Jesús respondió: «No más de esto». Y tocó su oreja y lo sanó.
rows.current_english_pob: But Jesus answered, “Enough of this!” And he touched his ear and healed him.
rows.spanish_base_english: But Jesus answered, “No more of this!” And he touched his ear and healed him.

rows.spanish: Y al cabo de un rato, otro hombre, al verlo, dijo: «Tú también eres uno de ellos». Pero Pedro dijo: «Hombre, no soy».
rows.current_english_pob: And after a little while, another man, seeing him, said, “You also are one of them.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And after a little while, another man, seeing him, said, “You also are one of them.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not.”

rows.spanish: Y saliendo, lloró amargamente.
rows.current_english_pob: And after going outside, he wept bitterly.
rows.spanish_base_english: And going outside, he wept bitterly.

rows.spanish: Entonces Herodes, al ver a Jesús, se alegró mucho, porque desde hacía mucho tiempo quería verlo, ya que había oído hablar de él, y esperaba ver alguna señal hecha por él.
rows.current_english_pob: When Herod saw Jesus, he rejoiced greatly, for he had for a long time wanted to see him because he had heard about him, and he was hoping to see some sign done by him.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when Herod saw Jesus, he rejoiced greatly, for he had for a long time wanted to see him because he had heard about him, and he was hoping to see some sign done by him.

rows.spanish: Herodes y Pilato se hicieron amigos entre sí aquel mismo día, porque antes estaban enemistados entre sí.
rows.current_english_pob: And Herod and Pilate became friends with each other on that very day, for previously they had been in hostility toward one another.
rows.spanish_base_english: And Herod and Pilate became friends with each other on that very day, for previously they had been hostile toward each other.

rows.spanish: Él les dijo: «Ustedes me trajeron a este hombre como uno que estaba desviando al pueblo, y he aquí, después de examinarlo delante de ustedes, no hallé en este hombre ningún fundamento para los cargos que ustedes presentan contra él».
rows.current_english_pob: He said to them, “You brought this man to me as one who was misleading the people, and behold, after examining him before you, I found no basis in this man for the charges you bring against him.”
rows.spanish_base_english: He said to them, “You brought this man to me as one who was misleading the people, and behold, after examining him before you, I found no basis in this man for the charges you bring against him.”

rows.spanish: Pero ni siquiera Herodes, porque nos lo devolvió. Y he aquí, nada digno de muerte se ha hecho por él.
rows.current_english_pob: But neither did Herod, for he sent him back to us. And look, nothing deserving of death has been done by him.
rows.spanish_base_english: But neither did Herod, for he sent him back to us. And behold, nothing deserving of death has been done by him.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, tenía la obligación de poner en libertad a un preso para ellos en la fiesta.
rows.current_english_pob: He had an obligation to release one man to them at the festival.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now he had an obligation to release one man to them at the festival.

rows.spanish: Lo seguía una gran multitud del pueblo, incluidas mujeres que se golpeaban el pecho y se lamentaban por él.
rows.current_english_pob: A large crowd of people followed him, including women who were beating their breasts and mourning for him.
rows.spanish_base_english: And a large crowd of the people and of women was following him, and the women were beating their breasts and mourning for him.

rows.spanish: Porque, he aquí, vienen días en que dirán: «Bienaventuradas las estériles, y los vientres que no dieron a luz, y los pechos que no amamantaron».
rows.current_english_pob: For look, days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren women, and the wombs that never bore, and the breasts that never nursed.’
rows.spanish_base_english: For behold, days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren women, and the wombs that never bore, and the breasts that never nursed.’

rows.spanish: Pero uno de los criminales que estaban colgados lo insultaba, diciendo: «¿No eres tú el Mesías? Sálvate a ti mismo y a nosotros».
rows.current_english_pob: One of the criminals who were hanging there was reviling him, saying, “Are you not the Messiah? Save yourself and us.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Now one of the criminals who were hanging there was reviling him, saying, “Are you not the Messiah? Save yourself and us.”

rows.spanish: Entonces, cuando el centurión vio lo que había sucedido, glorificó a Dios, diciendo: «Ciertamente este hombre era justo».
rows.current_english_pob: When the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God, saying, “Certainly this man was righteous.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God, saying, “Certainly this man was righteous.”

rows.spanish: Y he aquí un hombre llamado José, miembro del consejo, hombre bueno y recto—
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, a man named Joseph, who was a council member, a good and righteous man—
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, a man named Joseph, who was a council member, a good and righteous man—

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, las mujeres que habían venido con él desde Galilea siguieron y vieron el sepulcro, y cómo fue colocado su cuerpo.
rows.current_english_pob: The women who had come with him from Galilee followed and saw the tomb and how his body was laid.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the women who had come with him from Galilee followed and saw the tomb and how his body was laid.

rows.spanish: Y sucedió que, mientras estaban perplejas acerca de esto, he aquí, dos hombres se presentaron junto a ellas con vestiduras resplandecientes.
rows.current_english_pob: And it happened, while they were perplexed about this, that behold, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing.
rows.spanish_base_english: And it happened, while they were perplexed about this, that behold, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing.

rows.spanish: Y eran María Magdalena, Juana, María, la madre de Jacobo, y las demás mujeres con ellas; estaban diciéndoles estas cosas a los apóstoles.
rows.current_english_pob: They were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them; they were telling these things to the apostles.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now they were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them; they were telling these things to the apostles.

rows.spanish: Y estas palabras les parecieron disparates, y no les creían a ellas.
rows.current_english_pob: And these words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.
rows.spanish_base_english: And these words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe them.

rows.spanish: Pero Pedro se levantó y corrió al sepulcro; y, asomándose para mirar dentro, vio los lienzos de lino solos; y se fue por su cuenta, maravillándose de lo que había sucedido.
rows.current_english_pob: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb; and stooping to look in, he sees the linen cloths alone, and he went away to himself, marveling at what had happened.
rows.spanish_base_english: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb; and stooping to look in, he saw the linen cloths alone, and he went away to himself, marveling at what had happened.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí que dos de ellos iban aquel mismo día a una aldea que distaba sesenta estadios de Jerusalén, cuyo nombre era Emaús.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, two of them were going that very day to a village sixty stadia from Jerusalem, whose name was Emmaus,
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, two of them were going that very day to a village sixty stadia from Jerusalem, whose name was Emmaus,

rows.spanish: Y él les dijo: «¿Qué cosas?». Ellos le dijeron: «Las cosas acerca de Jesús el Nazareno, que fue un hombre, un profeta, poderoso en obra y palabra delante de Dios y de todo el pueblo».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said to them, “What things?” And they said to him, “The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who became a man, a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said to them, “What things?” And they said to him, “The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who was a prophet, mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,”

rows.spanish: Pero nosotros esperábamos que él era quien iba a redimir a Israel. Pero, además de todo esto, ya es el tercer día desde que sucedieron estas cosas.
rows.current_english_pob: But we were hoping that he is the one who is about to redeem Israel. Yet besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.
rows.spanish_base_english: But we were hoping that he was the one who was going to redeem Israel. But besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.

rows.spanish: Y como ellos todavía no lo creían de alegría y se maravillaban, les dijo: «¿Tienen aquí algo de comer?»
rows.current_english_pob: And while they still were disbelieving because of joy and were marveling, he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And while they still were disbelieving for joy and marveling, he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, yo estoy enviando la promesa de mi Padre sobre ustedes. Pero quédense en la ciudad hasta que sean revestidos de poder desde lo alto.
rows.current_english_pob: And look, I am sending the promise of my Father upon you. But stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, I am sending the promise of my Father upon you. But stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.

rows.spanish: El comienzo de la buena noticia de Jesús el Mesías.
rows.current_english_pob: The beginning of the good news of Jesus the Messiah.
rows.spanish_base_english: The beginning of the good news of Jesus Messiah.

rows.spanish: Así como está escrito en Isaías el profeta: «He aquí, envío a mi mensajero delante de tu rostro, quien preparará tu camino».
rows.current_english_pob: Just as it is written in Isaiah the prophet: ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way.’
rows.spanish_base_english: Just as it is written in Isaiah the prophet: ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way.’

rows.spanish: Y Juan estaba vestido con pelo de camello y un cinturón de cuero alrededor de su cintura, y comía langostas y miel silvestre.
rows.current_english_pob: John was clothed with camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist, and he was eating locusts and wild honey.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now John was clothed with camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist, and he was eating locusts and wild honey.

rows.spanish: Y Jesús les dijo: «Vengan tras mí, y haré que lleguen a ser pescadores de personas».
rows.current_english_pob: And Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of men.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of people.”

rows.spanish: Y entraron en Cafarnaúm, y enseguida, el sábado, enseñaba en la sinagoga.
rows.current_english_pob: And they went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath he began teaching in the synagogue.
rows.spanish_base_english: And they went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath he was teaching in the synagogue.

rows.spanish: La suegra de Simón estaba acostada con fiebre, y enseguida le dijeron acerca de ella.
rows.current_english_pob: Simon’s mother-in-law was lying sick with a fever, and immediately they told him about her.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now Simon’s mother-in-law was lying sick with a fever, and immediately they told him about her.

rows.spanish: Pero después de salir, comenzó a proclamarlo ampliamente y a divulgar la noticia, de modo que Jesús ya no podía entrar abiertamente en un pueblo, sino que estaba fuera, en lugares desiertos; y acudían a él de todas partes.
rows.current_english_pob: But after he went out, he began to proclaim widely and to spread the message, so that Jesus could no longer enter a town openly, but stayed outside in deserted places; and people were coming to him from everywhere.
rows.spanish_base_english: But after he went out, he began to proclaim it widely and to spread the message, so that Jesus could no longer enter a town openly, but was outside in deserted places; and they were coming to him from everywhere.

rows.spanish: Y al oírlo, Jesús les dice: «Los fuertes no tienen necesidad de médico, sino los que están enfermos. No vine a llamar a justos, sino a pecadores».
rows.current_english_pob: And when Jesus heard it, he says to them, “Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And hearing it, Jesus says to them, “Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, los discípulos de Juan y los fariseos estaban ayunando. Y vienen y le dicen: «¿Por qué los discípulos de Juan y los discípulos de los fariseos ayunan, pero tus discípulos no ayunan?»
rows.current_english_pob: John's disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. And they come and say to him, "Why do John's disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?"
rows.spanish_base_english: Now John's disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. And they come and say to him, "Why do John's disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?"

rows.spanish: Y les dijo: «¿Nunca han leído lo que hizo David cuando tuvo necesidad y hambre, él y los que estaban con él?»
rows.current_english_pob: And he said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and was hungry, he and those with him?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him?”

rows.spanish: Porque había sanado a muchos, de modo que todos los que tenían aflicciones se abalanzaban sobre él para tocarlo.
rows.current_english_pob: For he had healed many, so that all who had afflictions were pressing in on him in order to touch him.
rows.spanish_base_english: For he had healed many, so that all who had afflictions were falling upon him in order to touch him.

rows.spanish: Porque cualquiera que haga la voluntad de Dios, esa persona es mi hermano y hermana y madre.
rows.current_english_pob: For whoever does the will of God, this one is my brother and sister and mother.
rows.spanish_base_english: For whoever does the will of God, he is my brother and sister and mother.

rows.spanish: Y otra vez comenzó a enseñar junto al mar. Y una multitud muy grande se reúne hacia él, de modo que, entrando en una barca, se sentó sobre el mar, y toda la multitud estaba junto al mar, en tierra.
rows.current_english_pob: And again he began to teach beside the sea. And a very large crowd gathers to him, so that he got into a boat and sat on the sea, and the whole crowd was by the sea on the land.
rows.spanish_base_english: And again he began to teach beside the sea. And a very large crowd gathers to him, so that, getting into a boat, he sat on the sea, and the whole crowd was by the sea on the land.

rows.spanish: Y les decía: «A ustedes se les ha dado el misterio del reino de Dios, pero a los de afuera todo les llega en parábolas»
rows.current_english_pob: And he was saying to them, “To you the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given, but to those outside everything comes in parables,”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he was saying to them, “To you the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given, but to those outside everything is in parables,”

rows.spanish: Y él decía: «¿Cómo compararíamos el reino de Dios, o con qué parábola lo presentaríamos?»
rows.current_english_pob: And he was saying, “How should we compare the kingdom of God, or in what parable should we set it forth?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he was saying, “How should we compare the kingdom of God, or by what parable should we present it?”

rows.spanish: Y había allí, junto al monte, una gran piara de cerdos alimentándose.
rows.current_english_pob: There was there near the mountain a large herd of pigs feeding.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now there was there near the mountain a large herd of pigs feeding.

rows.spanish: Y entrando, les dice: «¿Por qué están haciendo alboroto y llorando? La niña no ha muerto, sino que duerme».
rows.current_english_pob: And after entering, he says to them, “Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The child has not died, but is sleeping.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And entering in, he says to them, “Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The child has not died, but is sleeping.”

rows.spanish: Y cualquier lugar que no los reciba ni los escuche, al salir de allí, sacudan el polvo de debajo de sus pies como testimonio para ellos.
rows.current_english_pob: And whatever place does not receive you or listen to you, as you leave there, shake off the dust that is under your feet as a testimony against them.
rows.spanish_base_english: And whatever place does not receive you or listen to you, as you leave there, shake off the dust that is under your feet as a testimony to them.

rows.spanish: Y ella salió y dijo a su madre: «¿Qué debo pedir?» Y ella dijo: «La cabeza de Juan el Bautizador».
rows.current_english_pob: And after going out, she said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” And she said, “The head of John the Baptizer.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And she went out and said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” And she said, “The head of John the Baptizer.”

rows.spanish: Pero él les dice: «¿Cuántos panes tienen? Vayan y vean». Y después de averiguarlo, dicen: «Cinco, y dos peces».
rows.current_english_pob: But he said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” And when they found out, they said, “Five, and two fish.”
rows.spanish_base_english: But he says to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” And when they found out, they say, “Five, and two fish.”

rows.spanish: Y recogieron doce cestas llenas de fragmentos, y de los peces.
rows.current_english_pob: And they picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces, and some of the fish.
rows.spanish_base_english: And they picked up twelve baskets full of broken pieces, and from the fish.

rows.spanish: Pues todos lo vieron y se turbaron. Pero él enseguida habló con ellos y les dice: «Tengan valor; soy yo; no tengan miedo».
rows.current_english_pob: For they all saw him and were troubled. But he immediately spoke with them and says to them, “Take courage; I am; do not be afraid.”
rows.spanish_base_english: For they all saw him and were troubled. But he immediately spoke with them and says to them, “Take courage; it is I; do not be afraid.”

rows.spanish: Y por dondequiera que entraba en aldeas, ciudades o zonas rurales, en las plazas de mercado ponían a los enfermos, y le rogaban que siquiera tocaran el borde de su manto; y cuantos lo tocaban eran sanados.
rows.current_english_pob: And wherever he entered villages or cities or countryside, they were laying the sick in the marketplaces and begged him that they might even touch the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched it were being healed.
rows.spanish_base_english: And wherever he entered villages or cities or countryside, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged him that they might even touch the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched him were being healed.

rows.spanish: Y, llamando de nuevo a la multitud, les dijo: «Escúchenme, todos ustedes, y entiendan».
rows.current_english_pob: And calling the crowd to him again, he was saying to them, “Listen to me, all of you, and understand.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And calling the crowd to him again, he said to them, “Listen to me, all of you, and understand.”

rows.spanish: Nada hay fuera de una persona que, al entrar en ella, pueda hacerla impura; sino que las cosas que salen de la persona son las que hacen impura a la persona.
rows.current_english_pob: There is nothing outside a man that by going into him is able to defile him; rather, the things that come out from the man are what defile the man.
rows.spanish_base_english: There is nothing outside a person that by going into him is able to defile him; rather, the things that come out from the person are what defile the person.

rows.spanish: Y decía: «Lo que sale del hombre, eso hace impuro al hombre»
rows.current_english_pob: And he was saying, “What comes out from the man—that defiles the man.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he was saying, “What comes out of the man, that defiles the man.”

rows.spanish: Y la mujer era griega, sirofenicia de origen, y seguía pidiéndole que expulsara al demonio de su hija.
rows.current_english_pob: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by birth, and she kept asking him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by birth, and she kept asking him to cast the demon out of her daughter.

rows.spanish: Y fue a su casa y halló a la niña acostada en la cama, y el demonio ya había salido.
rows.current_english_pob: And when she went away to her house, she found the child lying on the bed, and the demon gone.
rows.spanish_base_english: And she went away to her house and found the child lying on the bed, and the demon gone.

rows.spanish: Había unos cuatro mil, y los despidió.
rows.current_english_pob: There were about four thousand, and he sent them away.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now there were about four thousand, and he sent them away.

rows.spanish: Se habían olvidado de llevar pan y, salvo por un solo pan, no tenían ninguno consigo en la barca.
rows.current_english_pob: And they had forgotten to take bread, and except for one loaf they had no bread with them in the boat.
rows.spanish_base_english: And they had forgotten to take bread, and they had no more than one loaf with them in the boat.

rows.spanish: Y alzando la vista, dijo: «Veo a las personas, porque las veo caminar como árboles».
rows.current_english_pob: And looking up, he said, “I see people, because I see them walking around like trees.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And looking up, he said, “I see people, for I see them like trees, walking around.”

rows.spanish: Entonces volvió a ponerle las manos sobre los ojos; el hombre vio con claridad, quedó restaurado y distinguía todo nítidamente.
rows.current_english_pob: Then again he laid his hands on his eyes, and he saw clearly and was restored, and he was seeing everything distinctly.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then again he laid his hands on his eyes, and he looked intently and was restored, and he began to see everything clearly.

rows.spanish: Y de repente, al mirar alrededor, ya no vieron a nadie, sino solo a Jesús con ellos.
rows.current_english_pob: And suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone except Jesus alone with them.
rows.spanish_base_english: And suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone but Jesus alone with them.

rows.spanish: Pero Jesús lo tomó de la mano, lo levantó, y él se puso de pie.
rows.current_english_pob: But Jesus, taking hold of his hand, raised him up, and he stood up.
rows.spanish_base_english: But Jesus, taking him by the hand, raised him up, and he arose.

rows.spanish: Desde allí siguieron por Galilea, y él no quería que nadie lo supiera.
rows.current_english_pob: And from there they went on through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know.
rows.spanish_base_english: And departing from there, they were passing through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know.

rows.spanish: Y llegaron a Capernaúm. Y cuando estaba en la casa, les preguntó: «¿Qué conversaban en el camino?»
rows.current_english_pob: And they came to Capernaum. And when he was in the house, he was asking them, “What were you discussing on the way?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And they came to Capernaum. And when he was in the house, he asked them, “What were you discussing on the way?”

rows.spanish: Y sentándose, llamó a los doce y les dijo: «Si alguien quiere ser el primero, será el último de todos y servidor de todos».
rows.current_english_pob: And sitting down, he called the twelve and says to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he will be last of all and servant of all.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And sitting down, he called the twelve and said to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he will be last of all and servant of all.”

rows.spanish: Quien reciba a uno de tales niños en mi nombre, a mí me recibe; y quien me reciba, no me recibe a mí, sino al que me envió.
rows.current_english_pob: Whoever receives one of such children in my name receives me; and whoever receives me receives not me, but the one who sent me.
rows.spanish_base_english: Whoever receives one of these children in my name receives me; and whoever receives me receives not me, but the one who sent me.

rows.spanish: Jesús los miró y dijo: «Para los seres humanos es imposible, pero no para Dios, porque para Dios todas las cosas son posibles».
rows.current_english_pob: Jesus looked at them and said, “With men it is impossible, but not with God, because all things are possible with God.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Jesus looked at them and said, “With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.”

rows.spanish: Iban por el camino, subiendo a Jerusalén, y Jesús iba delante de ellos; y se asombraban, mientras los que seguían tenían miedo. Y tomando aparte otra vez a los Doce, comenzó a decirles las cosas que iban a sucederle.
rows.current_english_pob: They were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going ahead of them; and they were astonished, while those who were following were afraid. And taking the Twelve aside again, he began to tell them the things that were about to happen to him.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now they were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going ahead of them; and they were astonished, while those who were following were afraid. And taking the Twelve aside again, he began to tell them the things that were about to happen to him.

rows.spanish: Ellos le dijeron: «Concédenos que uno se siente a tu derecha y otro a tu izquierda en tu gloria».
rows.current_english_pob: They said to him, “Grant to us that one of us may sit at your right and one at your left in your glory.”
rows.spanish_base_english: They said to him, “Grant us that one may sit at your right and one at your left in your glory.”

rows.spanish: Y cualquiera que quiera ser el primero entre ustedes será esclavo de todos.
rows.current_english_pob: And whoever wants to be first among you will be the servant of all.
rows.spanish_base_english: And whoever wants to be first among you will be the slave of all.

rows.spanish: Y respondiéndole, Jesús dijo: «¿Qué quieres que haga por ti?». Y el ciego le dijo: «Rabboni, para que recobre la vista».
rows.current_english_pob: And answering him, Jesus said, “What do you want me to do for you?” And the blind man said to him, “Rabboni, that I may see again.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And answering him, Jesus said, “What do you want me to do for you?” And the blind man said to him, “Rabboni, that I may see again.”

rows.spanish: Y cuando se acercan a Jerusalén, a Betfagé y Betania, hacia el Monte de los Olivos, envía a dos de sus discípulos.
rows.current_english_pob: And when they were approaching Jerusalem, at Bethphage and Bethany, near the Mount of Olives, he sends two of his disciples
rows.spanish_base_english: And when they draw near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, toward the Mount of Olives, he sends two of his disciples

rows.spanish: Y trajeron el pollino a Jesús, y pusieron sobre él sus mantos, y se sentó sobre él.
rows.current_english_pob: And they brought the colt to Jesus, and they threw their cloaks on it, and he sat on it.
rows.spanish_base_english: And they brought the colt to Jesus, and they put their cloaks on it, and he sat on it.

rows.spanish: Y muchos extendieron sus mantos sobre el camino, y otros extendieron ramas cortadas de los campos.
rows.current_english_pob: And many spread their cloaks on the road, and others spread leafy branches cut from the fields.
rows.spanish_base_english: And many spread their cloaks on the road, and others spread branches cut from the fields.

rows.spanish: Y al día siguiente, cuando habían salido de Betania, tuvo hambre.
rows.current_english_pob: And on the next day, when they had gone out from Bethany, he was hungry.
rows.spanish_base_english: And on the next day, when they had gone out from Bethany, he became hungry.

rows.spanish: En verdad les digo: quien diga a este monte: «Sé quitado y sé arrojado al mar», y no duda en su corazón, sino que cree que lo que dice sucederá, así será para él.
rows.current_english_pob: Truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and be thrown into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says is happening, it will be so for him.
rows.spanish_base_english: Truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be taken up and be thrown into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says will happen, it will be so for him.

rows.spanish: Y al tiempo oportuno envió a un esclavo a los viñadores, para que recibiera de los viñadores parte del fruto de la viña.
rows.current_english_pob: And at the proper time he sent a servant to the vine-growers, so that he might receive from the vine-growers some of the fruit of the vineyard.
rows.spanish_base_english: And at the proper time he sent a slave to the vine-growers, so that he might receive from the vine-growers some of the fruit of the vineyard.

rows.spanish: Y los saduceos vinieron a Jesús, que dicen que no hay resurrección, y le preguntaron, diciendo:
rows.current_english_pob: And Sadducees came to him, who say there is no resurrection, and they began questioning him, saying,
rows.spanish_base_english: And Sadducees came to him, who say there is no resurrection, and they questioned him, saying,

rows.spanish: Y uno de los escribas se acercó, y al oírlos debatir, viendo que les había respondido bien, le preguntó: «¿Cuál es el mandamiento primero de todos?»
rows.current_english_pob: And one of the scribes came up and heard them debating, and seeing that he had answered them well, he asked him, “Which commandment is the first of all?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And one of the scribes came up and heard them debating, and seeing that he had answered them well, he asked him, “Which commandment is first of all?”

rows.spanish: David mismo dijo en el Espíritu Santo: «Yahvé dijo a mi Señor: “Siéntate a mi derecha hasta que ponga a tus enemigos debajo de tus pies”».
rows.current_english_pob: David himself said in the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet.”’
rows.spanish_base_english: David himself said in the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet.”’

rows.spanish: Y mientras estaba sentado en el Monte de los Olivos, enfrente del templo, Pedro, Santiago, Juan y Andrés le preguntaron en privado.
rows.current_english_pob: And as he was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew were asking him privately,
rows.spanish_base_english: And as he was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately,

rows.spanish: Y primero es necesario que la buena noticia sea proclamada a todas las naciones.
rows.current_english_pob: And the good news must first be proclaimed to all the nations.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the good news must first be proclaimed to all the nations.

rows.spanish: Ahora aprendan la parábola de la higuera: cuando su rama ya se ha vuelto tierna y echa hojas, saben que el verano está cerca.
rows.current_english_pob: Learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.

rows.spanish: Es como un hombre de viaje, que dejó su casa y dio autoridad a sus esclavos, a cada uno su trabajo, y mandó al portero que velara.
rows.current_english_pob: It is like a man away on a journey, who left his house and gave authority to his servants, to each one his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to stay awake.
rows.spanish_base_english: It is like a man away on a journey, who left his house and gave authority to his slaves, to each one his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to stay awake.

rows.spanish: no sea que venga de repente y los encuentre durmiendo.
rows.current_english_pob: lest, coming suddenly, he find you sleeping.
rows.spanish_base_english: lest he come suddenly and find you sleeping.

rows.spanish: Faltaban dos días para la Pascua y los panes sin levadura. Y los principales sacerdotes y los escribas buscaban cómo, con engaño, prenderlo y matarlo.
rows.current_english_pob: The Passover and Unleavened Bread were two days away. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how, by deceit, they might arrest him and kill him,
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the Passover and Unleavened Bread were two days away. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how, by deceit, they might arrest him and kill him,

rows.spanish: Ahora el que lo entregaba les había dado una señal, diciendo: «Aquel a quien yo bese, ese es. Préndanlo y llévenselo bien asegurado».
rows.current_english_pob: The one betraying him had given them a signal, saying, “The one I kiss is he. Seize him and lead him away securely.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the one betraying him had given them a signal, saying, “The one I kiss is he. Seize him and lead him away securely.”

rows.spanish: Pero uno de los que estaban cerca desenvainó la espada y golpeó al esclavo del sumo sacerdote, y le cortó la oreja.
rows.current_english_pob: But one of those standing nearby drew his sword and struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his ear.
rows.spanish_base_english: But one of those standing nearby drew his sword and struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his ear.

rows.spanish: Y Pedro le siguió desde lejos, hasta el patio del sumo sacerdote, y estaba sentado con los guardias y calentándose junto al fuego.
rows.current_english_pob: And Peter followed him from a distance, as far as inside the courtyard of the high priest. He was sitting with the officers and warming himself by the fire.
rows.spanish_base_english: And Peter followed him from a distance, as far as the courtyard of the high priest, and he was sitting with the officers and warming himself by the fire.

rows.spanish: Ahora los principales sacerdotes y todo el consejo buscaban testimonio contra Jesús con el fin de darle muerte, pero no lo encontraban.
rows.current_english_pob: The chief priests and the whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus in order to put him to death, and they were not finding any.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the chief priests and the whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus in order to put him to death, but they were not finding any.

rows.spanish: Y levantándose el sumo sacerdote en medio, le preguntó a Jesús: «¿No respondes nada? ¿Qué testifican estos hombres contra ti?»
rows.current_english_pob: And the high priest stood up in the middle and questioned Jesus, saying, “Do you answer nothing? What are these men testifying against you?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And the high priest stood up in the midst and questioned Jesus, saying, “Do you answer nothing? What are these men testifying against you?”
