rows.spanish: Y al ver a Pedro calentándose, le miró fijamente y le dijo: «Tú también estabas con Jesús el Nazareno».
rows.current_english_pob: And seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him and says, “You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said, “You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.”

rows.spanish: Pero Pilato volvió a preguntarle, diciendo: «¿No respondes nada? Mira cuántas acusaciones presentan contra ti.»
rows.current_english_pob: But Pilate again questioned him, saying, “Do you give no answer? Look how many charges they are bringing against you.”
rows.spanish_base_english: But Pilate again questioned him, saying, “Do you give no answer? See how many charges they bring against you.”

rows.spanish: Ahora, en la fiesta, les soltaba a un preso, al que pedían.
rows.current_english_pob: At the feast he would release for them one prisoner whom they asked for.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now at the feast he would release for them one prisoner whom they asked for.

rows.spanish: Ahora el hombre llamado Barrabás estaba detenido con los rebeldes que habían cometido asesinato en la rebelión.
rows.current_english_pob: The man called Barabbas was bound with the rebels who had committed murder in the rebellion.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the man called Barabbas was bound with the rebels who had committed murder in the rebellion.

rows.spanish: Y cuando se burlaron de él, le quitaron la púrpura y le pusieron sus propias ropas. Y lo sacaron para crucificarlo.
rows.current_english_pob: And when they had mocked him, they stripped the purple robe off him and put his own clothes on him. And they lead him out to crucify him.
rows.spanish_base_english: And when they had mocked him, they stripped the purple robe off him and put his own clothes on him. And they led him out to crucify him.

rows.spanish: Era ya la tercera hora, y lo crucificaron.
rows.current_english_pob: It was the third hour, and they crucified him.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now it was the third hour, and they crucified him.

rows.spanish: Cuando el centurión, que estaba de pie frente a él, vio que expiró así, dijo: «Verdaderamente, este hombre era Hijo de Dios»
rows.current_english_pob: When the centurion, who was standing opposite him, saw that he breathed his last in this way, he said, “Truly this man was God's Son.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when the centurion, who was standing opposite him, saw that he breathed his last in this way, he said, “Truly this man was God's Son.”

rows.spanish: Y entrando en el sepulcro, vieron a un joven sentado a la derecha, vestido con una vestidura blanca, y quedaron alarmadas.
rows.current_english_pob: And when they entered the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right, clothed in a white robe, and they were alarmed.
rows.spanish_base_english: And entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right, clothed in a white robe, and they were alarmed.

rows.spanish: Después de resucitar, muy temprano el primer día de la semana, apareció primero a María Magdalena, de quien había expulsado siete demonios.
rows.current_english_pob: After he had risen, early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now after he had risen, early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.

rows.spanish: Libro de la genealogía de Jesús, el Mesías, hijo de David, hijo de Abraham.
rows.current_english_pob: The book of the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
rows.spanish_base_english: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, el nacimiento de Jesús Mesías ocurrió así: cuando su madre María había sido desposada con José, antes de que ellos se unieran, se halló encinta del Espíritu Santo.
rows.current_english_pob: The birth of Jesus the Messiah happened in this way: when his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now the birth of Jesus Messiah happened in this way: when his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be pregnant from the Holy Spirit.

rows.spanish: Pero mientras él consideraba estas cosas, he aquí, un ángel de Yahvé se le apareció en sueños, diciendo: «José, hijo de David, no temas tomar contigo a María, tu esposa, porque lo que ha sido concebido en ella proviene del Espíritu Santo». O, «tomar a María, tu esposa». La expresión griega se refiere a recibirla en tu casa como esposa dentro del matrimonio.
rows.current_english_pob: But as he was considering these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for what has been conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.”
rows.spanish_base_english: But as he was considering these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary your wife, for what has been conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.”

rows.spanish: Ahora todo esto sucedió para que se cumpliera lo que fue dicho por el Señor mediante el profeta, diciendo,
rows.current_english_pob: All this happened so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
rows.spanish_base_english: Now all this happened so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,

rows.spanish: He aquí, la virgen concebirá y dará a luz un hijo, y le pondrán por nombre Emanuel, que traducido significa: «Dios con nosotros».
rows.current_english_pob: Behold, the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and they will call his name Immanuel—which is translated, 'God with us.'
rows.spanish_base_english: Behold, the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and they will call his name Immanuel—which is translated, 'God with us.'

rows.spanish: Después de que nació Jesús en Belén de Judea, en los días de Herodes el rey, he aquí unos magos del oriente llegaron a Jerusalén,
rows.current_english_pob: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, wise men from the east arrived in Jerusalem,
rows.spanish_base_english: Now after Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, wise men from the east arrived in Jerusalem,

rows.spanish: Y ellos le dijeron: «En Belén de Judea, porque así está escrito por medio del profeta:»
rows.current_english_pob: And they said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for thus it has been written through the prophet:
rows.spanish_base_english: And they said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for thus it has been written through the prophet:”

rows.spanish: Entonces Herodes mandó llamar en secreto a los magos y averiguó de ellos con exactitud el tiempo en que había aparecido la estrella.
rows.current_english_pob: Then Herod secretly summoned the magi and determined from them the exact time when the star had appeared,
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Herod secretly summoned the magi and determined from them the time when the star had appeared,

rows.spanish: Después de oír al rey, se pusieron en camino; y he aquí, la estrella que habían visto en el oriente iba delante de ellos hasta que llegó y se detuvo encima de donde estaba el niño.
rows.current_english_pob: After hearing the king, they went on their way, and behold, the star that they had seen in the east went before them until it came and stood over where the child was.
rows.spanish_base_english: After hearing the king, they went on their way, and behold, the star that they had seen in the east went before them until it came and stood over where the child was.

rows.spanish: Y al entrar en la casa, vieron al niño con María, su madre, y postrándose le rindieron homenaje; y abriendo sus tesoros, le ofrecieron dones: oro, franquincienso y mirra.
rows.current_english_pob: And when they came into the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother, and falling down they paid homage to him, and opening their treasure chests they offered him gifts: gold and frankincense and myrrh.
rows.spanish_base_english: And when they came into the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother, and falling down they paid homage to him, and opening their treasures they offered him gifts: gold and frankincense and myrrh.

rows.spanish: Después de que se fueron, he aquí, un ángel de Yahvé se le apareció a José en un sueño, diciendo: «Levántate, toma al niño y a su madre, y huye a Egipto, y quédate allí hasta que yo te diga; porque Herodes está por buscar al niño para destruirlo».
rows.current_english_pob: After they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you; for Herod is about to seek the child in order to destroy him.”
rows.spanish_base_english: After they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you; for Herod is about to seek the child in order to destroy him.”

rows.spanish: y estuvo allí hasta la muerte de Herodes, para que se cumpliera lo que fue dicho por el Señor por medio del profeta, diciendo: «De Egipto llamé a mi hijo».
rows.current_english_pob: and was there until the death of Herod, so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled: “Out of Egypt I called my son.”
rows.spanish_base_english: and was there until the death of Herod, so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, “Out of Egypt I called my son.”

rows.spanish: Entonces Herodes, al ver que había sido burlado por los magos, se enojó mucho y, enviando hombres, mató a todos los niños varones que había en Belén y en todos sus alrededores, de dos años para abajo, conforme al tiempo que había averiguado de los magos.
rows.current_english_pob: Then Herod, seeing that he had been tricked by the magi, became very angry, and sending men, he killed all the boys in Bethlehem and in all its surrounding districts, from two years old and under, according to the exact time he had determined from the magi.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Herod, seeing that he had been tricked by the magi, became very angry, and sending men, he killed all the boys in Bethlehem and in all its surrounding districts, from two years old and under, according to the time that he had determined from the magi.

rows.spanish: Se oyó una voz en Ramá, llanto y gran lamento: Raquel, llorando por sus hijos, no quería ser consolada, porque ya no están.
rows.current_english_pob: A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and great mourning: Rachel weeping for her children, and she refused to be comforted, because they are no more.
rows.spanish_base_english: A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and great mourning: Rachel weeping for her children, and she was not willing to be comforted, because they are no more.

rows.spanish: Pero después de que Herodes murió, he aquí un ángel del Señor aparece en un sueño a José en Egipto.
rows.current_english_pob: But after Herod died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt.
rows.spanish_base_english: But after Herod died, behold, an angel of the Lord appears in a dream to Joseph in Egypt.

rows.spanish: En aquellos días vino Juan el Bautista, predicando en el desierto de Judea.
rows.current_english_pob: In those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea,
rows.spanish_base_english: Now in those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea,

rows.spanish: Juan mismo vestía ropa de pelo de camello y un cinturón de cuero alrededor de su cintura, y su alimento eran saltamontes y miel silvestre.
rows.current_english_pob: John himself wore clothing made of camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now John himself wore clothing made of camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.

rows.spanish: Yo, en efecto, los bautizo con agua para arrepentimiento, pero el que viene detrás de mí es más fuerte que yo, de quien no soy digno de llevar sus sandalias. Él mismo los bautizará en el Espíritu Santo y fuego.
rows.current_english_pob: I indeed baptize you in water for repentance, but the one coming after me is stronger than I. I am not worthy to carry his sandals. He himself will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire.
rows.spanish_base_english: I indeed baptize you in water for repentance, but the one coming after me is stronger than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He himself will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire.

rows.spanish: Pero Juan seguía tratando de impedírselo, diciendo: «Yo necesito ser bautizado por ti, ¿y tú vienes a mí?»
rows.current_english_pob: But John tried to prevent him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?”
rows.spanish_base_english: But John kept trying to prevent him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?”

rows.spanish: Y cuando Jesús fue bautizado, subió inmediatamente del agua. Y he aquí, los cielos se abrieron, y vio al Espíritu de Dios descendiendo como una paloma y que venía sobre él.
rows.current_english_pob: And when Jesus was baptized, he immediately came up from the water. And behold, the heavens were opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him.
rows.spanish_base_english: And when Jesus was baptized, he immediately came up from the water. And behold, the heavens were opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí una voz desde los cielos, que decía: «Este es mi Hijo amado, en quien me complazco».
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, a voice from the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, a voice from the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”

rows.spanish: Pero él respondió: «Escrito está: “No solo de pan vivirá el ser humano, sino de toda palabra que sale de la boca de Dios”».
rows.current_english_pob: But he answered, “It is written: ‘Man will not live by bread alone, but by every word proceeding through the mouth of God.’”
rows.spanish_base_english: But he answered, “It is written: ‘Man will not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God.’”

rows.spanish: Entonces Jesús le dice: «¡Vete, Satanás! Porque está escrito: “A Yahvé tu Dios adorarás, y solo a él servirás”»
rows.current_english_pob: Then Jesus says to him, “Go away, Satan! For it is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him only.’”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Jesus says to him, “Go away, Satan! For it is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve only him.’”

rows.spanish: Entonces el diablo lo dejó, y he aquí, ángeles se acercaron y le ministraban.
rows.current_english_pob: Then the devil left him, and behold, angels came and were ministering to him.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then the devil left him, and behold, angels came and were ministering to him.

rows.spanish: Al oír que Juan había sido entregado, se retiró a Galilea.
rows.current_english_pob: When he heard that John had been handed over, he withdrew into Galilee.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when he heard that John had been handed over, he withdrew into Galilee.

rows.spanish: para que se cumpliera lo dicho por medio de Isaías el profeta, diciendo:
rows.current_english_pob: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:
rows.spanish_base_english: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:

rows.spanish: Y ellos inmediatamente dejaron las redes y le siguieron.
rows.current_english_pob: And they immediately left their nets and followed him.
rows.spanish_base_english: And they immediately left the nets and followed him.

rows.spanish: Porque en verdad les digo, hasta que pasen el cielo y la tierra, ni una iota ni un solo trazo pasará de la ley, hasta que todo suceda.
rows.current_english_pob: For truly I say to you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke will ever pass away from the law until all is accomplished.
rows.spanish_base_english: For truly I say to you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke will ever pass away from the law until all things happen.

rows.spanish: Por tanto, si estás presentando tu ofrenda ante el altar, y allí recuerdas que tu hermano tiene algo contra ti,
rows.current_english_pob: Therefore, if you are offering your gift on the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you,
rows.spanish_base_english: Therefore, if you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you,

rows.spanish: Mantente bien dispuesto hacia tu acusador rápidamente, mientras estás con él en el camino, no sea que tu acusador te entregue al juez, y el juez al oficial, y seas arrojado a la cárcel.
rows.current_english_pob: Come to terms with your accuser quickly, while you are with him on the way, lest your accuser hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.
rows.spanish_base_english: Be well-disposed toward your accuser quickly, while you are with him on the way, lest your accuser hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.

rows.spanish: Pero yo les digo: no juren en absoluto; ni por el cielo, porque es el trono de Dios.
rows.current_english_pob: But I say to you, do not swear at all: neither by heaven, because it is the throne of God;
rows.spanish_base_english: But I say to you, do not swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;

rows.spanish: Pero cuando des a los necesitados, no sepa tu mano izquierda lo que hace tu mano derecha,
rows.current_english_pob: But when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
rows.spanish_base_english: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

rows.spanish: Pero cuando ores, entra en tu cuarto interior, y después de cerrar tu puerta, ora a tu Padre, que está en lo oculto; y tu Padre, que ve en lo oculto, te recompensará.
rows.current_english_pob: But you, when you pray, go into your inner room, and after shutting your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
rows.spanish_base_english: But when you pray, go into your inner room, and after shutting your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.

rows.spanish: Por tanto, oren así: Padre nuestro en los cielos, sea considerado santo tu nombre.
rows.current_english_pob: Therefore, pray like this: Our Father in the heavens, may your name be treated as holy,
rows.spanish_base_english: Therefore, you should pray like this: Our Father in the heavens, may your name be treated as holy,

rows.spanish: Y cuando ayunen, no sean sombríos como los hipócritas, porque desfiguran sus rostros para mostrarle a la gente que ayunan. En verdad les digo: ya han recibido su recompensa.
rows.current_english_pob: And whenever you fast, do not look gloomy like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to people to be fasting. Truly I say to you, they have received their reward in full.
rows.spanish_base_english: And whenever you fast, do not become gloomy like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to people to be fasting. Truly I say to you, they have received their reward in full.

rows.spanish: Porque los gentiles buscan todas estas cosas; porque su Padre celestial sabe que ustedes necesitan todas estas cosas.
rows.current_english_pob: For the Gentiles eagerly seek all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
rows.spanish_base_english: For the Gentiles seek all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.

rows.spanish: Por tanto, no se preocupen por mañana, porque mañana se preocupará por sí mismo. Cada día tiene ya sus propios problemas.
rows.current_english_pob: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
rows.spanish_base_english: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble.

rows.spanish: ¿O cómo le dirás a tu hermano: «Déjame sacar la mota de tu ojo», y he aquí, la viga está en tu propio ojo?
rows.current_english_pob: Or how will you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye?
rows.spanish_base_english: Or how will you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye?

rows.spanish: ¿O qué hombre hay entre ustedes a quien su hijo le pide pan? ¿Acaso le dará una piedra?
rows.current_english_pob: Or what man is there among you whom his son asks for bread—he will not give him a stone, will he?
rows.spanish_base_english: Or what man is there among you whose son asks him for bread, and he will give him a stone?

rows.spanish: Si ustedes, pues, siendo malos, saben dar buenos dones a sus hijos, ¡cuánto más su Padre en los cielos dará cosas buenas a los que le piden!
rows.current_english_pob: If you, then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in the heavens give good things to those who ask him?
rows.spanish_base_english: If you, then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in the heavens give good things to those who ask him.

rows.spanish: Porque estrecha es la puerta y difícil el camino que lleva a la vida, y pocos son los que la hallan.
rows.current_english_pob: For the gate is narrow and the way that leads to life is hard, and few are those who find it.
rows.spanish_base_english: For the gate is narrow and the way that leads to life is constricted, and few are those who find it.

rows.spanish: Así, todo árbol bueno produce fruto bueno, pero el árbol podrido produce fruto malo.
rows.current_english_pob: So, every good tree produces good fruit, but the bad tree produces bad fruit.
rows.spanish_base_english: So, every good tree produces good fruit, but the rotten tree produces bad fruit.

rows.spanish: No todos los que me dicen: «Señor, Señor» entrarán en el reino de los cielos, sino el que hace la voluntad de mi Padre que está en los cielos entrará.
rows.current_english_pob: Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven will enter.
rows.spanish_base_english: Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven will enter.

rows.spanish: Cayó la lluvia, vinieron los ríos, soplaron los vientos y golpearon aquella casa; esta cayó, y grande fue su caída.
rows.current_english_pob: And the rain came down, and the rivers came, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell—and its fall was great.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the rain came down, and the rivers came, and the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell—and great was its fall.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí un leproso se acercó y se postró ante él, diciendo: «Señor, si quieres, puedes limpiarme».
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, a leper came and bowed down before him, saying, “Lord, if you are willing, you are able to cleanse me.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, a leper came and bowed down before him, saying, “Lord, if you are willing, you are able to cleanse me.”

rows.spanish: Y cuando Jesús entró en la casa de Pedro, vio a la suegra de Pedro acostada y con fiebre.
rows.current_english_pob: And when Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his mother-in-law lying in bed with a fever.
rows.spanish_base_english: And when Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his mother-in-law lying down and having a fever.

rows.spanish: Y le tocó la mano, y la fiebre la dejó, y ella se levantó y le sirvió.
rows.current_english_pob: And he touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she got up and began serving him.
rows.spanish_base_english: And he touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she got up and served him.

rows.spanish: Cuando Jesús vio una multitud alrededor de él, dio órdenes de ir al otro lado.
rows.current_english_pob: When Jesus saw a crowd around him, he gave orders to go to the other side.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when Jesus saw many crowds around him, he gave orders to depart to the other side.

rows.spanish: Y acercándose un escriba, le dijo: «Maestro, te seguiré adondequiera que vayas».
rows.current_english_pob: And a scribe came up and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And one scribe came up and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, se levantó un gran temporal sobre el mar, de modo que la barca era cubierta por las olas; pero él dormía.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was being swamped by the waves; but he was sleeping.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was being swamped by the waves; but he was sleeping.

rows.spanish: Y les dijo: «¿Por qué están ustedes asustados, ustedes de poca fe?» Entonces, habiéndose levantado, reprendió a los vientos y al mar, y hubo una gran calma.
rows.current_english_pob: And he said to them, “Why are you fearful, you of little faith?” Then he got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said to them, “Why are you afraid, you of little faith?” Then, having risen, he rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, clamaron, diciendo: «¿Qué tenemos nosotros que ver contigo, Hijo de Dios? ¿Has venido aquí antes del tiempo señalado para atormentarnos?»
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, they cried out, saying, “What have we to do with you, Son of God? Have you come here before the appointed time to torment us?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, they cried out, saying, “What have we to do with you, Son of God? Have you come here before the appointed time to torment us?”

rows.spanish: Había a cierta distancia de ellos una gran manada de cerdos que se estaba alimentando.
rows.current_english_pob: A large herd of pigs was feeding some distance away from them.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now a large herd of pigs was feeding some distance away from them.

rows.spanish: Y les dijo: «Vayan». Entonces salieron y entraron en los cerdos; y he aquí, toda la piara se precipitó por la pendiente escarpada hacia el mar, y murieron en las aguas.
rows.current_english_pob: And he said to them, “Go.” Then they came out and went into the pigs; and behold, the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the waters.
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said to them, “Go.” Then they came out and went into the pigs; and behold, the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the waters.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, toda la ciudad salió al encuentro de Jesús, y cuando lo vieron, le rogaron que se fuera de su región.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, the whole city went out to meet Jesus, and when they saw him, they begged him to depart from their region.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, the whole city went out to meet Jesus, and when they saw him, they begged him to depart from their region.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, le trajeron un paralítico acostado en una cama. Cuando Jesús vio la fe de ellos, le dijo al paralítico: «Ten ánimo, niño; tus pecados son perdonados».
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, they brought to him a paralytic lying on a bed. And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Take courage, child; your sins are forgiven.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, they brought to him a paralytic lying on a bed. And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Take courage, child; your sins are forgiven.”

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, algunos de los escribas se dijeron entre sí: «Este hombre blasfema».
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man is blaspheming.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, some of the scribes said among themselves, “This man is blaspheming.”

rows.spanish: Porque, ¿qué es más fácil: decir: «Tus pecados te son perdonados», o decir: «Levántate y camina»?
rows.current_english_pob: For which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
rows.spanish_base_english: For which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?”

rows.spanish: Pero para que sepan que el Hijo del Hombre tiene autoridad en la tierra para perdonar pecados”—entonces le dice al paralítico: “Levántate, recoge tu cama y vete a tu casa.”
rows.current_english_pob: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—then he said to the paralytic, “Get up, pick up your bed, and go to your house.”
rows.spanish_base_english: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—then he says to the paralytic, “Get up, pick up your bed, and go to your house.”

rows.spanish: Y se levantó y se fue a su casa.
rows.current_english_pob: And he got up and went home.
rows.spanish_base_english: And he got up and went away to his house.

rows.spanish: Y mientras él estaba a la mesa en la casa, he aquí que muchos recaudadores de impuestos y pecadores vinieron y se pusieron a la mesa con Jesús y sus discípulos.
rows.current_english_pob: And as he was reclining at table in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and were reclining at table with Jesus and his disciples.
rows.spanish_base_english: And as he was reclining at table in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and were reclining at table with Jesus and his disciples.

rows.spanish: Y al ver esto los fariseos, decían a sus discípulos: “¿Por qué come su maestro con cobradores de impuestos y pecadores?”
rows.current_english_pob: And when the Pharisees saw it, they said to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And when the Pharisees saw it, they were saying to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

rows.spanish: Pero nadie pone un parche de tela sin encoger sobre una prenda vieja, porque el parche se arranca de la prenda, y resulta una rasgadura peor.
rows.current_english_pob: But no one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, for the patch pulls away from the garment, and a worse tear results.
rows.spanish_base_english: But no one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, for the patch tears away from the garment, and a worse tear results.

rows.spanish: Mientras él les hablaba estas cosas, he aquí, vino un jefe y se postró ante él, diciendo: «Mi hija acaba de morir. Pero ven y pon tu mano sobre ella, y vivirá».
rows.current_english_pob: While he was saying these things to them, look, a ruler came and bowed down before him, saying, “My daughter has just died. But come and lay your hand on her, and she will live.”
rows.spanish_base_english: While he was saying these things to them, behold, a ruler came and bowed down before him, saying, “My daughter has just died. But come and lay your hand on her, and she will live.”

rows.spanish: Y Jesús se levantó y lo siguió, y sus discípulos también siguieron.
rows.current_english_pob: And Jesus rose and followed him, and his disciples did too.
rows.spanish_base_english: And Jesus rose and followed him, and his disciples followed too.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí una mujer que sufría de hemorragias desde hacía doce años se acercó por detrás y tocó el borde de su prenda.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, a woman who had been suffering from bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the fringe of his garment.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, a woman who had been suffering from bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the fringe of his garment.

rows.spanish: Pero Jesús, volviéndose y viéndola, dijo: «Ten ánimo, hija; tu fe te ha salvado.» Y la mujer fue sanada desde aquella hora.
rows.current_english_pob: But Jesus, turning and seeing her, said, “Take courage, daughter; your faith has made you well.” And the woman was made well from that hour.
rows.spanish_base_english: But Jesus, turning and seeing her, said, “Take courage, daughter; your faith has saved you.” And the woman was healed from that hour.

rows.spanish: Él decía: «Apártense, porque la niña no ha muerto, sino que duerme». Y se burlaban de él.
rows.current_english_pob: He was saying, “Go away, for the girl is not dead, but is sleeping.” And they were laughing at him.
rows.spanish_base_english: He was saying, “Go away, for the girl has not died, but is sleeping.” And they were laughing at him.

rows.spanish: Mientras salían, he aquí que le trajeron un hombre mudo y endemoniado.
rows.current_english_pob: As they were going out, behold, they brought to him a mute, demon-possessed man.
rows.spanish_base_english: As they were going out, behold, they brought to him a mute, demon-possessed man.

rows.spanish: Y cuando el demonio fue expulsado, el mudo habló. Y las multitudes se maravillaron, diciendo: «Nunca se ha visto algo así en Israel».
rows.current_english_pob: And when the demon had been cast out, the mute man spoke. And the crowds were amazed, saying, “Never has anything like this appeared in Israel.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And when the demon had been cast out, the mute man spoke. And the crowds marveled, saying, “Never has anything like this been seen in Israel.”

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, estos son los nombres de los doce apóstoles: primero, Simón llamado Pedro y Andrés su hermano; Jacobo, el hijo de Zebedeo, y Juan su hermano,
rows.current_english_pob: These are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother,
rows.spanish_base_english: Now these are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother,

rows.spanish: Jesús envió a estos doce, dándoles instrucciones, diciendo: «No vayan por el camino de los gentiles, ni entren en una ciudad de los samaritanos».
rows.current_english_pob: Jesus sent out these twelve, instructing them, saying, “Do not go on any road to the Gentiles, and do not enter a town of the Samaritans.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Jesus sent out these twelve, instructing them, saying, “Do not go on the way of the Gentiles, and do not enter a town of the Samaritans.”

rows.spanish: Miren, yo los envío como ovejas en medio de lobos; por tanto, sean prudentes como las serpientes y inocentes como las palomas.
rows.current_english_pob: Look, I am sending you out as sheep in the midst of wolves; therefore be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.
rows.spanish_base_english: Behold, I am sending you out as sheep in the midst of wolves; therefore be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.

rows.spanish: Y serán llevados ante gobernadores y reyes por causa de mí, como testimonio a ellos y a los gentiles.
rows.current_english_pob: And you will even be brought before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
rows.spanish_base_english: And you will be brought before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.

rows.spanish: Un discípulo no está por encima del maestro, ni un esclavo por encima de su amo.
rows.current_english_pob: A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a servant above his master.
rows.spanish_base_english: A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a slave above his master.

rows.spanish: Basta al discípulo que llegue a ser como su maestro, y el esclavo como su amo. Si al dueño de la casa lo llamaron Beelzebul, ¿cuánto más a los de su casa?
rows.current_english_pob: It is enough for the disciple that he become like his teacher, and the servant like his master. If they called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household.
rows.spanish_base_english: It is enough for the disciple that he become like his teacher, and the slave like his master. If they called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household.

rows.spanish: Por tanto, no les tengan miedo, porque nada hay oculto que no será revelado, ni nada escondido que no será dado a conocer.
rows.current_english_pob: Therefore, do not fear them, for nothing is covered that will not be revealed, and hidden that will not be made known.
rows.spanish_base_english: Therefore, do not fear them, for nothing is concealed that will not be revealed, and hidden that will not be made known.

rows.spanish: Lo que yo les digo en la oscuridad, díganlo a la luz; y lo que oyen al oído, proclamen en las azoteas.
rows.current_english_pob: What I tell you in the darkness, say in the light; and what you hear in your ear, proclaim on the housetops.
rows.spanish_base_english: What I tell you in the darkness, say in the light; and what you hear in the ear, proclaim on the housetops.

rows.spanish: Así que a todo el que me reconozca delante de las personas, yo también lo reconoceré delante de mi Padre que está en los cielos.
rows.current_english_pob: Therefore everyone who acknowledges me before people, I also will acknowledge him before my Father who is in heaven.
rows.spanish_base_english: Therefore everyone who confesses me before men, I also will confess before my Father who is in heaven.

rows.spanish: Y Juan, al oír en la prisión acerca de las obras del Mesías, mandó decir por medio de sus discípulos
rows.current_english_pob: When John heard in prison about the works of the Messiah, he sent word through his disciples
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when John heard in prison about the works of the Messiah, he sent word through his disciples

rows.spanish: y le dijo: «¿Eres tú el que ha de venir, o debemos esperar a otro?»
rows.current_english_pob: and said to him, “Are you the Coming One, or should we expect another?”
rows.spanish_base_english: and said to him, “Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect another?”

rows.spanish: Y Jesús les respondió: «Vayan e infórmenle a Juan lo que oyen y ven:»
rows.current_english_pob: And Jesus answered them, “Go and report to John what you hear and see:
rows.spanish_base_english: And Jesus answered them, “Go and report to John what you hear and see:”

rows.spanish: Mientras ellos se iban, Jesús comenzó a hablar a las multitudes acerca de Juan: «¿Qué salieron a ver al desierto: una caña sacudida por el viento?».
rows.current_english_pob: As these men were going away, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed being shaken by the wind?”
rows.spanish_base_english: As these men were going away, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?”

rows.spanish: Este es aquel de quien está escrito: «He aquí, yo envío a mi mensajero delante de tu rostro, el cual preparará tu camino delante de ti».
rows.current_english_pob: This is he about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I am sending my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’
rows.spanish_base_english: This is he about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I am sending my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’

rows.spanish: ¿A qué compararé esta generación? Es como niños sentados en las plazas, que llaman a los otros,
rows.current_english_pob: But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces, who call out to the others,
rows.spanish_base_english: But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces, calling out to the others,

rows.spanish: Pero él les dijo: «¿No han leído lo que hicieron David y los que estaban con él cuando tuvieron hambre?».
rows.current_english_pob: But he said to them, “Have you not read what David and those with him did when they were hungry?”
rows.spanish_base_english: But he said to them, “Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those with him were hungry?”

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, un hombre con una mano marchita. Y le preguntaron, diciendo: «¿Es lícito sanar en sábado?» para acusarlo.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, there was a man with a withered hand. And they asked him, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?” so that they might accuse him.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, there was a man with a withered hand. And they asked him, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbaths?” so that they might accuse him.

rows.spanish: ¡Cuánto más vale, entonces, un hombre que una oveja! Así que es lícito hacer el bien en los sábados.
rows.current_english_pob: How much more valuable, then, is a man than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.
rows.spanish_base_english: How much more valuable, then, is a man than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbaths.

rows.spanish: Pero los fariseos salieron y consultaron entre sí contra él, sobre cómo destruirlo.
rows.current_english_pob: But the Pharisees went out and conspired against him, how they might destroy him.
rows.spanish_base_english: But the Pharisees went out and took counsel against him, how they might destroy him.

rows.spanish: He aquí, mi siervo a quien he escogido, mi amado en quien mi alma se ha deleitado. Pondré mi Espíritu sobre él, y proclamará justicia a las naciones.
rows.current_english_pob: Behold, my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved in whom my soul has delighted. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice to the nations.
rows.spanish_base_english: Behold, my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved in whom my soul has delighted. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice to the nations.

rows.spanish: Los hombres de Nínive se levantarán en el juicio junto con esta generación y la condenarán, porque se arrepintieron ante la proclamación de Jonás, y he aquí, algo mayor que Jonás está aquí.
rows.current_english_pob: The men of Nineveh will rise up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, because they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.
rows.spanish_base_english: The men of Nineveh will rise up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, because they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.

rows.spanish: La reina del Sur se levantará en el juicio con esta generación y la condenará, porque vino de los extremos de la tierra para oír la sabiduría de Salomón, y he aquí, algo mayor que Salomón está aquí.
rows.current_english_pob: The queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.
rows.spanish_base_english: The queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, cuando el espíritu inmundo sale del hombre, pasa por lugares sin agua buscando descanso, y no lo encuentra.
rows.current_english_pob: When the unclean spirit goes out from the man, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and does not find it.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when the unclean spirit goes out from the man, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and does not find it.

rows.spanish: Entonces se va y toma consigo siete otros espíritus, más malvados que él, y, al entrar, habitan allí; y el estado final de aquel hombre llega a ser peor que el primero. Así también será con esta generación mala.
rows.current_english_pob: Then it goes and takes with it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they enter and live there; and the last state of that man becomes worse than the first. So it will be also with this evil generation.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then it goes and brings with itself seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they enter and live there; and the last state of that man becomes worse than the first. So it will be also with this evil generation.

rows.spanish: Mientras él aún hablaba a las multitudes, he aquí, su madre y sus hermanos estaban de pie afuera, buscando hablarle.
rows.current_english_pob: While he was still speaking to the crowds, behold, his mother and his brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak to him.
rows.spanish_base_english: While he was still speaking to the crowds, behold, his mother and his brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak to him.

rows.spanish: Y les habló muchas cosas en parábolas, diciendo: «He aquí, el sembrador salió a sembrar».
rows.current_english_pob: And he spoke many things to them in parables, saying: “Look, the sower went out to sow.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he spoke many things to them in parables, saying: “Behold, the sower went out to sow.”

rows.spanish: Pero otra semilla cayó en la buena tierra y daba fruto: una al ciento por uno, otra al sesenta y otra al treinta.
rows.current_english_pob: But other seed fell on the good soil and was producing fruit—one a hundredfold, another sixty, and another thirty.
rows.spanish_base_english: But other seed fell on the good soil and was producing fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixty, and some thirty.

rows.spanish: Y en ellos se cumple la profecía de Isaías, que dice: «De cierto oirán, pero nunca entenderán; y viendo verán, pero nunca percibirán».
rows.current_english_pob: And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says: ‘You will indeed hear, but never understand, and you will indeed see, but never perceive.’
rows.spanish_base_english: And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says: ‘You will indeed hear, but never understand, and seeing you will see, but never perceive.’

rows.spanish: Y el que fue sembrado entre espinos: este es el que oye la palabra, pero la preocupación de esta era y el engaño de las riquezas ahogan la palabra, y se queda sin fruto.
rows.current_english_pob: And the one sown among the thorns—this is the one who hears the word, but the worries of this age and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the one sown among the thorns—this is the one who hears the word, but the चिंता of this age and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful.

rows.spanish: Pero mientras la gente dormía, vino su enemigo y sembró malezas entre el trigo y se fue.
rows.current_english_pob: But while people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat and went away.
rows.spanish_base_english: But while the people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat and went away.

rows.spanish: Entonces se acercaron los esclavos del dueño de la casa y le dijeron: «Señor, ¿no sembraste buena semilla en tu campo? ¿De dónde, pues, salen las malas hierbas?»
rows.current_english_pob: So the servants of the master of the house came to him and said, ‘Lord, did you not sow good seed in your field? Where then do the weeds come from?’
rows.spanish_base_english: So the slaves of the master of the house came to him and said, ‘Lord, did you not sow good seed in your field? Where then do the weeds come from?’

rows.spanish: Les dijo: «Un enemigo hizo esto». Entonces los esclavos le dijeron: «¿Quieres, entonces, que vayamos y los recojamos?»
rows.current_english_pob: He said to them, “An enemy did this.” Then the servants said to him, “So do you want us to go and gather them up?”
rows.spanish_base_english: He said to them, “An enemy did this.” Then the slaves said to him, “Do you want us to go and gather them up?”

rows.spanish: Es, en verdad, menor que todas las semillas, pero cuando ha crecido, es mayor que las plantas del huerto y se convierte en árbol, de modo que las aves del cielo vienen y anidan en sus ramas.
rows.current_english_pob: It is indeed the smallest of all seeds, but when it has grown, it is larger than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches.
rows.spanish_base_english: It is indeed smaller than all the seeds, but when it has grown, it is larger than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches.

rows.spanish: de modo que se cumpliera lo que fue dicho por medio del profeta, cuando dijo: «Abriré mi boca en parábolas; declararé cosas escondidas desde la fundación.»
rows.current_english_pob: so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the beginning.”
rows.spanish_base_english: so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.”

rows.spanish: Entonces los justos resplandecerán como el sol en el reino de su Padre. El que tiene oídos, que oiga.
rows.current_english_pob: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. The one who has ears, let him hear.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He who has ears, let him hear.

rows.spanish: Otra vez, el reino de los cielos es semejante a una red de arrastre echada al mar y que recoge de toda clase.
rows.current_english_pob: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet cast into the sea and gathering fish of every kind.
rows.spanish_base_english: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet cast into the sea and gathering from every kind.

rows.spanish: Cuando se llenó, la arrastraron hasta la orilla, se sentaron y recogieron los buenos en recipientes, pero echaron fuera los podridos.
rows.current_english_pob: When it was filled, they pulled it up onto the shore, sat down, and gathered the good fish into containers, but threw the bad ones out.
rows.spanish_base_english: When it was filled, they pulled it up onto the shore, sat down, and gathered the good fish into containers, but threw the rotten ones out.

rows.spanish: Y al llegar a su pueblo natal, les enseñaba en su sinagoga, de modo que ellos se asombraban y decían: «¿De dónde saca este hombre esta sabiduría y estos poderes?»
rows.current_english_pob: And coming to his hometown, he was teaching them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And coming to his hometown, he was teaching them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these powers?”

rows.spanish: Pero cuando llegó el cumpleaños de Herodes, la hija de Herodías danzó en medio y agradó a Herodes.
rows.current_english_pob: But when Herod’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced before them and pleased Herod,
rows.spanish_base_english: But when Herod’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in the midst and pleased Herod,

rows.spanish: Ella, impulsada por su madre, dijo: «Dame aquí, en una bandeja, la cabeza de Juan el Bautizador».
rows.current_english_pob: And she, prompted by her mother, said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptizer.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And she, having been prompted by her mother, says, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.”

rows.spanish: Al oír esto, Jesús se retiró de allí en barca a un lugar desierto, para estar a solas. Pero cuando las multitudes oyeron, lo siguieron a pie desde los pueblos.
rows.current_english_pob: When Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there by boat to a desolate place by himself. But when the crowds heard, they followed him on foot from the towns.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there by boat to a desolate place by himself. But when the crowds heard, they followed him on foot from the towns.

rows.spanish: Ya al anochecer, los discípulos se acercaron a él y le dijeron: «El lugar está desierto, y ya es tarde. Despide a las multitudes, para que vayan a las aldeas y compren comida para sí mismos».
rows.current_english_pob: When evening came, the disciples came to him and said, “The place is deserted, and the hour is already late. Send the crowds away, so that they may go into the villages and buy food for themselves.”
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when evening came, the disciples came to him and said, “The place is deserted, and the hour is already late. Send the crowds away, so that they may go into the villages and buy food for themselves.”

rows.spanish: Ahora los que comieron eran unos cinco mil hombres, además de las mujeres y los niños.
rows.current_english_pob: Those who ate were about five thousand men, besides women and children.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now those who ate were about five thousand men, besides women and children.

rows.spanish: Y enseguida obligó a los discípulos a subir a la barca y adelantarse a él a la otra orilla, hasta que despidiera a las multitudes.
rows.current_english_pob: And immediately he compelled the disciples to get into the boat and go on ahead of him to the other side, while he dismissed the crowds.
rows.spanish_base_english: And immediately he compelled the disciples to get into the boat and go on ahead of him to the other side, until he should dismiss the crowds.

rows.spanish: Pero ustedes dicen: «Quien diga a su padre o a su madre: “Cualquier cosa con la que yo pudiera ayudarte es un regalo”».
rows.current_english_pob: But you say, ‘Whoever says to his father or his mother, “Whatever you would have benefited from me is a gift to God,”’
rows.spanish_base_english: But you say, ‘Whoever says to his father or his mother, “Whatever you would have benefited from me is a gift,”’

rows.spanish: Entonces los discípulos se acercaron y le dijeron: «¿Sabes que los fariseos se ofendieron al oír esas palabras?»
rows.current_english_pob: Then the disciples came and said to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this saying?”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then the disciples came and said to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this word?”

rows.spanish: Estas son las cosas que contaminan al hombre, pero comer con manos no lavadas no contamina al hombre.
rows.current_english_pob: These are the things that defile a man, but to eat with unwashed hands does not defile the man.
rows.spanish_base_english: These are the things that defile the man, but to eat with unwashed hands does not defile the man.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí que una mujer cananea salió de aquellas regiones y gritaba, diciendo: «Ten misericordia de mí, Señor, Hijo de David; mi hija está gravemente endemoniada».
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, a Canaanite woman from those regions came out and was crying out, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is severely demon-possessed.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, a Canaanite woman from those regions came out and was crying out, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is badly demon-possessed.”

rows.spanish: de modo que la multitud se maravilló al ver a los mudos hablando, a los lisiados sanos, a los cojos caminando y a los ciegos viendo; y glorificaron al Dios de Israel.
rows.current_english_pob: so that the crowd marveled as they saw the mute speaking, the crippled made well, the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.
rows.spanish_base_english: so that the crowd marveled as they saw the mute speaking, the crippled healthy, the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.

rows.spanish: Los que habían comido eran cuatro mil hombres, sin contar mujeres y niños.
rows.current_english_pob: Those who had eaten were four thousand men, besides women and children.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now those who had eaten were four thousand men, besides women and children.

rows.spanish: Y se acercaron los fariseos y saduceos y, poniéndolo a prueba, le pidieron que les mostrara una señal del cielo.
rows.current_english_pob: And the Pharisees and Sadducees came up and, testing him, asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the Pharisees and Sadducees came and, testing him, asked him to show them a sign from heaven.

rows.spanish: Pero Jesús, al saber esto, dijo: «¿Por qué discuten entre ustedes, ustedes de poca fe, que no tienen pan?»
rows.current_english_pob: But Jesus, knowing this, said, “Why are you discussing among yourselves, you of little faith, that you did not bring bread?”
rows.spanish_base_english: But Jesus, knowing this, said, “Why are you discussing among yourselves, you of little faith, that you have no bread?”

rows.spanish: ¿Cómo no entienden que no les hablé a ustedes sobre el pan? Pero cuídense de la levadura de los fariseos y de los saduceos.
rows.current_english_pob: How is it that you do not understand that I was not speaking to you about bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
rows.spanish_base_english: How do you not understand that I did not speak to you about bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, cuando Jesús llegó a la región de Cesarea de Filipo, les preguntaba a sus discípulos, diciendo: «¿Quién dice la gente que es el Hijo del Hombre?»
rows.current_english_pob: When Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, “Who do people say the Son of Man is?”
rows.spanish_base_english: Now when Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi, he was asking his disciples, saying, “Who do people say the Son of Man is?”

rows.spanish: Les dice: «Pero ustedes, ¿quién dicen que soy yo?»
rows.current_english_pob: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?”
rows.spanish_base_english: He says to them, “But who do you say that I am?”

rows.spanish: Y yo también te digo que tú eres Pedro, y sobre esta roca edificaré mi iglesia, y las puertas del Hades no prevalecerán contra ella.
rows.current_english_pob: And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
rows.spanish_base_english: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.

rows.spanish: Pero él, volviéndose, dijo a Pedro: «¡Ve detrás de mí, Satanás! Eres para mí una piedra de tropiezo, porque no piensas en las cosas de Dios, sino en las de los hombres».
rows.current_english_pob: But he turned and said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, because you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on human concerns.”
rows.spanish_base_english: But he turned and said to Peter, “Go behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, because you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men.”

rows.spanish: Porque el Hijo del Hombre está a punto de venir en la gloria de su Padre con sus ángeles, y entonces retribuirá a cada uno conforme a su obra.
rows.current_english_pob: For the Son of Man is about to come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will repay each one according to his conduct.
rows.spanish_base_english: For the Son of Man is about to come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will repay each one according to his deed.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, Moisés y Elías aparecieron ante ellos, conversando con él.
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with him.
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with him.

rows.spanish: Mientras él aún hablaba, he aquí, una nube brillante los cubrió con su sombra, y he aquí, una voz desde la nube dijo: «Este es mi Hijo amado, en quien me he complacido; escúchenlo».
rows.current_english_pob: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice from the cloud said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased; listen to him.”
rows.spanish_base_english: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice from the cloud said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased; listen to him.”

rows.spanish: Él dijo: «Sí». Y cuando entró en la casa, Jesús le habló primero, diciendo: «¿Qué te parece, Simón? ¿De quiénes cobran los reyes de la tierra impuestos o impuesto de capitación: de sus propios hijos o de otros?»
rows.current_english_pob: He said, “Yes.” And when he came into the house, Jesus spoke to him first, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth collect duties or a poll tax—from their own sons or from others?”
rows.spanish_base_english: He said, “Yes.” And when he came into the house, Jesus spoke to him first, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth collect duties or poll tax—from their own sons or from others?”

rows.spanish: Cuando dijo, «De los extraños», Jesús le dijo: «Así que los hijos están libres».
rows.current_english_pob: When he said, “From strangers,” Jesus said to him, “Then the sons are free.”
rows.spanish_base_english: When he said, “From strangers,” Jesus said to him, “Then the sons are free.”

rows.spanish: Y llamando a un niño para que se acercara a él, lo puso en medio de ellos.
rows.current_english_pob: And calling a child to himself, he placed him among them.
rows.spanish_base_english: And calling a child to himself, he set him in their midst.

rows.spanish: ¡Ay del mundo por causa de los tropiezos! Porque es necesario que vengan los tropiezos, pero ¡ay del hombre por quien viene el tropiezo!
rows.current_english_pob: Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks; for it is necessary that the stumbling blocks come, but woe to the man through whom the stumbling block comes.
rows.spanish_base_english: Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks; for it is necessary that the stumbling blocks come, but woe to the man through whom the stumbling block comes.

rows.spanish: Y si tu ojo te hace tropezar, arráncalo y arrójalo lejos de ti. Es mejor para ti entrar en la vida con un solo ojo que, teniendo dos ojos, ser arrojado a la Gehenna de fuego.
rows.current_english_pob: And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye than, having two eyes, to be thrown into fiery Gehenna.
rows.spanish_base_english: And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye than, having two eyes, to be thrown into the Gehenna of fire.

rows.spanish: De la misma manera, no es la voluntad ante su Padre que está en los cielos que perezca uno de estos pequeños.
rows.current_english_pob: In the same way, it is not the will of your Father in heaven that even one of these little ones should perish.
rows.spanish_base_english: In the same way, it is not the will before your Father in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.

rows.spanish: Pero si se niega a escuchar a ellos, díselo a la asamblea. Y si también se niega a escuchar a la asamblea, sea para ti como el gentil y el recaudador de impuestos.
rows.current_english_pob: But if he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly. And if he also refuses to listen to the assembly, let him be to you like a Gentile and a tax collector.
rows.spanish_base_english: But if he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly. And if he also refuses to listen to the assembly, let him be to you like the Gentile and the tax collector.

rows.spanish: Por este motivo, el reino de los cielos puede compararse a un rey que quiso ajustar cuentas con sus siervos.
rows.current_english_pob: For this reason the kingdom of heaven may be compared to a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
rows.spanish_base_english: For this reason the kingdom of heaven has become like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his slaves.

rows.spanish: Entonces el siervo cayó y se postró ante él, diciendo: «Ten paciencia conmigo, y te lo pagaré todo».
rows.current_english_pob: So the servant fell down and prostrated himself before him, saying, ‘Be patient with me, and I will repay you everything.’
rows.spanish_base_english: So the slave fell down before him and kept pleading, saying, ‘Be patient with me, and I will repay you everything.’

rows.spanish: Entonces el amo de aquel esclavo, movido a compasión, lo dejó ir y le perdonó la deuda.
rows.current_english_pob: Then the master of that servant, moved with compassion, released him and forgave him the debt.
rows.spanish_base_english: Then the master of that slave, moved with compassion, released him and forgave him the debt.

rows.spanish: Pero cuando aquel esclavo salió, encontró a uno de sus compañeros esclavos, que le debía cien denarios, y agarrándolo, empezó a estrangularlo, diciendo: «Paga lo que debes».
rows.current_english_pob: But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii, and seizing him, he began choking him, saying, ‘Pay back whatever you owe.’
rows.spanish_base_english: But when that slave went out, he found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii, and seizing him, he began choking him, saying, ‘Pay back what you owe.’

rows.spanish: Entonces su coesclavo cayó y le rogaba, diciendo: «Ten paciencia conmigo, y te lo pagaré».
rows.current_english_pob: So his fellow servant fell down and pleaded with him, saying, ‘Be patient with me, and I will repay you.’
rows.spanish_base_english: So his fellow slave fell down and pleaded with him, saying, ‘Be patient with me, and I will repay you.’

rows.spanish: Por tanto, al ver sus compañeros esclavos lo que había sucedido, se entristecieron mucho, y fueron e informaron a su señor todo lo que había sucedido.
rows.current_english_pob: Therefore, when his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were deeply grieved, and they came and reported to their lord everything that had happened.
rows.spanish_base_english: Therefore, when his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they were deeply grieved, and they came and reported to their lord everything that had happened.

rows.spanish: Entonces su amo lo llamó y le dijo: «¡Esclavo malvado! Te perdoné toda aquella deuda, porque me rogaste».
rows.current_english_pob: Then his master summoned him and said to him, ‘Wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me.’
rows.spanish_base_english: Then his master summoned him and said to him, ‘Wicked slave, I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me.’

rows.spanish: ¿No debías tú también haber tenido misericordia de tu compañero esclavo, así como yo también tuve misericordia de ti?
rows.current_english_pob: Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I also had mercy on you?
rows.spanish_base_english: Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I also had mercy on you?

rows.spanish: Así también mi Padre celestial hará con ustedes, si cada uno no perdona a su hermano de sus corazones.
rows.current_english_pob: So also my heavenly Father will do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from the heart.
rows.spanish_base_english: So also my heavenly Father will do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts.

rows.spanish: Respondió: «¿No han leído que el que los creó desde el principio los hizo varón y hembra?»
rows.current_english_pob: He answered, “Have you not read that the one who created them from the beginning made them male and female?”
rows.spanish_base_english: He answered, “Have you not read that he who created them from the beginning made them male and female?”

rows.spanish: y dijo: «Por esta razón un hombre dejará a su padre y a su madre y se unirá a su esposa, y los dos serán una sola carne».
rows.current_english_pob: and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’?”
rows.spanish_base_english: and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.’

rows.spanish: Sus discípulos le dijeron: «Si tal es el caso de un hombre con su esposa, no conviene casarse».
rows.current_english_pob: His disciples said to him, “If that is the case of a man with his wife, it is not beneficial to marry.”
rows.spanish_base_english: His disciples said to him, “If such is the case of a man with his wife, it is not advisable to marry.”

rows.spanish: Y uno se acercó y le dijo: «Maestro, ¿qué cosa buena debo hacer para tener vida eterna?»
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, a man came up to him and said, “Teacher, what good thing must I do so that I may have eternal life?”
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, one came up to him and said, “Teacher, what good thing must I do that I may have eternal life?”

rows.spanish: Entonces Pedro le respondió: «Mira, nosotros hemos dejado todo y te hemos seguido; ¿qué tendremos, pues?».
rows.current_english_pob: Then Peter answered him, “Look, we have left everything and followed you. What then will we have?”
rows.spanish_base_english: Then Peter answered him, “Behold, we have left everything and followed you. What then will there be for us?”

rows.spanish: Pues el reino de los cielos es semejante a un dueño de casa que salió muy temprano para contratar obreros para su viña.
rows.current_english_pob: For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
rows.spanish_base_english: For the kingdom of heaven is like a master of a house who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.

rows.spanish: Cuando llegaron los contratados alrededor de la undécima hora, cada uno recibió un denario.
rows.current_english_pob: And when those hired about the eleventh hour came, they received a denarius each.
rows.spanish_base_english: And those who came about the eleventh hour received a denarius each.

rows.spanish: Y él le dijo: «¿Qué quieres?». Ella le dijo: «Ordena que estos dos hijos míos se sienten, uno a tu derecha y uno a tu izquierda, en tu reino».
rows.current_english_pob: And he said to her, “What do you want?” She said to him, “Command that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your kingdom.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And he said to her, “What do you want?” She said to him, “Command that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your kingdom.”

rows.spanish: Y el que quiera ser el primero entre ustedes deberá ser su siervo.
rows.current_english_pob: And whoever wants to be first among you must be your servant.
rows.spanish_base_english: And whoever wants to be first among you will be your slave.

rows.spanish: Y he aquí, dos ciegos, sentados junto al camino, al oír que Jesús pasaba, gritaron diciendo: «¡Señor, ten misericordia de nosotros, Hijo de David!»
rows.current_english_pob: And behold, two blind men sitting by the road, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, saying, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And behold, two blind men sitting by the road, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, saying, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.”

rows.spanish: Pero la multitud los reprendió para que se callaran. Sin embargo, ellos clamaron todavía más, diciendo: «¡Señor, ten misericordia de nosotros, Hijo de David!»
rows.current_english_pob: But the crowd rebuked them, telling them to be silent. Yet they cried out all the more, saying, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.”
rows.spanish_base_english: But the crowd rebuked them so that they would be silent. Yet they cried out all the more, saying, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.”

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, esto sucedió para que se cumpliera lo que fue dicho por medio del profeta, diciendo:
rows.current_english_pob: This happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:
rows.spanish_base_english: Now this happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:

rows.spanish: Ahora la mayor parte de la multitud tendió sus mantos sobre el camino, y otros estaban cortando ramas de los árboles y las tendían sobre el camino.
rows.current_english_pob: Most of the crowd spread their garments on the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now most of the crowd spread their garments on the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.

rows.spanish: Y al ver una higuera junto al camino, se acercó a ella y no halló nada en ella, sino solo hojas. Y le dijo: «Que nunca más de ti salga fruto para siempre». Y al instante la higuera se secó.
rows.current_english_pob: And seeing a fig tree by the road, he came up to it and found nothing on it except leaves alone. And he said to it, “May no fruit ever come from you again.” And the fig tree withered at once.
rows.spanish_base_english: And seeing a fig tree by the road, he came up to it and found nothing on it except leaves only. And he said to it, “May fruit never again come from you forever.” And the fig tree withered at once.

rows.spanish: Pero Jesús les respondió: «Yo también les haré una pregunta, y si ustedes me la responden, yo también les diré con qué autoridad hago estas cosas».
rows.current_english_pob: But Jesus answered them, “I also will ask you one question, and if you answer me, I also will tell you by what authority I do these things.”
rows.spanish_base_english: But Jesus answered them, “I also will ask you one question, which if you tell me, I also will tell you by what authority I do these things.”

rows.spanish: Y respondiendo a Jesús, dijeron: «No sabemos». Él también les dijo: «Tampoco yo les diré con qué autoridad hago estas cosas».
rows.current_english_pob: So they answered Jesus, “We do not know.” He also said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And answering Jesus, they said, “We do not know.” He also said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

rows.spanish: Y los arrendatarios tomaron a sus esclavos; a uno golpearon, a otro mataron y a otro apedrearon.
rows.current_english_pob: And the tenant farmers took his servants; one they beat, another they killed, and another they stoned.
rows.spanish_base_english: And the tenant farmers took his slaves; one they beat, another they killed, and another they stoned.

rows.spanish: El reino de los cielos fue comparado con un rey que dio un banquete de bodas para su hijo.
rows.current_english_pob: The kingdom of heaven may be compared to a king who gave a wedding feast for his son.
rows.spanish_base_english: The kingdom of heaven was compared to a king who gave a wedding feast for his son.

rows.spanish: Otra vez envió a otros esclavos, diciendo: «Digan a los invitados: “Miren, he preparado mi banquete; mis bueyes y mis reses cebadas han sido degollados, y todo está listo. Vengan al banquete de bodas”».
rows.current_english_pob: Again he sent other servants, saying, ‘Tell those who have been invited, “Look, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and my fattened cattle have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding feast.”’
rows.spanish_base_english: Again he sent other slaves, saying, ‘Tell those who have been invited, “Look, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and my fattened cattle have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding feast.”’

rows.spanish: Pero los demás, apoderándose de sus esclavos, los maltrataron y los mataron.
rows.current_english_pob: But the rest, seizing his servants, mistreated them and killed them.
rows.spanish_base_english: But the rest, seizing his slaves, mistreated them and killed them.

rows.spanish: Pero el rey se indignó, y enviando sus tropas, destruyó a aquellos asesinos y quemó su ciudad.
rows.current_english_pob: But the king became angry, and he sent his troops, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
rows.spanish_base_english: But the king became angry, and sending his troops, he destroyed those murderers and burned their city.

rows.spanish: Y aquellos esclavos salieron a los caminos y reunieron a todos los que encontraron, tanto malos como buenos; y la sala de bodas quedó llena de comensales reclinados a la mesa.
rows.current_english_pob: And those servants went out into the roads and gathered everyone they found, both evil and good; and the wedding hall was filled with guests reclining at the table.
rows.spanish_base_english: And those slaves went out into the roads and gathered everyone they found, both evil and good; and the wedding hall was filled with guests reclining at the table.

rows.spanish: Pero cuando el rey entró para observar a los invitados reclinados a la mesa, vio allí a un hombre que no estaba vestido con ropa de boda.
rows.current_english_pob: But when the king came in to look at the guests reclining at the table, he saw there a man not wearing a wedding garment.
rows.spanish_base_english: But when the king came in to look at the guests reclining at the table, he saw there a man not dressed in wedding clothes.

rows.spanish: Y le envían sus discípulos junto con los herodianos, diciendo: «Maestro, sabemos que eres verdadero y que enseñas el camino de Dios en verdad, y no te preocupa nadie, porque no miras la apariencia de los hombres».
rows.current_english_pob: And they send to him their disciples along with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and you do not care about anyone, for you do not look at the face of men.”
rows.spanish_base_english: And they send to him their disciples along with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are true and teach the way of God in truth, and you do not care about anyone, for you do not look at the face of men.”

rows.spanish: Ahora bien, había entre nosotros siete hermanos. El primero se casó y murió, y sin tener descendencia, dejó a su esposa a su hermano.
rows.current_english_pob: There were seven brothers among us. The first married and died, and having no offspring, he left his wife to his brother.
rows.spanish_base_english: Now there were seven brothers among us. The first married and died, and having no offspring, he left his wife to his brother.

rows.spanish: Igualmente también el segundo y el tercero, hasta los siete.
rows.current_english_pob: Likewise also the second and the third, until all seven.
